### 0x02214 MDP_CTL_1_TOP

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00001F00
**Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline**

The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP.

Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode<br>DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode1 |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams. This field is a dont care for video mode streams<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |
<!-- page 444 -->

### 0x02218 MDP_CTL_1_FLUSH

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Register Flush register**

The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.

Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.

Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | TIMING_1 | Timing Interface 1 are ready for flush |
| 17 | CTL | Control Pipe register is ready for flush<br>This applies to upper pipe ONLY to change the adding/removal of layers |
| 16 | WB | Write Back registers are ready for flush |
| 15 | DSPP_2 | DSPP2 registers are ready for flush |
| 14 | DSPP_1 | DSPP1 registers are ready for flush |
| 13 | DSPP_0 | DSPP0 registers are ready for flush |
| 12 | DMA_1 | DMA_1 registers are ready for flush |
| 11 | DMA_0 | DMA_0 registers are ready for flush |
| 10 | LAYER_MIXER_4 | Layer Mixer4 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 7 | LAYER_MIXER_1 | Layer Mixer1 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 6 | LAYER_MIXER_0 | Layer Mixer0 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 5 | RGB_2 | RGB2 registers are ready for flush |
<!-- page 445 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | RGB_1 | RGB1 registers are ready for flush |
| 3 | RGB_0 | RGB0 registers are ready for flush |
| 2 | VIG_2 | VIG2 registers are ready for flush |
| 1 | VIG_1 | VIG1 registers are ready for flush |
| 0 | VIG_0 | VIG0 registers are ready for flush |

### 0x0221C MDP_CTL_1_CTL_START

**Type:** W
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Overlay Processor Start Signal for the given Control Operation**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | START | A write to this register will kick off operation for the given operation control and activate all layers |

### 0x02230 MDP_CTL_1_SW_RESET

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Software Reset of the given control operation**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path. This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete. Upon completion, this will return 0x0.<br>Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path. E.g. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well |

### 0x02234 MDP_CTL_1_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**Software Reset Override of the given control operation**
<!-- page 446 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path. This value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath.<br>It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath.<br>To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset.<br>Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0. SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete.<br>The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted |

### 0x02414 MDP_CTL_2_TOP

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00001F00

Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline

The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP.

Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode. DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode1 |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams. This field is a dont care for video mode streams.<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |
<!-- page 453 -->

### 0x02418 MDP_CTL_2_FLUSH

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Register Flush register

The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.

Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.

Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | TIMING_1 | Timing Interface 1 are ready for flush |
| 17 | CTL | Control Pipe register is ready for flush<br>This applies to upper pipe ONLY to change the adding/removal of layers |
| 16 | WB | Write Back registers are ready for flush |
| 15 | DSPP_2 | DSPP2 registers are ready for flush |
| 14 | DSPP_1 | DSPP1 registers are ready for flush |
| 13 | DSPP_0 | DSPP0 registers are ready for flush |
| 12 | DMA_1 | DMA_1 registers are ready for flush |
| 11 | DMA_0 | DMA_0 registers are ready for flush |
| 10 | LAYER_MIXER_4 | Layer Mixer4 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 7 | LAYER_MIXER_1 | Layer Mixer1 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 6 | LAYER_MIXER_0 | Layer Mixer0 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 5 | RGB_2 | RGB2 registers are ready for flush |
<!-- page 454 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | RGB_1 | RGB1 registers are ready for flush |
| 3 | RGB_0 | RGB0 registers are ready for flush |
| 2 | VIG_2 | VIG2 registers are ready for flush |
| 1 | VIG_1 | VIG1 registers are ready for flush |
| 0 | VIG_0 | VIG0 registers are ready for flush |

### 0x0241C MDP_CTL_2_CTL_START

**Type:** W

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Overlay Processor Start Signal for the given Control Operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | START | A write to this register will kick off operation for the given operation control and activate all layers |

### 0x02430 MDP_CTL_2_SW_RESET

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Software Reset of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path. This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete. Upon completion, this will return 0x0.<br>Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path<br>i.e. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well |

### 0x02434 MDP_CTL_2_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Software Reset Override of the given control operation
<!-- page 455 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path. This value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath.<br>It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath.<br>To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset.<br>Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0. SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete.<br>The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted. |

<!-- page 461 -->
### 0x02614 MDP_CTL_3_TOP

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00001F00

**Description:**
Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline

The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP.

Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode.<br>DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core.<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams. This field is a don't care for video mode streams.<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |
<!-- page 462 -->
### 0x02618 MDP_CTL_3_FLUSH

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

**Description:**
Register Flush register

The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.

Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.

Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | TIMING_1 | Timing Interface 1 are ready for flush |
| 17 | CTL | Control Pipe register is ready for flush<br>This applies to upper pipe ONLY to change the adding/removal of layers |
| 16 | WB | Write Back registers are ready for flush |
| 15 | DSPP_2 | DSPP2 registers are ready for flush |
| 14 | DSPP_1 | DSPP1 registers are ready for flush |
| 13 | DSPP_0 | DSPP0 registers are ready for flush |
| 12 | DMA_1 | DMA_1 registers are ready for flush |
| 11 | DMA_0 | DMA_0 registers are ready for flush |
| 10 | LAYER_MIXER_4 | Layer Mixer4 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 7 | LAYER_MIXER_1 | Layer Mixer1 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 6 | LAYER_MIXER_0 | Layer Mixer0 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 5 | RGB_2 | RGB2 registers are ready for flush |
<!-- page 463 -->

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

### 0x0261C MDP_CTL_3_CTL_START

**Type:** W

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

**Description:**
Overlay Processor Start Signal for the given Control Operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | START | A write to this register will kick off operation for the given operation control and activate all layers |

### 0x02630 MDP_CTL_3_SW_RESET

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

**Description:**
Software Reset of the given control operation

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path. This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete. Upon completion, this will return 0x0.<br>Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path.<br>i.e. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well |

### 0x02634 MDP_CTL_3_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

**Description:**
Software Reset Override of the given control operation
<!-- page 464 -->
#### MDP_CTL_3_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path. This value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath.<br>It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath.<br>To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset.<br>Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0. SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete.<br>The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted. |

### 0x02814 MDP_CTL_4_TOP

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00001F00

**Description:**
Operation Mode Configuration for the Pipeline

The purpose of the register is to define the complete data path of this operation and that includes all the way to the interfaces such as DSI/HDMI/eDP.

Changing of the data path dynamically is NOT supported and requires stopping that data path, reconfiguring the connections, and restarting the datapath.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | MODE_SEL | Interface Mode of the destination interface<br>Needed to distinguish interfaces such as DSI that can be either mode.<br>DSI can also interleave streams of different types (i.e. command and video) to a single core.<br>0x0: Video Mode<br>0x1: Command Mode |
| 16:15 | STREAM_SEL | Stream Identification<br>Used For Interleaving of Command Streams. This field is a don't care for video mode streams.<br>0x0: Stream 0<br>0x1: Stream 1<br>0x2: Stream 2 |
| 7:4 | OUT_SEL | Output Ping-Pong Interface Connection to external display interface<br>0x0: No connection from Ping-Pong buffers to output interfaces<br>0x1: Interface 0<br>0x2: Interface 1<br>0x3: Interface 2<br>0x4: Interface 3 |
| 3:0 | MEM_SEL | Memory Output Connection<br>0x0: NO memory output selected<br>0x1: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x2: Memory BLOCK mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x3: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 0<br>0x4: Memory LINE mode output selected for rotation 1<br>0x5: Memory LINE mode output selected for linear memory writeback |


<!-- page 471 -->

### 0x02818 MDP_CTL_4_FLUSH

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Register Flush register**

The flush register is used to indicate a pipe/layermixers registers are all programmed, and are safe to update to the back copy of the double buffered registers.

Each pipes/layermixers flush mask bit will be used only when the associated pipe/layermixer is running at active refresh pull mode, e.g., direct out going to LCDC/HDMI/DSI Video.

In such operation mode, the associated pipe/layermixers double buffered registers back copies are updated with the new values at the vsync boundary only when the flush mask bit has already been written a 1.

Each flush mask bit would also returned a 0 once the back copies are updated.

Before the back copies are updated, the associate mask bit would returned a 1 if it has been previously written a 1.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 30 | TIMING_1 | Timing Interface 1 are ready for flush |
| 17 | CTL | Control Pipe register is ready for flush<br>This applies to upper pipe ONLY to change the adding/removal of layers |
| 16 | WB | Write Back registers are ready for flush |
| 15 | DSPP_2 | DSPP2 registers are ready for flush |
| 14 | DSPP_1 | DSPP1 registers are ready for flush |
| 13 | DSPP_0 | DSPP0 registers are ready for flush |
| 12 | DMA_1 | DMA_1 registers are ready for flush |
| 11 | DMA_0 | DMA_0 registers are ready for flush |
| 10 | LAYER_MIXER_4 | Layer Mixer4 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 9 | LAYER_MIXER_3 | Layer Mixer3 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 8 | LAYER_MIXER_2 | Layer Mixer2 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 7 | LAYER_MIXER_1 | Layer Mixer1 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 6 | LAYER_MIXER_0 | Layer Mixer0 registers are ready for flush<br>This includes the cursor registers stored in the layer mixer register space |
| 5 | RGB_2 | RGB2 registers are ready for flush |
<!-- page 472 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | RGB_1 | RGB1 registers are ready for flush |
| 3 | RGB_0 | RGB0 registers are ready for flush |
| 2 | VIG_2 | VIG2 registers are ready for flush |

### 0x02830 MDP_CTL_4_SW_RESET

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Software Reset of the given control operation**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will trigger a soft reset for the described data path This register is self-clearing and will return 0x1 if soft reset sequence is not complete<br>Upon completion, this will return 0x0<br>Note that this will soft reset the peripheral display interfaces that are described in this path<br>i.e. if driving intf_0 it will reset the pixel clock domain of intf_0 as well |
<!-- page 473 -->

### 0x02834 MDP_CTL_4_SW_RESET_OVERRIDE

**Type:** RW  
**Reset State:** 0x00000000  
**Software Reset Override of the given control operation**

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | RESET | Writing to this bit will assert reset for the described data path This value contained in this register will be forced onto the datapath<br>It will reset the state machines within the scheduler as well for the given datapath<br>To use this register sequence, SW shall write a value of 0x1 to this register to assert reset<br>Once SW wants to de-assert reset, SW shall write a value of 0x0 SW will need to ensure the duration of the value 0x1 is long enough to ensure the path is clean and all memory reads are complete<br>The datapath will not be triggered if this bit is asserted |

### 0x052F0 MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_PA_LUTV

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`
* **Properties**: PA LUTV data, Auto-incremented by hardware or by software. 256 entries are available for reading. double buffered: NO. Hardware maintains 2 copies.
<!-- page 487 -->
#### 0x052F0 MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_PA_LUTV (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Software issue an write to the LUT<br>0: VALUE will be written to RAM at INDEX if INDEX_UPDATE=1 or at INDEX+1 if INDEX_UPDATE=0<br>1: VALUE will not be written to RAM, this setting is appropriate for example when INDEX needs to be updated for read |
| 16 | INDEX_UPDATE | Software issue an index update<br>0: No index update by software<br>1: Update LUT index to value specified by INDEX |
| 15:8 | INDEX | VALUE is stored in this INDEX of the HIST_LUTn, next write will be stored to the next higher INDEX |
| 7:0 | VALUE | Value read depends on the LUT select and which one is available for reading by software.<br>The read sequence should always begin with WR INDEX_UPDATE=1, INDEX=\<rptr start location\> subsequent RD will start from the start location and every read will auto-increment the rptr |

### 0x05050 MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000040

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY.
The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool.
The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.
* So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP)
* A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries)

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` or `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2`.

An example programming would set the following:
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0` : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2` : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
<!-- page 504 -->

* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

**double buffered:** YES

#### MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 Bits:

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |

### 0x05054 MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1

* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

### 0x05070 MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_SRC_ADDR_SW_STATUS

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**double buffered:** YES

Security Status of the source buffer plane.
This is programmed by SW to indicate if the buffer is NON-SECURE or SECURE.
This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | SRC3_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 3 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 2 | SRC2_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 2 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 0 | SRC0_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 0 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x050B4 MDP_VP_0_VIG_0_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000
**double buffered:** YES

Decimation Configuration.
Note that there is no decimation on DMA pipe which means no decimation in line mode on DMA or block mode.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HORZ_S | Horizontal Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4.<br>S refers to the number of pixels skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 pixel skip S pixels. The algorithm is applied to ALL components. Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behavior. The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 pixel drop 1 pixel. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally<br>0x3: Read 1 pixel drop 3 pixels. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally<br>0x7: Read 1 pixel drop 7 pixels. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally<br>0xF: Read 1 pixel drop 15 pixels. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |
| 3:0 | VERT_S | Vertical Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4.<br>S refers to the number of lines skipped.<br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 line skip S lines. The algorithm is applied to ALL components. Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behavior. The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 line drop 1 line. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally *(Note: source manual says horizontally)*<br>0x3: Read 1 line drop 3 lines. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally *(Note: source manual says horizontally)*<br>0x7: Read 1 line drop 7 lines. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally *(Note: source manual says horizontally)*<br>0xF: Read 1 line drop 15 lines. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally *(Note: source manual says horizontally)* |
<!-- page 509 -->

### 0x15050 MDP_VP_0_RGB_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000040
- **Double Buffered**: YES

**Description**: FIFO watermark to aid in generation of `mdpREQPRIORITY`.

The watermark here refers to the number of 128-bit entries available in the Shared Memory Pool (SMP).
The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.
- A value of `0` indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP).
- A value of `100` indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit).

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` or `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2`.

#### Example Programming:
- `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0` : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
- `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
- `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2` : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

#### Priority Generation:
- `mdpREQPRIORITY` = `11` (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP, meaning it is relatively empty and needs filling).
- `mdpREQPRIORITY` = `10` when above `FIFO_0` and `FIFO_1` but below `FIFO_2`.
- `mdpREQPRIORITY` = `01` when above `FIFO_0` but below `FIFO_1` and `FIFO_2`.
- `mdpREQPRIORITY` = `00` (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP, meaning it is relatively full).

| Bits | Name | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |
<!-- page 526 -->
### 0x15054 MDP_VP_0_RGB_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1

- **Type**: RW

The watermark here refers to the number of 128-bit entries available in the Shared Memory Pool (SMP).

- A value of `0` indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP).

This is the middle FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2` or lower than `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0`.

### 0x15070 MDP_VP_0_RGB_0_SSPP_SRC_ADDR_SW_STATUS

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
- **Double Buffered**: YES

**Description**: Security Status of the source buffer plane.

This is programmed by SW to indicate if the buffer is NON-SECURE or SECURE. This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction.

> [!NOTE]
> SW should program `SRC0_ADDR_CP`, `SRC1_ADDR_CP`, `SRC2_ADDR_CP`, and `SRC3_ADDR_CP` to the same value.
> Memory transactions will not complete if this status does not correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.

| Bits | Name | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 3 | SRC3_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 3 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane, then this value is ignored.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 2 | SRC2_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 2 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane, then this value is ignored.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane, then this value is ignored.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 0 | SRC0_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 0 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane, then this value is ignored.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x150B4 MDP_VP_0_RGB_0_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
- **Double Buffered**: YES

**Description**: Decimation Configuration.

> [!NOTE]
> There is no decimation on the DMA pipe, which means no decimation in line mode on DMA or block mode.

| Bits | Name | Description |
|:---|:---|:---|
| 11:8 | HORZ_S | Horizontal Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4.<br>S refers to the number of pixels skipped.<br>Algorithm: read 1 pixel, skip S pixels. Applied to ALL components.<br>Only the following values are supported (others result in undefined behavior). Used in conjunction with QSEED2.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 pixel, drop 1 pixel (decimate by 2 horizontally)<br>0x3: Read 1 pixel, drop 3 pixels (decimate by 4 horizontally)<br>0x7: Read 1 pixel, drop 7 pixels (decimate by 8 horizontally)<br>0xF: Read 1 pixel, drop 15 pixels (decimate by 16 horizontally) |
| 3:0 | VERT_S | Vertical Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4.<br>S refers to the number of lines skipped.<br>Algorithm: read 1 line, skip S lines. Applied to ALL components.<br>Only the following values are supported (others result in undefined behavior). Used in conjunction with QSEED2.<br>0x0: No decimation is performed<br>0x1: Read 1 line, drop 1 line (decimate by 2 vertically)<br>0x3: Read 1 line, drop 3 lines (decimate by 4 vertically)<br>0x7: Read 1 line, drop 7 lines (decimate by 8 vertically)<br>0xF: Read 1 line, drop 15 lines (decimate by 16 vertically)<br>*(Note: Datasheet incorrectly states "horizontally" for VERT_S values)* |


<!-- page 531 -->

* **Type:** RW

* **Source Format Configuration for each virtual pipeline:** YES
* **when:** On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

| 25:23 | SRC_CHROMA_SAMP | Source Chroma Sampling:<br>0x0: RGB/YUV 4:4:4<br>0x1: 4:2:2 - H2V1<br>0x2: 4:2:2 - H1V2<br>0x3: 4:2:0 - N2V1<br>0x4: 4:2:0 - N1V2 |

### 0x17030 MDP_VP_0_RGB_1_SSPP_SRC_FORMAT (Continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 20:19 | FETCH_PLANES | Determines the number of planes to fetch:<br>0x0: Interleaved<br>0x1: Planar<br>0x2: Pseudo-planar |
| 18 | UNPACK_ALIGN | Unpacking alignment:<br>0x0: TO LSB<br>0x1: TO MSB |
| 17 | UNPACK_TIGHT | Unpacking tightness:<br>0x0: Loose<br>0x1: Tight |
| 13:12 | UNPACK_COUNT | Valid unpacking pattern count:<br>0x0 = 1 component<br>0x1 = 2 components<br>...<br>0x3 = 4 components<br>Unpacking applies to interleaved plane (chroma plane in pseudo-planar) |
| 11 | ROT90 | Source image is to be rotated 90 degrees |
| 10:9 | SRC_BPP | Effective source byte per pixel:<br>0x0: 1 byte<br>0x1: 2 bytes<br>0x2: 3 bytes<br>0x3: 4 bytes<br>This is used ONLY when unpacking the interleaved plane |
| 8 | SRCC3_EN | Alpha Enable:<br>0x0: Source has NO alpha<br>0x1: Source has alpha |
| 7:6 | SRCC3 | Number of bits for component 3 (Alpha):<br>0x0: 1 bits<br>0x1: 4 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 5:4 | SRCC2 | Number of bits for component 2 (R/Cr):<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 3:2 | SRCC1 | Number of bits for component 1 (B/Cb):<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |
| 1:0 | SRCC0 | Number of bits for component 0 (G/Luma):<br>0x0: 4 bits<br>0x1: 5 bits<br>0x2: 6 bits<br>0x3: 8 bits |

### 0x17048 MDP_VP_0_RGB_1_SSPP_FETCH_CONFIG

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000087
* **Description:** SSPP Client Fetch Configuration per Virtual Pipeline. This register must NOT be altered during operation and MDP must be idle when changing values.
* **Double Buffered:** NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 22 | PRI_ARB_DIS | Primary arbitration disable |
| 21 | PMARK_DIS | Priority marker disable |
| 17:16 | TILE_SIZE | Tile Size for processing of BLOCK formats.<br>Note that this only applies to blocks that operate in block mode which is limited to DMA source pipe. This setting has no effect for all other source pipes (ViG/RGB).<br>0x0: 128x128<br>Others: ILLEGAL / Not Supported |
| 12 | ADDR_SYNC_MODE | Boundary on which fetch address synchronizes.<br>Setting this field to line forces the address updates on the next line which performs the software requested feature of updating on hsync.<br>Note that updating on line boundaries will likely result in tearing on the panel since hardware is fetching from new memory buffer.<br>0x0: frame (default)<br>0x1: line |

### 0x17050 MDP_VP_0_RGB_1_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000040
* **Description:** FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY. The watermark here refers to the number of 128-bit entries available in the Shared Memory Pool (SMP).
* **Double Buffered:** YES

The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.
* A value of 0 indicates completely FULL (no more entries available in the SMP).
* A value of 100 indicates 100 entries available in the SMP.

This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` or `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2`.

#### Example Programming:
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0` : 50 (meaning 50 entries free in SMP - least room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` : 100 (meaning 100 entries free in SMP - middle ground room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2` : 150 (meaning 150 entries free in SMP - most room available)

#### Priority Generation (`mdpREQPRIORITY`):
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e., lots of space available in SMP, need to fetch).
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 10 when above `FIFO_0` and `FIFO_1` but below `FIFO_2`.
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 01 when above `FIFO_0` but below `FIFO_1` and `FIFO_2`.
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e., SMP is nearly full).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |
<!-- page 548 -->

### 0x17070 MDP_VP_0_RGB_1_SSPP_SRC_ADDR_SW_STATUS

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000
* **Description:** Security Status of the source buffer plane. This is programmed by SW to indicate if the buffer is NON-SECURE or SECURE. This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction.
* **Double Buffered:** YES

SW should program `SRC0_ADDR_CP`, `SRC1_ADDR_CP`, `SRC2_ADDR_CP`, and `SRC3_ADDR_CP` to the same value.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | SRC3_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 3 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored. Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 2 | SRC2_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 2 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored. Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored. Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 0 | SRC0_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 0 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored. Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x170B4 MDP_VP_0_RGB_1_SSPP_DECIMATION_CONFIG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

Decimation Configuration

Note that there is no decimation on DMA pipe which means no decimation in line mode on DMA or block mode.

double buffered: YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:8 | HORZ_S | Horizontal Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4. <br>S refers to the number of pixels skipped. <br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 pixel skip S pixels. The algorithm is applied to ALL components. Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behavior. The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios. <br>0x0: No decimation is performed <br>0x1: Read 1 pixel drop 1 pixel. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally <br>0x3: Read 1 pixel drop 3 pixels. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally <br>0x7: Read 1 pixel drop 7 pixels. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally <br>0xF: Read 1 pixel drop 15 pixels. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |
| 3:0 | VERT_S | Vertical Configuration for decimation; required to support downscaling greater than 1/4. <br>S refers to the number of lines skipped. <br>The algorithm is always the following: read 1 line skip S lines. The algorithm is applied to ALL components. Decimation only supports the following values. All other values will result in undefined behavior. The decimation block will provide coarse scaling and should be used in conjunction with qseed2 to support all scaling ratios. <br>0x0: No decimation is performed <br>0x1: Read 1 line drop 1 line. Used to decimate by 2 horizontally <br>0x3: Read 1 line drop 3 lines. Used to decimate by 4 horizontally <br>0x7: Read 1 line drop 7 lines. Used to decimate by 8 horizontally <br>0xF: Read 1 line drop 15 lines. Used to decimate by 16 horizontally |

### Register: MDP_VP_0_DMA_0_SSPP_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0
* **Address offset:** 0x25050
* **Type:** Read/Write
* **Clock:** undefined
* **Reset State:** 0x00000040
* **Double buffered:** YES

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of mdpREQPRIORITY.

The watermark here refers to the # of 128-entries available in the Shared Memory Pool. The value programmed here should be aware of the amount programmed in the Shared Memory Pool.

So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the SMP).

A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit). This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 or REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2.

An example programming would set the following:
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 : 50 (meaning 50 entries free to be written into SMP - least room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1 : 100 (meaning 100 entries free to be written into SMP - middle ground room available)
* REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2 : 150 (meaning 150 entries free to be written into SMP - most room available)

mdpREQPRIORITY generation:
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in SMP)
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* mdpREQPRIORITY = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in SMP so its good)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:16 | RESERVED_BITS31_16 | Reserved |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |
<!-- page 573 -->

### Register: MDP_VP_0_DMA_0_SSPP_SRC_ADDR_SW_STATUS
* **Address offset:** 0x25070
* **Type:** Read/Write
* **Clock:** undefined
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000
* **Double buffered:** YES

Security Status of the source buffer plane.

This is programmed by SW to indicate if the buffer is NON-SECURE or SECURE. This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 3 | SRC3_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 3 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>- 0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>- 0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 2 | SRC2_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 2 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>- 0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>- 0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 1 | SRC1_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 1 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>- 0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>- 0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |
| 0 | SRC0_ADDR_CP | Secure status bit for source plane 0 (if used).<br>If the format doesn't fetch from that plane then this value is ignored.<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>SW should program SRC0_ADDR_CP, SRC1_ADDR_CP, SRC2_ADDR_CP, SRC3_ADDR_CP to the same value.<br>- 0x0: Non Content Protected Buffer State<br>- 0x1: Content Protected Buffer State |

## 4.1.1.4.14 MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0 register definitions

### LAYER
Layer Mixer hardware register description

### 0x45000 MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_OP_MODE

**Type:** RW
**Reset State:** 0x00000000

LayerMixer Operation Control
double buffered: YES
when: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BLEND3_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage3 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 3 | BLEND2_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage2 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 2 | BLEND1_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage1 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 1 | BLEND0_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage0 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 0 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |

### 0x45004 MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_OUT_SIZE

**Type:** RW

double buffered: YES
when: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)

### Register: MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG (0x45204)

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000087

Cursor Client Fetch Configuration per Virtual Pipeline.
* **Double buffered**: NO
* **Note**: This register must NOT be altered during operation and MDP must be idle when changing values.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17:16 | TILE_SIZE | Tile Size for processing of BLOCK formats. Note that this only applies to blocks that operate in block mode which is limited to DMA source pipe. This setting has no effect for all other source pipes (ViG/RGB).<br>0x0: 128x128<br>0x1: 64x64<br>0x2: 32x32 |
| 12 | ADDR_SYNC_MODE | Boundary on which fetch address synchronizes. Setting this field to line forces the address updates on the next line which performs the software requested feature of updating on hsync. Note that updating on line boundaries will likely result in tearing on the panel since hardware is fetching from new memory buffer.<br>0x0: frame (default)<br>0x1: line |
<!-- page 613 -->
*Continuation of Register: MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG (0x45204)*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:8 | MAL | Describes the Minimum Access Length for the source pipeline. This value should align with the DRAM's expected transaction alignment unit. This setting forces the source fetch pipe to be aligned to DRAM and implement re-alignment for maximum efficiency.<br>0x0: 128b alignment (default)<br>0x1: 256b alignment<br>0x2: 512b alignment |
| 7:4 | MAX_BURST_SIZE | Maximum burst beat size. Hardware fetch engines operate on 128-bit bus. Possible values:<br>0x8: burst of 8<br>0x4: burst of 4<br>0x2: burst of 2 |
| 3:0 | REQ_DEPTH_LIMIT | Pending request limit, default max value of 0x7 means maximum pending requests allowed in the design. Anything less limits the bus requests to that number + 1. |

### Register: MDP_VP_0_LAYER_0_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0 (0x45220)

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000008

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of `mdpREQPRIORITY`.
The watermark here refers to the dedicated cursor fetch memory.
The value programmed here should be aware of the amount of dedicated cursor fetch memory.
So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the dedicated memory).
A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries).
This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` or `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2`.

An example programming would set the following:
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0` : 0x08 (meaning 0x08 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - least room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` : 0x10 (meaning 0x10 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - middle ground room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2` : 0x20 (meaning 0x20 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - most room available)

* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory)
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 10 above FIFO_0 and FIFO_1 but below FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 01 above FIFO_0 but below FIFO_1 and FIFO_2
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory so its good)

* **Double buffered**: YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |
<!-- page 615 -->

## 4.1.1.4.15 MDP_VP_0_LAYER_3 register definitions

**LAYER**
Layer Mixer hardware register description

### Register: MDP_VP_0_LAYER_3_OP_MODE (0x48000)

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000

LayerMixer Operation Control.
* **Double buffered**: YES
* **when**: On frame boundaries (vsync or SW trigger)
<!-- page 618 -->
*Continuation of Register: MDP_VP_0_LAYER_3_OP_MODE (0x48000)*

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | BLEND3_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage3 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 3 | BLEND2_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage2 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 2 | BLEND1_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage1 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 1 | BLEND0_COLOR3_OUT | Selects which source to drive on color3 component output for stage0 blend.<br>0x0: BG Layer Color3<br>0x1: FG Layer Color3 |
| 0 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |

### 0x48204 MDP_VP_0_LAYER_3_CURSOR_FETCH_CONFIG

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000087

Cursor Client Fetch Configuration per Virtual Pipeline.

* **Double buffered:** NO

This register must NOT be altered during operation and MDP must be idle when changing values.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17:16 | TILE_SIZE | Tile Size for processing of BLOCK formats.<br>Note that this only applies to blocks that operate in block mode which is limited to DMA source pipe. This setting has no effect for all other source pipes (ViG/RGB).<br>0x0: 128x128<br>0x1: 64x64<br>0x2: 32x32 |
| 12 | ADDR_SYNC_MODE | Boundary on which fetch address synchronizes.<br>Setting this field to line forces the address updates on the next line which performs the software requested feature of updating on hsync.<br>Note that updating on line boundaries will likely result in tearing on the panel since hardware is fetching from new memory buffer.<br>0x0: frame (default)<br>0x1: line |

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9:8 | MAL | Describes the Minimum Access Length for the source pipeline. This value should align with the DRAM's expected transaction alignment unit.<br>This setting forces the source fetch pipe to be aligned to DRAM and implement re-alignment for maximum efficiency.<br>0x0: 128b alignment (default)<br>0x1: 256b alignment<br>0x2: 512b alignment |
| 7:4 | MAX_BURST_SIZE | Maximum burst beat size.<br>Hardware fetch engines operate on 128-bit bus. Possible values:<br>0x8: burst of 8<br>0x4: burst of 4<br>0x2: burst of 2 |
| 3:0 | REQ_DEPTH_LIMIT | Pending request limit, default max value of 0x7 means maximum pending requests allowed in the design.<br>Anything less limits the bus requests to that number + 1. |

### 0x48220 MDP_VP_0_LAYER_3_CURSOR_REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000008

FIFO watermark to aid in generation of `mdpREQPRIORITY`.
The watermark here refers to the dedicated cursor fetch memory.
The value programmed here should be aware of the amount of dedicated cursor fetch memory.
So a value of 0 indicates completely FULL (i.e. there are no more entries available in the dedicated memory).
A value of 100 indicates 100 entries in the Shared Memory Pool (each entry being 128-bit entries).
This is the lowestmost FIFO depth and should not be programmed higher than `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` or `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2`.

An example programming would set the following:
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_0` : 0x08 (meaning 0x08 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - least room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_1` : 0x10 (meaning 0x10 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - middle ground room available)
* `REQPRIORITY_FIFO_WATERMARK_2` : 0x20 (meaning 0x20 entries free to be written into dedicated cursor fetch memory - most room available)

* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 11 (highest priority request) when above all 3 watermark levels (i.e. lots of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory)
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 10 above `FIFO_0` and `FIFO_1` but below `FIFO_2`
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 01 above `FIFO_0` but below `FIFO_1` and `FIFO_2`
* `mdpREQPRIORITY` = 00 (lowest priority request) when below all 3 watermark levels (i.e. not a lot of space available in dedicated cursor fetch memory so its good)

* **Double buffered:** YES

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:0 | WATERMARK | Watermark Level for FIFO_0 |
<!-- page 646 -->

| 29 | SIX_ZONE_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable six zone adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable six zone adj on HUE |

| 27 | PA_VAL_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on VALUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on VALUE |
| 26 | PA_SAT_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on SATURATION<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on SATURATION |
| 25 | PA_HUE_MASK | 0x0: Disable HSIC adj on HUE<br>0x1: Enable HSIC adj on HUE |
| 22 | GC_LUT_EN | 0x0: Disabled - mapped linearly from 12-bit to 8-bit<br>0x1: Enabled |

| 19 | PA_LUTV_EN | Histogram Enhancement Lookup Table enable |

### 0x55230 MDP_VP_0_DSPP_0_PA_LUTV

* **Type:** RW
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

PA LUTV data
Auto-incremented by hardware
256 entries are available for reading double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | VALUE_UPDATEN | Software issue an write to the LUT<br>0: VALUE will be written to RAM at INDEX if INDEX_UPDATE=1 or at INDEX+1 if INDEX_UPDATE=0<br>1: VALUE will not be written to RAM, this setting is appropriate for example when INDEX needs to be updated for read |
| 16 | INDEX_UPDATE | Software issue an index update<br>0: No index update by software<br>1: Update LUT index to value specified by INDEX |
<!-- page 659 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15:8 | INDEX | VALUE is stored in this INDEX of the PA_LUTV, next write will be stored to the next higher INDEX |
| 7:0 | VALUE | Value read depends on the LUT select and which one is available for reading by software<br>The read sequence to the LUT should always begin with WR INDEX_UPDATE=1, INDEX=\<rptr start location\><br>subsequent RD will start from the start location and every read will auto-increment the rptr |

### 0x652B0 MDP_WB_0_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Security Status of the destination buffer plane

This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF This value is logically or ed with the source content protection produced by hardware

This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction

Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used) Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

---

### 0x65AB0 MDP_WB_1_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

- **Type**: RW
- **Reset State**: 0x00000000
- **Security Status of the destination buffer plane**: This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF. This value is logically ORed with the source content protection produced by hardware. This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction. Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used). Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x662B0 MDP_WB_2_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

Type: RW

Reset State: 0x00000000

Security Status of the destination buffer plane

This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF This value is logically or ed with the source content protection produced by hardware

This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction

Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful double buffered: NO

MDP_WB_2_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used) Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

### Register: MDP_WB_3_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS (0x66AB0)

- **Type:** RW
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000
- **Notes:**
  - Security Status of the destination buffer plane
  - This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF. This value is logically ORed with the source content protection produced by hardware.


<!-- page 731 -->
This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction.

Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful.
**double buffered:** NO

### MDP_WB_3_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used). Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |

### 0x672B0 MDP_WB_4_DST_ADDR_SW_STATUS

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Security Status of the destination buffer plane**:
  This provides a SW override to the hardware calculated content protection sent to VBIF. This value is logically ORed with the source content protection produced by hardware.
  This information will be presented to VBIF per transaction and reflected as part of the memory transaction.
  Note that the VBIF context banks need to be properly programmed for the output to be successful.
* **double buffered**: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 0 | DST_ADDR_CP | This is the secure status bit for destination plane 0 (if used)<br>Memory transactions will not complete if this status doesn't correspond to system programming in the rest of the path to memory.<br>0x0: Content Protected Buffer State<br>0x1: Non Content Protected Buffer State |
<!-- page 747 -->

## 4.1.1.4.22 MDP_INTF_1 register definitions

**INTF**
Display Interface hardware register description

### 0x6B800 MDP_INTF_1_TIMING_ENGINE_EN

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Display Interface Timing Engine Enable register double buffered**: YES (when: On frame boundaries)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | OSYNC_LOCK | |
| 0 | EN | Display Interface enable<br>Should be the LAST register programmed for the interface. Be sure to program ALL timing registers and setting up of the display pipeline BEFORE enabling this register.<br>Upon disabling of this bit, hardware will stop driving the interface at the NEXT vsync boundary.<br>A VSYNC interrupt WILL be generated but a VSYNC will NOT be generated on the interface. |

### 0x6B804 MDP_INTF_1_INTF_CONFIG

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00040000
* **Display Interface Configuration register**:
  Note that the configuration register ONLY applies to INTF_4 which transmits to MHL.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | PROG_FETCH_START_EN | Programmable Fetch feature enable bit<br>0: programmable line counter disabled - default value to be backward compatible<br>1: programmable line counter enabled |
| 30 | ACTIVE_V_EN | Active V Enable |
| 29 | ACTIVE_H_EN | Active H Enable |
<!-- page 748 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 28 | VSYNC_INTERRUPT_MODE | vsync interrupt generation mode<br>0 = generate an interrupt every vsync<br>1 = generate an interrupt every 2 fields (applicable to interlace mode) |
| 27:24 | REPEAT_PIXEL_MODE | Pixel repeat mode<br>0x1 = repeat each pixel 2 times 0x2 = repeat each pixel 3 times<br>...<br>15 = repeat pixel 16 times |
| 23 | DSI_VIDEO_STOP_MODE | This bit controls how video mode stream is stopped when DSI dynamic refresh is triggered. It is not applicable for non-DSI interface.<br>0x0: disable timing engine when DSI sets the video stop signal;<br>0x1: halt timing engine counters when DSI sets the video stop signal |
| 21 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_H_MTHD | Horizontal Chroma Down Sample method 0x0: non-pixel dropping<br>0x1: pixel dropping |
| 20 | CHROMA_DWN_SAMPLE_EN | Chroma Down Sample enable for YUV444 0x0: Disabled<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 18 | CSC_DST_DATA_FORMAT | Destination Data Format 0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 17 | CSC_SRC_DATA_FORMAT | Source Data Format 0x0: RGB<br>0x1: YCbCr |
| 16 | CSC_EN | Enables the color matrix conversion 0x0: Bypass<br>0x1: Enabled |
| 13:11 | NIBBLE_SWAP_EN | Enable nibble swapping within each pixel byte.<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[0]: 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [7:0]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[3:0] with pixel_data[7:4]<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[1] = 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [15:8]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[11:8] with pixel_data[15:12]<br>NIBBLE_SWAP_EN[2] = 0 = no swapping for pixel_data [23:16]; 1 = enable swapping of pixel_data[19:16] with pixel_data[23:20] |
| 10 | PACK_ALIGN | 0x0: LSB<br>0x1: MSB |
| 9:8 | PACK_422 | 0x0: Y2Cr1Y1Cb1<br>0x1: Cr1Y2Cb1Y1<br>0x2: Y2Cb1Y1Cr1<br>0x3: Cb1Y2Cr1Y1 |
| 6:4 | OUT_MODE | 0x0: YCbCr or RGB4444 separate syncs 24-bit interface<br>0x1: RSVD<br>0x2: YCbCr 422 separate syncs 16-bit interface |
| 2 | INTERLACE_INIT_SEL | 0x0: start with even field<br>0x1: start with odd field |
| 1 | REPEAT_PIXEL | 0x0: Do NOT repeat<br>0x1: Repeat |
| 0 | INTERLACE_MODE | double buffered: YES<br>0x0: Progressive Out<br>0x1: Interlace out |
<!-- page 749 -->

This is the start between start of HSYNC pulse and the start of the next HSYNC pulse.<br>Note: hsync_period = width + h_porch where width = output image width, h_porch = (h_back_porch + h_front_porch), h_back_porch starts at the beginning of hsync pulse. |

### 0x6B81C MDP_INTF_1_DISPLAY_V_START_F0

* **Type**: RW
* **Reset State**: 0x00000000
* **Display Interface Vertical Active Start Control for field 0 double buffered**: YES


<!-- page 751 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DISPLAY_START_Y | **Display Y Start**<br>Defines the time period between the field0 start of vsync pulse and the first displayed line position in pixel clocks<br>display_start_y = v_back_porch * hcycle<br>where hcycle = horizontal_back_porch + horizontal_active + horizontal_front_porch<br>For eDP control the value programmed into this register differs slightly and should be programmed to the first active pixel and not the first pixel on that line!<br>In particular, the programming for eDP should be: display_start_y = (v_back_porch * hcycle) + horizontal_back_porch |

**Type:** RW

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

Display Interface Vertical Active Start Control for field 1 double buffered: NO

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DISPLAY_START_Y | **Display Y Start**<br>Defines the time period between the field1 start of vsync pulse and the first displayed line position in pixel clocks<br>display_start_y = v_back_porch * hcycle<br>where hcycle = horizontal_back_porch + horizontal_active + horizontal_front_porch<br>For eDP control the value programmed into this register differs slightly and should be programmed to the first active pixel and not the first pixel on that line!<br>In particular, the programming for eDP should be: display_start_y = (v_back_porch * hcycle) + horizontal_back_porch |

| 27:24 | INPUT_SEL | RW | **Input Selection**<br>This field allows the selected input to propagate to the MISR in the event that multiple inputs want to share the same physical MISR. For example, the video interface might want to MISR on active pixel data only or active + timing information as well. This field would select which input is sent to the MISR |
| 10 | STATUS_CLEAR | W | **Status Clear**<br>This is a write only register that doesn't have any effect prior to MDP5 1.5.0 since there was no logic associated with it.<br>Write 0x1: Clears the MISR_STATUS register<br>Write 0x0: Has no effect on the MISR_STATUS register |
| 9 | STATUS | R | **Status**<br>Read only register. Set to 0x1 when misr signature has been updated |
| 8 | ENABLE | RW | **MISR Enable**<br>MISR enable which starts/ends calculation of MISR on the next vsync/trigger event. This essentially double buffers the enable so that the misr doesn't start/end immediately but rather at a defined time. The MISR calculation would run until the end of programmed number of frames |
| 7:0 | FRAME_COUNT | RW | **Frame Count**<br>Number of frames to run before capturing |

## 4.1.2 MIPI Display Serial Interface (DSI) and Physical Layer (DSI PHY)

This section describes the MIPI® Display Serial Interface (DSI) and companion Physical Layer (DSI PHY).

### 4.1.2.1 DSI overview

The display serial interface (DSI) is a mobile industry processor interface (MIPI®). The DSI defines a serial bus and communication protocol between the host (source of the image data) and the device (destination of the image data). The bus includes one high-speed clock lane and one or more datalanes of serialized data. Each lane is carried on two wires and uses low-voltage differential signaling.

The single DSI controller (DSI0), integrated in the SoC mobile display subsystem (MDSS), is a hardware implementation of the MIPI DSI link application, protocol, and lane-management layers. The DSI controller receives pixel streams from the mobile display processor (MDP) and panel commands from memory, then transfers the data to a companion MIPI PHY (DSI0_PHY), which serializes the data and sends it to DSI panel over the serial bus.

Figure 4-96 shows a high-level overview of the DSI controller with companion DSI PHY.

#### Figure 4-96: DSI overview
*Description:* This block diagram illustrates the MDSS (Mobile Display Subsystem) and its interface with external components and subsystems.
- **MDSS (Mobile Display Subsystem):** Contains three main blocks:
  - **MIPI DSI controller:** The central block of the diagram. It receives:
    - Clocks and Reset inputs from the **GCC** (Global Clock Controller).
    - VBIF interface connection (bidirectional), Video interface (input), and Command interface (input) from the **MDP**.
    - It sends an Interrupt to the **APSS** (Application Processor Subsystem).
    - It connects to the **DSI PHY** via a Configuration line (output) and a PPI interface (bidirectional).
  - **MDP (Mobile Display Processor):** Positioned below the DSI controller. It connects to the DSI controller as described, and connects bidirectionally to the **VBIF** block below it.
  - **VBIF (Video Bus Interface):** Positioned at the bottom of the MDSS block. It connects bidirectionally to the **System NoC** (Network on Chip) bus.
- **System NoC:** A system bus at the bottom of the diagram, connecting bidirectionally to the MDSS VBIF block.
- **GCC (Global Clock Controller):** Located to the left of the MDSS block, supplying clocks and resets to the MIPI DSI controller.
- **APSS (Application Processor Subsystem):** Located to the left of the MDSS block, receiving interrupts from the MIPI DSI controller.
- **DSI PHY:** Located to the right of the MDSS block. It contains an internal **PLL** (Phase Locked Loop). It interfaces with the MIPI DSI controller and outputs to external pins:
  - **Clock lane** (one-way output)
  - **Data lane 0** (bidirectional)
  - **Data lane 1** (bidirectional)
  - **Data lane 2** (bidirectional)
  - **Data lane 3** (bidirectional)
<!-- page 768 -->

The DSI controller and companion DSI PHY provide the following main features:
- Compliance with MIPI Alliance Specification v1.01 for Display Serial Interface
- Compliance with MIPI D-PHY Specification v0.65, v0.81, v0.90
- Compliance with MIPI DCS Specification v01-02-00
- Video mode support with progressive timing generation
- Command mode support
- Interleaving of video and command mode streams
- Interleaving of multiple command mode streams
- One clock lane and up to four data lanes
- Maximum output resolution up to 1200 x 800 @ 60 fps
- Up to 1.5 Gbps per lane with 24 bpp support

#### 4.1.2.4.2 DSI lane enable

Each lane can be enabled by a writing 1 to a dedicated bit in `DSI_0_CTRL` register, as follows:
* Logical data lane 0 enable: `DLN0_EN` bit
* Logical data lane 1 enable: `DLN1_EN` bit
* Logical data lane 2 enable: `DLN2_EN` bit
* Logical data lane 3 enable: `DLN3_EN` bit
* Clock lane enable: `CLKLN_EN` bit

#### 4.1.2.4.3 DSI lane force TX stop

Each lane can be forced to transit to LP-11 (stop state) by writing 1 to a dedicated bit in `DSI_0_LANE_CTRL` register, as follows:
* Logical Data lane 0 force stop: `DLN0_FORCE_TX_STOP` bit
* Logical Data lane 1 force stop: `DLN1_FORCE_TX_STOP` bit
* Logical Data lane 2 force stop: `DLN2_FORCE_TX_STOP` bit
* Logical Data lane 3 force stop: `DLN3_FORCE_TX_STOP` bit
* Clock lane force stop: `CLKLN_FORCE_TX_STOP` bit

#### 4.1.2.4.4 DSI continuous clock

A clock can be sent continuously to the display panel through the clock lane by setting the `CLKLN_HS_FORCE_REQUEST` bit in `DSI_0_LANE_CTRL` register.

*Description:* A block diagram showing the internal connectivity of the DSI within the system. The main blocks are APSS, DSI PHY (containing a PLL), GCC, MDSS, and System NoC.
- **MDSS (Multimedia Display Subsystem)** contains:
  - **MDP**: Generates `MDP_IRQ`.
  - **MIPI DSI controller**: Generates `DSI0_IRQ`.
  - A logic gate (AND-like symbol) that combines `MDP_IRQ` and `DSI0_IRQ` to output `MDSS_IRQ` to the **APSS**.
  - **VBIF**: Connects bidirectionally to the **System NoC**.
- **MIPI DSI controller** connects to **DSI PHY**:
  - Outgoing `Configuration` signal.
  - Bidirectional `PPI interface`.
- **DSI PHY PLL** outputs two clocks to **GCC**: `DSIPLL0_OUT_0` and `DSIPLL0_OUT_1`.
- **GCC (Global Clock Controller)** outputs several clock and reset signals to **MDSS**:
  - `GCC_MDSS_BYTE0_CLK`
  - `GCC_MDSS_ESC0_CLK`
  - `GCC_MDSS_PCLK0_CLK`
  - `GCC_MDSS_MDP_CLK`
  - `GCC_MDSS_AHB_CLK`
