| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | INPUT_SERVICE_MASK | 0x0 = Not masked<br>0x1 = The flag in 0x0000 0018 QUP_OPERATIONAL does not cause an interrupt but provides status only. |
| 8 | OUTPUT_SERVICE_MASK | 0x0 = Not masked<br>0x1 = The flag in 0x0000 0018 QUP_OPERATIONAL does not cause an interrupt but provides status only. |

### 6.1.5.3.10 QUP_MX_OUTPUT_COUNT (0x0000 0100)

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: CC_QUP_CORE_CLK
- **Reset state**: 0x00000000

Unless otherwise stated, the register bits written return the value when read. This register only applies to Block_Mode. The counter decrements for each output transfer when the STATE field (see 0x0000 0004 QUP_STATE register) is moved from the RESET_STATE to the RUN_STATE. The PAUSE_STATE does not affect the count.

> [!NOTE]
> 1. Allows the total number of mini-core transfers to be less than an exact multiple of OUTPUT_BLOCK_SIZE. Any additional outputs are discarded.

#### QUP_MX_OUTPUT_COUNT Bits
| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | MX_CONFIG_DURING_RUN | W | Write only value.<br>0x0 (W) = The MX_OUTPUT_COUNT value only applies in reset_state (legacy behavior).<br>0x1 (W) = The MX_OUTPUT_COUNT value also applies in run_state and allows writing the transaction data in a few portions when not knowing the transaction size in advance. Reconfiguration during run is only allowed after the last portion has ended (that is, MAX_OUTPUT_DONE_FLAG was asserted). |
| 15:0 | MX_OUTPUT_COUNT | RW | 0x0 = The output count function is not enabled for use.<br>Other = Number of writes of size N to the mini-core per RUN_STATE. See note 1. |

### 6.1.5.3.14 QUP_MX_WRITE_COUNT (0x0000 0150)

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: CC_QUP_CORE_CLK
- **Reset state**: 0x00000000
<!-- page 1747 -->

The 0x0000 0100 QUP_MX_OUTPUT_COUNT register applies to Block_Mode and Bam_Mode, and this register applies to FIFO_mode. If this register is nonzero, then the qup_irq is asserted after shifting in the number of shifts specified by this register.

Unlike the 0x0000 0100 QUP_MX_OUTPUT_COUNT register case, the software should not program the 0x0000 0150 QUP_MX_WRITE_COUNT value to be more than the actual depth of the FIFO (BLOCK_SIZE_OUTPUT * FIFO_SIZE_OUTPUT).

| Bits | Name | Type | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

Reconfiguration during run is only allowed after the last portion has ended (that is, MAX_OUTPUT_DONE_FLAG was asserted). |
| 15:0 | MX_WRITE_COUNT | RW | The number of writes of size N. This is used only if the core is in FIFO_Mode. |

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: CC_QUP_CORE_CLK
- **Reset state**: 0x00000000

Unless otherwise stated, the register bits written return the value when read. This register only applies to Block_Mode and Bam_Mode (for nonbalanced SPI). The counter decrements for each input transfer when the STATE bit in the 0x0000 0004 QUP_STATE register is moved from the RESET_STATE to the RUN_STATE. The PAUSE_STATE does not affect the count.

> 1. Allows the number of shift register transfers to be less than an exact multiple of INPUT_BLOCK_SIZE. When count is reached, the remaining INPUT_BLOCK_SIZE is filled with zeroes.

Reconfiguration during run is only allowed after the last portion has ended (that is, MAX_INPUT_DONE_FLAG was asserted). |

### 6.1.5.3.18 QUP_MX_READ_COUNT (0x0000 0208)

- **Type**: RW
- **Clock**: CC_QUP_CORE_CLK
- **Reset state**: 0x00000000

The 0x0000 0200 QUP_MX_INPUT_COUNT register applies to Block_Mode and Bam_Mode, and the QUP_MX_READ_COUNT register applies to FIFO_mode. If this register is nonzero, then the qup_input_service_irq is asserted after shifting in the number of shifts specified by this register.

Unlike the 0x0000 0200 QUP_MX_INPUT_COUNT register case, the software should not program the QUP_MX_READ_COUNT value to be more than the actual depth of the FIFO (BLOCK_SIZE_INPUT * FIFO_SIZE_INPUT). If the SPI mini-core and slave operation is enabled, it results in an InputOverRun error.

Reconfiguration during run is only allowed after the last portion has ended (that is, MAX_INPUT_DONE_FLAG is asserted). |

Unless otherwise stated, register bits written return the value when read.

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 11 | FORCE_CS | 0x0 = The chip select is not asserted<br>0x1 = The chip select is asserted unconditionally with no relationship to 0x0000 0004 QUP_STATE or transaction state. |
| 10 | CLK_IDLE_HIGH | 0x0 = CC_QUP_SPI_CLK is low when SPI is idle (SPI_CS is not asserted).<br>0x1 = CC_QUP_SPI_CLK is high when SPI is idle (SPI_CS is not asserted). |

The number of transfers is determined by SPI_MX_OUTPUT_COUNT and/or SPI_MX_INPUT_COUNT registers. Applies only in MASTER mode. |
| 7:4 | CS_N_POLARITY | These four bits control the polarity of four SPI_CS#_N respectively.<br>0x0 = SPI_CS#_N active LOW.<br>Other = Setting any of this bit to 1 makes the associated SPI_CS#_N active HIGH.<br>This field is a 'don't care' in SLAVE operation. |

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** CC_QUP_CORE_CLK

### 6.1.5.3.24 0x0000 0308 QUP_SPI_ERROR_FLAGS (Continued)

* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

All bits in this register are set by hardware and remain set until cleared by software. Writing a one to a bit clears it while writing a zero leaves the bit unchanged.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | TRANSFER_CANCEL_DONE | 0x0 (R) = No error<br>0x0 (W) = Leaves this bit unchanged<br>0x1 (R) = The SPI controller has completed canceling the transfer that was scheduled for cancellation (LOCAL_ID = TRANSFER_CANCEL_ID).<br>0x1 (W) = Clears the error flag |
| 2 | TRANSFER_CANCEL_ID_MATCH | 0x0 (R) = No error<br>0x0 (W) = Leaves this bit unchanged<br>0x1 = The SPI controller is ready for cancel operation: it has found the transfer that was scheduled for cancellation (LOCAL_ID = TRANSFER_CANCEL_ID) and the logic is done with previous activity.<br>0x1 (W) = Clears the error flag |
| 1 | SPI_SLV_CLK_OVER_RUN_ERR | 0x0 (R) = No error<br>0x0 (W) = Leaves this bit unchanged<br>0x1 (R) = Number of CC_QUP_SPI_CLK ticks which occurred while SPI_CS#_N was asserted was greater than the programmed value of N. When this happens, only the first N bits are passed to the SPI input FIFO and the output shift value is held at zero.<br>0x1 (W) = Clears the error flag |
| 0 | SPI_SLV_CLK_UNDER_RUN_ERR | 0x0 (R) = No error<br>0x0 (W) = Leaves this bit unchanged<br>0x1 (R) = Number of CC_QUP_SPI_CLK ticks which occurred while SPI_CS#_N was asserted was less than the programmed value of N. When this occurs, the bits that were received are passed to the SPI input FIFO and the CURRENT output bit is forced to zero.<br>0x1 (W) = Clears the error flag |

If set, each bit enables generation of SPI_ERROR_IRQ and the setting of the corresponding error flag in the 0x0000 0308 QUP_SPI_ERROR_FLAGS register for the specified error case. At reset, all error enable bits are set to 1.

For SLAVE operation, this field is not applicable.<br>0x0 = SPI_CS#_N remains deasserted for exactly one clock tick.<br>0x1 = two clock ticks<br>…<br>0x3F = indicates 64 clock ticks. |

* **Type:** RW

* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

| 0 | CLEAR | This command should be given only when the I2C mini-core is idle. When in doubt the software can use SW_RESET to reset the mini-core.<br>0x0 (R) = Clear is complete, the hardware sets the CLEAR bit to zero.<br>0x1 (R) = When set, an I2C bus clear is executed per the I2C standard. A bus clear consists of nine I2C clock ticks with data wire left not-driven. This has the effect of clearing any slave which has lost read sync.<br>The bit cannot be cleared by software. After a bus clear, both clock and data lines should be high. If not, an external slave has hung the bus by holding down one or both lines. Reset the slave to clear if possible. Any slave reset mechanism is beyond the scope of the I2C mini-core. |

## 6.2 Universal Asynchronous Receiver/Transmitter (UART)

This section describes the universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter (UART) module.

### 6.2.1 UART overview

The UART controller is used for transmitting and receiving data through a serial UART/SIM/IrDA interface. It is used for communication with other UART protocol-compliant devices.

Figure 6-35 shows a high level overview of UART instances integrated within the bus access manager (BAM) low speed peripheral (BLSP) block in the SoC.

#### Figure 6-35: UART overview
*Description:* This diagram illustrates the high-level architecture and integration of the UART instances (UART0 and UART1) within the BLSP (BAM Low-Speed Peripheral) block of the SoC.
The components and connections shown are:
- **BLSP (BAM Low-Speed Peripheral):** The main block containing the following sub-components:
  - **QUP (Qualcomm Universal Peripheral):** Contains UART0 and UART1.
  - **eDML**
  - **BAM (Bus Access Manager)**
- **External Connections from BLSP/QUP:**
  - **UART0 Pins:**
    - `CTS_N`
    - `RFR_N`
    - `UART_RX/UIM_CLK` (shares connection with UIM block)
    - `UART_TX/UIM_DATA` (shares connection with UIM block)
  - **UART1 Pins:**
    - `UART_RX/UIM_CLK`
    - `UART_TX/UIM_DATA`
    - `CTS_N`
    - `RFR_N`
- **System Blocks (outside BLSP):**
  - **GCC (Global Clock Controller):** Provides Clocks and Resets to the QUP/UART blocks.
  - **APSS (Applications Processor Subsystem):** Receives Interrupts from QUP/UART blocks.
  - **TCSR (Top Control and Status Registers):** Connects to the system.
  - **Peripheral and system configuration NoC:** Connects to BAM and the rest of the system.

The following main features are supported in UART:
* Up to 4 Mbps UART interface
* Baud rates from 75 bps to 115200 bps and 4 Mbps
* Single-character mode
* 5-8 bits character size, 0.5 bits to 2 bits stop bit, no/even/odd/space parity
* Optional hardware flow control based on CTS/RFR (hardware or software based)
<!-- page 1763 -->

* Rx break, hunt char, sticky error status, overflow detection, FIFO watermarking, FIFO resizing, hardware data timeout, hardware inactivity timeout
* BAM/eDML internal interface
* Integration with internal UIM controller

Table 6-55 lists some of the UART use cases.

#### Table 6-55: UART use cases

| Use case | Example scenario |
| :--- | :--- |
| Bluetooth communication | Communication with an external Bluetooth device. |
| Image download and factory test | Loading an image onto the device. Used when minimum system functionality is available and no interrupts are used, or when factory test-mode is required. |
| Diagnostics | Used for the Qualcomm diagnostic messaging system. It replaces the USB for this use during initial chip bring-up, when the USB is not available or in older builds for QPST/QXDM connection. |
| SIM/UIM card communication | Communicating with the device SIM/UIM card |
| IrDA communication | Communicating with external IrDA devices |
| Data | Driving an asynchronous communication port for data applications. USB has generally replaced UART for this application. |
| Debug | Can be used to drive an external asynchronous communication port as a debug port. |
| JTAG | JTAG communication (mentioned in GPIO allocations), though rarely used. |

### 6.2.1.1 UART acronyms and terms

Table 6-56 lists the common acronyms and terms used throughout this section.

#### Table 6-56: UART acronyms and terms

| Acronym or term | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| AHB | Advanced high performance bus; AMBA high-speed bus |
| BAM | Bus access module |
| BAM mode | A UART working mode for both Rx and Tx data channels independently. In this mode, BAM/eDML is the AHB master transferring data to/from UART. |
| BASI | BAM-aware slave interface, between eDML and UART. Allows communication for data transfer coordination on the AHB bus. |
| BCR | Backward compatibility register. Each bit in this register enables a feature/fix, that changes the behavior of the UART controller in a manner that is not backward compatible. |
| Channel command | Executed by writing a value to the channel command field of the `UART_DM_CR` register. |
| CR command | Executed by writing 1 to the matching bit of the `UART_DM_CR` register. |
<!-- page 1764 -->

#### Table 6-56: UART acronyms and terms (Continued)

| Acronym or term | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| CRCI | Client rate control interface |
| CSR | Control/status registers |
| CTS | Clear to send–incoming flow control signal |
| CURRX | Formerly known as `valid_char_cnt`. Amount of characters received in UART that are linked to the current RX-transfer. |
| Data channel | Also referred to as channel. The internal data path of either Rx data or Tx data inside UART. |
| DM | Data mover |
| DMRX | A target value of an Rx transfer maximal length (in characters). Value is set in the `UART_DM_DMRX` register. |
| DMRX event | Occurs when `CURRX` value of an active RX transfer equals the `DMRX` value. This event triggers the sealing of the RX transfer and its inactivation. |
| DMRX low event | Occurs upon a write to the `UART_DM_DMRX` register with a value lower than the current `CURRX` value. This event triggers the sealing of the Rx transfer that had just been activated and its inactivation. |
| General command | Executed by writing a value to the general command field of the `UART_DM_CR` register. |
| GPIO | General purpose input/output |
| GSBI | General serial bus interface |
| IrDA | Infrared data association |
| RAM | Random access memory |
| RFR | ReadyForReceive, outgoing flow control signal |
| Rx transfer | A term for the time frame and data frame of the transferring of an amount of data from the UART interface to the Rx client (SW/DM/BAM). |
| RXLEV | This is the name of the watermark interrupt, asserted when amount of data words in the Rx FIFO exceeds the value in `UART_DM_RFWR` register. It is also referred to as the value in `UART_DM_RFWR` register. |
| SC | Single character–packing/unpacking of one character per word |
| SIM | Subscriber identity module |
| Single character mode | A UART packing/unpacking mode for both Rx and Tx channels independently. Words read/written from/to UART FIFO hold a single character instead of four in the normal mode. |
| SoC | System on chip |
| Stale | A feature of the Rx channel. The stale mechanism is used to flush the contents of the packing buffer into the Rx FIFO, so that the characters kept in the packing buffer can be externally read. |
| SW-stale | A CR register command that triggers the stale mechanism. |
| Timeout stale (TO stale) | A counter mechanism to trigger the stale mechanism. Count expires when a character has not been received for a predetermined number of cycles. Target value is set in the `UART_DM_IPR` register. |
| TLMM | Top level mode mux |
<!-- page 1765 -->

#### Table 6-56: UART acronyms and terms (Continued)

| Acronym or term | Definition |
| :--- | :--- |
| TXLEV | This is the name of the watermark interrupt, asserted when amount of vacant words in the Tx FIFO exceeds the value in `UART_DM_TFWR` register. It is also referred to as the value in `UART_DM_TFWR` register. |
| UART | Universal asynchronous receiver/transmitter |
| UART_DM | Universal asynchronous receiver transmitter with data mover interface |
| UIM | User identity module |
| Word | Any reference to a word is to a 32-bit word, width of the AHB-bus |
| WWT timer | Work-waiting-timeout feature is used to alert software (through an IRQ) that a character has not been received for a predetermined number of cycles. Target value is set in the `UART_DM_WWT_TIMEOUT` register. WWT differs from stale timeout mechanism by immediately alerting software and by not triggering the stale mechanism. This feature is mainly used for UIM/SIM card communication. |

Figure 6-37 shows the UART protocol data format (character frame transmission). For more information on the configuration of protocol parameters (baud rate, stop-bit length, parity bit, number of bits per character), see Section 6.2.4.8.

#### Figure 6-37: UART protocol data format
*Description:* This diagram illustrates the structure of a single UART frame transmitted over the serial data line.
- **Serial Data Line:** The line is normally high (logic 1) when idle.
- **Start Bit:** The transmission begins with a transition from logic 1 to logic 0, representing the Start bit.
- **Word Data:** The data bits are transmitted sequentially (D1 through D8). The incoming data is sampled at the center of each bit pulse.
- **Parity Bit (Optional):** Follows the data bits if parity is enabled.
- **Stop Bit:** The frame concludes with a Stop bit, returning the line to logic 1.

### 6.2.4 UART functional description

Figure 6-39 shows a high-level functional overview of UART within BLSP.

#### Figure 6-39: UART functional block diagram
*Description:* This diagram details the functional blocks and interfaces of the UART modules within the BLSP.
- **System Level Connections:**
  - **Peripheral and system configuration NoC** connects to the BLSP block.
  - **APSS** connects to the BLSP block.
- **BLSP Internal Components:**
  - **Secure BAM-lite:** Bus Access Manager (Lite version) used for DMA.
  - **eDML:** Enhanced Data Mover Lite.
  - **Configuration AHB bus:** Connects the configuration register interfaces.
  - **UART0 & UART1:** The core UART blocks. Each is connected to the Secure BAM-lite via a **BASI** (BAM-aware slave interface) for coordinated data transfers.
  - **UIM:** User Identity Module interface logic.
- **Output:** The UART signals route to the **TLMM** (Top Level Mode Mux) for I/O pins.

The UART controller functions as a slave on an AHB bus. This bus is used to configure UART by software/BAM or to read/write data from/to UART by software/BAM.

UART can also communicate with a BAM module through a BASI interface. This feature is used to read/write data from/to UART without (or minimal) software intervention between data transactions.

When data flows between the SoC peripheral NOC and the UART controller, data is stored in small internal RAMs in the UART controller and can be read by BAM or directly by the software.
* In a BAM use case, the BAM hardware maintains the data flow, assisted by the BAM and the BASI interface between UART and BAM.
* In a non-BAM use case, periodic interrupts from UART controller and the software maintains the data flow.


<!-- page 1771 -->
UART0 and UART1 controllers are integrated with a single UIM controller. Configuration and control of the UIM controller is done through the UART AHB bus. For more details on UIM operation, see Section 6.2.4.11.1.

### 6.2.4.1 UART architecture
Figure 6-40 shows a simplified overview of UART internal blocks.

#### Figure: Figure 6-40 UART internal architecture
*Description:* A block diagram representing the UART internal architecture, divided into two clock domains: the AHB domain (left side) and the UART domain (right side).
- **AHB Domain components:**
  - **Register block**: Connected to the AHB bus.
  - **BASI**: Implements the BASI protocol (eDML interaction) and connects to the TX/RX FIFOs.
  - **TX FIFO** and **RX FIFO**: Implemented in a single RAM instance, connected to the Register block and BASI interface.
  - **irq ctrl**: Handles UART interrupts configuration, producing `irq`.
- **Boundary / Synchronization Interface:**
  - **Packing buffer** and **RX async FIFO**: RX data flows from the UART receiver in the UART domain, through the RX async FIFO and Packing buffer, into the RX FIFO in the AHB domain.
  - **Unpacking buffer** and **TX async FIFO**: TX data flows from the TX FIFO in the AHB domain, through the Unpacking buffer and TX async FIFO, to the UART transmitter in the UART domain.
  - **UIM synchronization block**: Synchronizes UIM-related signals across the clock domains.
- **UART Domain components:**
  - **UART receiver**: Samples communication on the RX line and moves it to the RX async FIFO.
  - **UART transmitter**: Converts characters from the TX async FIFO for the serial interface (TX).
  - **UIM / IrDA / SIM / IFC**: External interfaces connected to the UART controller.

The UART controller is built from the following main sub blocks:
- **Tx/Rx FIFOs**: The UART Tx and Rx FIFOs are implemented in a single RAM instance in the AHB clock domain, whose depth is defined by the RAM_ADDR_WIDTH generic (default is 128 words), which can be read in the UART_DM_GENERICS [GENERIC_RAM_ADDR_WIDTH] register field. Separation between the two FIFOs is defined in the UART_DM_BADR register.
- **Tx/Rx async FIFOs**: Each data channel (Tx + Rx) uses an 8-byte deep asynchronous FIFO (the Rx channel is actually a 10-bit wide FIFO used to hold parity/framing information as well). These FIFOs are used to synchronize data between the two clock domains. The Rx async FIFO is also used for the buffering of incoming data in case of sensitive events occurring in the Rx packing buffer, when incoming characters are rejected until the event has finished.
- **Interrupts control**: Handles UART interrupts configuration.
- **Register block**: Holds the UART registers and logic of the AHB bus used to read and write from/to the registers.
- **BASI interface**: Implements eDML interaction (BASI protocol).
- **Transmitter**: Receives a single character from the Tx async FIFO and converts it for a serial interface.
- **Receiver**: Samples communication on the Rx line of the serial interface and converts it into characters, and moves them to the Rx async FIFO.
<!-- page 1772 -->
- **Packing/unpacking buffers**: This is a serial-to-parallel/parallel-to-serial buffer that converts words into characters (or vice versa), used between the FIFOs (words) and the async FIFOs (characters).
- **IrDA interface**: This is used to convert serial protocol between receiver/transmitter and the serial interface to support IrDA communication.
- **SIM interface**: This is used to convert the serial protocol between receiver/transmitter and the serial interface to support SIM/UIM communication.

### 6.2.4.2 UART power and clock management

#### 6.2.4.2.1 UART clock management

##### AHB clock
The CC_HCLK_RAW clock is used by all blocks in the AHB domain. In general, these are all blocks that are not directly linked with transmitting/receiving data on the serial interfaces.

The frequency for this clock can be changed dynamically, as long as the minimum/maximum constraints are met:
- **Minimal clock rate**: 4.8 MHz (that is, XO/4)
- **Maximal clock rate**: 120 MHz

It can be turned off when no AHB transfer is currently in process with UART.

For frequencies and off times, an estimated minimal ratio of 30 AHB clock cycles for every 900 UART clock cycles must be maintained to prevent overrun.

##### UART clock
The CC_UART_DM_CLK_RAW clock is used by all blocks in the UART domain. In general, these are all blocks that link with transmitting/receiving data on the serial interfaces (receiver, transmitter, sim glue, IrDA-ifc, bit-generator, and so on).

The frequency for this clock can be changed dynamically, though the baud rate of the serial interface is impacted. To maintain the same baud rate, UART_DM_CSR register must be configured accordingly. The following minimum/maximum constraints also must be met:
- **Minimal clock rate**: Not limited; must be at least 16 times the maximal baud rate intended to be used.
- **Maximal clock rate**: 64 MHz (4 Mbps)

This clock must never be turned off to avoid losing incoming characters.

For clock frequencies and off times, an estimated minimal ratio of 30 AHB clock cycles for every 900 UART clock cycles must be maintained to prevent overrun.
<!-- page 1773 -->
##### UIM (source) clock
The CC_UART_DM_SIM_SRC_CLK_RAW is the clock being driven to the UIM card in case it is configured in the UART_DM_SIM_CFG register via bits SIM_CLK_ON and SIM_SEL.

Allowed clock rates from the UIM interface are usually 3 MHz to 4 MHz. A typical clock rate used is 3.84 MHz.

The UART also provides the option to divide the clock frequency by 2, by taking a 6 MHz to 8 MHz input clock and sending out a 3 MHz to 4 MHz clock to the card. The clock division can be configured in the UART_DM_SIM_CFG [SIM_CLK_TD8_SEL] register bit.

##### Clock gating
The UART provides clock gating for both the AHB clock and the UART clock to switch off clocks to modules that are not currently in use. Gating is enabled by default after a hardware reset. To disable gating, write '1' to the matching field in UART_DM_CLK_CTRL register.

The UART_DM_CLK_CTRL [AHB_CLK_CGC_CLOSE] register bit must be used in case the UART instance is not used and AHB clock cannot be switched off externally (for example in case the AHB clock is shared between different controllers, like within the BLSP).

#### 6.2.4.2.2 UART power management

##### Block level power features
UART has two features to disable logic for power savings:
- **Transmitter disabling**: This shuts down the transmitter logic after the current character is done transmitting. It is issued by a UART_TX_DISABLE command in the UART_DM_CR register and can be enabled again by issuing the UART_TX_EN command.
- **Receiver disabling**: This shuts down the receiver logic immediately and all incoming characters are lost. It is issued by a UART_RX_DISABLE command in the UART_DM_CR register and can be enabled again by issuing the UART_RX_EN command.

##### Switching off UIM pads power
In some cases, it can be useful to switch off the power rails of UIM cards. UIM power rails have the following signals: UIM_DATA and UIM_CLK. The UIM_DATA signal is bidirectional and must be disabled before collapsing its pad. The disable is done by enabling the input enable function of the pad.

The sequence of UIM pads power collapse has the following steps:
1. Initiate deactivation command to the relevant UIM card by configuring UART_DM_UIM_CMD [INITIATE_HW_DEACTIVATION] register bit.
2. Change the TLMM_IE_CTRL_DISABLE [IE_CTRL_DISABLE] register bit to 0 (this moves the control on the pads to TLMM module).
3. Collapse the UIM pads power by switching off the relevant power rail.
<!-- page 1774 -->
### 6.2.4.3 UART reset options
After a hardware reset (the controller has one async reset signal), the UART is not capable of any data transfer. Data channels are disabled by default, characters cannot be received through the Rx channel nor can be transmitted through the Tx channel. Furthermore, most registers hold all zero values, and should be reconfigured.

After a hardware reset, the UIM controller blocks the pass through of the UIM signals from UART to the card.

The UART and UIM should be initialized after every reset as described in Section 6.2.4.8.

The UART also features software reset commands via the UART_DM_CR register that reset data channels only and not registers and configuration.

#### 6.2.4.3.1 UART Rx channel reset
This reset is issued by executing a reset receiver channel command in the UART_DM_CR register.

This command resets the entire data channel. As a result, all characters in Rx FIFOs and buffers are lost, all blocks go back to the reset state, and Tx transfer is deactivated. Reset does not change the configuration in registers, that is, the Rx channel configuration remains the same as before.

#### 6.2.4.3.2 UART Tx channel reset
This reset is issued by executing a reset transmitter channel command in the UART_DM_CR register.

This command resets the entire data channel. As a result, all characters in Tx FIFOs and buffers are lost, all blocks go back to the reset state, and the Rx transfer is deactivated. Reset does not change the configuration in registers, that is, the Tx channel configuration remains the same as before.

#### 6.2.4.3.3 UART internal reset
This reset is issued by executing a uart_reset_int command in the UART_DM_CR register. It resets both data channels as explained above.

### 6.2.4.4 UART interrupts

#### 6.2.4.4.1 UART interrupts
A single interrupt line, UART_DM_INTR, is driven by UART towards the SoC interrupt controller. This signal is an OR function of an internal interrupts vector, calculated by AND-ing the UART_DM_ISR register (interrupt status) with the UART_DM_IMR register (interrupt masking).

`UART_DM_INTR <= OR (UART_DM_ISR vector AND UART_DM_IMR vector)`

Upon receiving an interrupt, the UART_DM_ISR and UART_DM_IMR registers must be read to conclude the events that caused the assertion and react accordingly.
<!-- page 1775 -->
If more than one interrupt bit is high and not masked, clearing a single interrupt bit does not cause the interrupt line to be deasserted. For deassertion, all high bits must be cleared or masked.

To deassert the interrupt line, a command in the UART_DM_CR register to clear the ISR bit must be issued for most bits. Some specific bits require a different procedure to be cleared.

Table 6-62 lists the summary of the UART interrupts.

#### Table 6-62 UART interrupts summary

| Interrupt | Type | Cause | Behavior | Software reaction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TX channel** | | | | |
| TXLEV | Status | Space in Tx FIFO exceeds the watermark defined by UART_DM_TFWR [TFWR] register field | Deasserted after writes to Tx FIFO when condition no longer valid | AHB master should write TxLEV-words to Tx FIFO |
| DELTA_CTS | Status | CTS_N input has changed state | Deasserted after clearing (reset CTS_N channel command) | Clear interrupt |
| TX_READY | Status | Tx FIFO finished handling previous Tx transfer | Deasserted after clearing (reset Tx READ general command). | Clear interrupt. Initiate new Tx transfer. |
| TX_ERROR | Error | Parity error in UIM/SIM transmission. | See Section 6.2.4.12 | |
| TX_DONE | Status | UIM/SIM transfer had finished transmitting | Deasserted after clearing (clear Tx-DONE channel command). | Clear interrupt. Retransmission should be considered. |
| TX_WRITE_ERROR | Error | A write to a full Tx FIFO attempted. | See Section 6.2.4.12 | |
| TX_COMP | Status | Tx transfer had finished transmitting. | Deasserted after clearing (clear Tx-WRITE_ERROR IRQ channel command). | Clear interrupt |
| **Rx channel** | | | | |
| RXHUNT | Status | A character matching the one programmed in UART_DM_HCR register had arrived. | Deasserted after clearing (clear reset error status channel command). | Clear interrupt |
| RXBREAK_CHANGE | Error | Break condition has changed state | See Section 6.2.4.12 | |
| RXSTALE | Status | Rx transfer had finished | Deasserted after clearing (reset stale interrupt channel command). | Clear interrupt. Read the UART_DM_RX_TOTAL_SNAP register. Continue according to control procedure of work mode. Initialize next Rx transfer. |
<!-- page 1776 -->
#### Table 6-62 UART interrupts summary (cont.)

| Interrupt | Type | Cause | Behavior | Software reaction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Rx channel (cont.)** | | | | |
| RXLEV | Status | Data in Rx FIFO exceeds the watermark defined by UART_DM_TFWR [RFWR] register field. | Deasserted after reads from Rx FIFO when condition no longer valid. | AHB master should read RxLEV words from Rx FIFO. |
| RXBREAK_START | Error | Break condition has started | See Section 6.2.4.12 | |
| RXBREAK_END | Error | Break condition has ended | See Section 6.2.4.12 | |
| PAR_FRAME_ERR | Error | Parity or framing error detected | See Section 6.2.4.12 | |
| RX_RD_ERROR | Error | A read from an empty Rx FIFO attempted | See Section 6.2.4.12 | |
| WWT | Status | Work-waiting-timeout value was exceeded | Deasserted after clearing (clear WWT IRQ channel command) | Clear interrupt |

#### 6.2.4.4.2 UIM controller interrupts
The UART_DM_UIM_INTR interrupt (when implemented in the SoC) notifies the chip-level interrupt controllers of events originating in the UIM controller (mostly card removal/insertion and battery-alarm events).

The UART_DM_UIM_INTR signal is an OR function of an internal interrupt vector, calculated by AND-ing the UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_ISR register (interrupt status) with the UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_IMR register (interrupt masking).

`UART_DM_UIM_INTR <= OR (UIM_IRQ_ISR-vector AND UIM_IRQ_IMR-vector)`

Upon receiving an interrupt, the UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_ISR and UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_IMR registers should be read to conclude the events that caused the assertion and react accordingly.

If more than one interrupt bit is high and not masked, clearing a single interrupt bit does not cause the interrupt line to be deasserted. For deassertion, all high bits must be cleared or masked.

#### Table 6-63 UIM controller interrupts summary

| Interrupt | Type | Cause | Behavior | Software reaction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| UIM card removal | Status | Card removal event detected | Deasserted after clearing (UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_CLR register). | Clear interrupt. Clear relevant data paths if active. |
| UIM card insertion | Status | Card insertion event detected | Deasserted after clearing (UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_CLR register). | Clear interrupt. Perform manual UIM activation sequence. |
<!-- page 1777 -->
#### Table 6-63 UIM controller interrupts summary (cont.)

| Interrupt | Type | Cause | Behavior | Software reaction |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Battery alarm | Status | Battery alarm event detected | Deasserted after clearing (UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_CLR register). | Wait for the power to run out. |
| Command done | Status | A configuration/command write finishes propagating to the UIM controller | Deasserted after clearing (UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_CLR register). | Clear interrupt. Perform additional writes if desired. |
<!-- page 1778 -->
### 6.2.4.5 UART system level performance management
The UART performance is bounded by the performance of the serial interface and bandwidth of service on the AHB bus. The serial interface performance can be altered by changing the serial interface bit rate in the UART_DM_CSR register. The external serial device on the other end should be configured respectively.

The maximal UART bit rate is 4 Mbps. For best performance, the AHB bandwidth of each channel should be the same. For using both channels (Rx + Tx), AHB bandwidth should be the sum of each channel bit rates.

Since the AHB bus can read 32 bits per cycle, to avoid overflow, the following condition must exist:

`Data-Rate-Rx (Mbps) + Data-Rate-Tx (Mbps) < Clock-Rate (Mhz) × 32 × α`

where $\alpha$ ($0 < \alpha < 1$) is the relative time-slice that the AHB master can attend to serving the UART controller.

### 6.2.4.6 UART interface modes
The UART can be used for three different interfaces: UART, SIM/UIM, and IrDA.

In general, interface modes are not channel independent, both channel modes (Tx/Rx) are tied.

Switching an interface mode requires resetting and enabling both Rx and Tx channels (as some interfaces, like SIM/UIM, have some correlation between the channels).

#### 6.2.4.6.1 UART interface mode
This is the default interface mode used for communication with other UART protocol devices.

Configuration of this mode is defined in the UART_DM_MR1 and UART_DM_MR2 registers.

#### 6.2.4.6.2 UIM/SIM interface mode
This interface mode is used for communication with a UIM/SIM card. This mode uses a different serial interface signal (UIM interface) than the other modes (UART interface).

This mode is available only when the value of SIM_GLUE_GEN equals to 1 in the UART_DM_GENERICS [GENERIC_SIM_GLUE] register bit.

The UIM/SIM interface mode is selected, when the UART_DM_SIM_CFG [SIM_SEL] register bit is set to 1.

Generally, in context of the data flow, this interface mode behaves quite similarly to the UART interface mode and normal FIFO/BAM control sequences (as described in this document) should be used. Additionally, a few other designated features can be used in this mode:
1. Because the UIM interface has one data line for both Rx + Tx communication, any data transmitted can also be received in the receiver (in addition to incoming data). This is configured in bit MASK_RX in the UART_DM_SIM_CFG register.
<!-- page 1779 -->
2. UIM specifications allow the retransmission of characters whenever the parity check fails. Set bit UIM_RX_MODE of the UART_DM_SIM_CFG register to 0 to enable the retransmission request when a received character from the SIM card contains an error. Reset bit UIM_TX_MODE to 0 to retransmit a character when a retransmission request from the SIM card arrives.
   Alternatively, Rx and Tx channels can work in block mode (errors are checked per block and not per character) where retransmission of a single character is not used. Set bits UIM_RX_MODE and UIM_TX_MODE to 1 for block mode.

##### Using the work-waiting timeout (WWT) timer with UIM
The work-waiting timeout (WWT) hardware counter can be used to detect conditions such as no response from the card or delayed responses from the card for a preprogrammed time length and fire the WWT interrupt. The time duration is configured in the UART_DM_WWT_TIMEOUT register (value in elementary time units). The feature is enabled by issuing a WWT counter enable channel command and disabled with a WWT counter disable channel command via the UART_DM_CR register.

After the WWT counter enable command is issued, one of the following happens:
1. New character is fully received (till the stop bit) in Rx FIFO within the programmed time in UART_DM_WWT_TIMEOUT register – the WWT counter is stopped and interrupt does not fire. To re-enable the counter, a new WWT counter enable command must be issued.
2. No character is received for the programmed time – WWT interrupt is fired.

> [!NOTE]
> If no pull-up is connected to the UIM_DATA line and noise creates such data pattern which can be considered as a start bit, then UART hardware considers this as a valid Rx character. It samples the character (WWT counter is stopped) and no WWT interrupt is fired later.

The WWT timer stops after a single character is received and must be re-enabled again for the subsequent characters in Rx.

If the HW WWT timer is enabled upon every Rx session and not restarted for every valid character that is received, then in order to detect the state when only part of the transfer is received, it is not enough to use only WWT mechanism. The RXSTALE timeout interrupt must be used as well by issuing an Enable Stale Event command in the UART_DM_CR register.

Another case that requires a special treatment is when the card pulls the UIM_DATA line low during Tx transmission (for example, issuing a command to UIM card). In that case, TX_COMP interrupt does not fire as the bytes cannot be successfully shifted out on the data line from the shift register. To receive WWT interrupt in this case WWT counter enable command must be issued (via the UART_DM_CR register) before Tx transmission and include the Tx transmission time in UART_DM_WWT_TIMEOUT register configuration.
<!-- page 1780 -->
#### Figure: Figure 6-41 UART WWT and stale timeout enable commands timing
*Description:* A timing diagram illustrating the enabling of WWT and stale timeout commands during a UIM card communication session. It shows the relative timing of the following events:
- **UART_DM_WWT_TIMEOUT configuration**: Programmed at the start.
- **WWT counter enable**: Triggered before the Tx transmission.
- **Tx command (HW transmit)**: Tx transmission occurs.
- **Enable stale event**: Issued during/after the Tx transmission.
- **IDLE time**: Idle period after Tx completes and before Rx begins.
- **Rx data (UIM card transmit)**: The UIM card transmits data back to the UART.

#### 6.2.4.6.3 IrDA interface mode
This interface mode is used for communication with infrared devices. This mode uses the default serial interface signals (UART interface).

This mode is available only when the value of IRDA_IFC_GEN generic equals to 1 in the UART_DM_GENERICS [GENERIC_IRDA_IFC] register bit.

Configuration of the IrDA mode is defined in the UART_DM_IRDA register, where at least the IRDA_EN bit should be set to 1 to enable this interface mode. Otherwise, the UART protocol is used.

### 6.2.4.7 UART work modes
Work modes of UART define, if either software or BAM-eDML is in charge of transferring data from/to UART.
- **Software mode**: This is a non-BAM use case. The peripheral data and configuration is performed exclusively by the software. This mode, however, creates a high load on software as the internal peripheral controller buffering is low and this causes a high interrupt rate. Software mode can be used for short transactions where BAM configuration overhead may be considerable.
- **BAM mode**: This is a BAM use case. Some of the peripheral data and configuration may be performed by the BAM hardware.

Work modes are determined per data channel, that is the Rx/Tx channels can work in a different mode. Configuring the work mode is done in the UART_DM_DMEN register, where the default value is the software mode for both Tx and Rx channels.

Switching a work mode requires resetting and enabling of the chosen data channel, as described in Figure 6-42.


<!-- page 1781 -->

#### Figure: Figure 6-42 UART work mode switching diagram
*Description:* A flow diagram showing the transition of UART work modes. It starts with "Tx/Rx reset + enable" transitioning to "Work mode initialization". From "Work mode initialization", it branches into two modes: "SW mode (FIFO/legacy)" and "BAM mode".

The UART work modes for Tx/Rx channels are further described in Section 6.2.4.9.4 and Section 6.2.4.10.4.

### 6.2.4.8 UART initialization

#### 6.2.4.8.1 UART general initialization

Table 6-64 lists the registers that must be configured during initialization (after each hard reset). The configurations are in no particular order.

##### Table 6-64 UART general configuration registers

| Register | Description | Recommended values |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| UART_DM_CSR | Clock selection register. Configures the bit rate of the serial interface for each channel. | Should be extracted from clock rate and the desired data rate. |
| UART_DM_MR1 | First mode register. Configures behavior/effect of control flow signals of the UART interface – RFR_N and CTS_N. | Automatic flow control must be used (set CTS_CTL and RX_RDY_CTL register bits). AUTO_RFR_LEVEL must be set to about 90% of Rx FIFO size. |
| UART_DM_MR2 | Second mode register. Configures the different features of UART including different UART protocol configuration (parity, stop-bit length, number of bits per character, and so on). | Use case specific |
<!-- page 1782 -->

##### Table 6-64 UART general configuration registers (continued)

| Register | Description | Recommended values |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| UART_DM_TFWR | Transmit FIFO watermark register. Controls assertion of TXLEV interrupt (software work mode) and space_avail_req signal (BAM work mode). Interrupt/signal is driven high while current amount of words in Tx FIFO is lower or equal (free space for words is greater) than the configured value in this register. | About 50% of the Tx FIFO |
| UART_DM_RFWR | Receive FIFO watermark register. Controls assertion of RXLEV interrupt (software work mode) and data_avail_req signal (BAM work mode). Interrupt/signal is driven high while current amount of words in Rx FIFO is greater than the configured value in this register. | About 50% of the Rx FIFO |
| UART_DM_IMR | Interrupt mask register | See Section 6.2.4.4.1 |
| UART_DM_IPR | Interrupt programming register. Mainly configures the stale timeout counter value. | Depending on the use:<br>- Use lower values when data is successive and is needed quickly<br>- Use high values for discontinuous data and when there is no rush of reading. |
| UART_DM_BADR | Base address register. Controls the division of UART FIFO-RAM between Tx and Rx FIFOs. | About 50% of RAM size. |
| UART_DM_CR | UART command register | Set to CR Protection Enable command to prevent software from overriding incomplete command. |
