### 6.2.4.9 UART Tx channel operation

#### 6.2.4.9.1 UART Tx channel data flow

AHB master (SW/eDML) reads data packed into words from the system memory and writes it to the Tx channel through dedicated registers on the AHB bus. UART stores them in the Tx FIFO. It then unpacks the words into characters and transmits them one character at a time through the UART or UIM/SIM serial interfaces, as shown in Figure 6-43.
<!-- page 1784 -->

#### Figure: Figure 6-43 UART Tx channel data flow
*Description:* A block diagram showing the flow of data for the UART Tx channel. It starts with the AHB bus where data is written. The data goes into the TX-FIFO. From the TX-FIFO, it passes through an unpacking buffer. Then, it goes to the Transmitter block, which feeds into the SIM, UIM interface (IFC), or UART interface.

The following data transformations occur inside UART for the Tx channel:
1. Data is unpacked from word format into character format.
2. Character data is transformed in two ways:
   - Inversion of each bit polarity (that is, logic 1 is replaced by logic 0). Configured for the IrDA interface by setting the INVERT_IRDA_TX bit of the UART_DM_IRDA register. For the SIM/UIM interface, this is done by setting the INV_D bit in UART_DM_SIM_CFG register.
   - Swapping of character bit order, making the MSB bit the first in order. This can be configured for the SIM/UIM interface by setting the SWAP_D bit in UART_DM_SIM_CFG register.

#### 6.2.4.9.2 UART Tx channel timeline

This section describes the internal timelines of the UART controller for the Tx channel. These timelines may alter according to different configuration modes (software or BAM mode).

Figure 6-44 describes a complete Tx transfer.

#### Figure: Figure 6-44 UART TX channel zoomed-out timeline diagram
*Description:* A timeline diagram with three tracks: AHB bus, TX-FIFO level, and UART transmitter status.
- Track 1 (AHB bus): Shows "configuration" writes at step 1. At step 2, "Writes to TX-FIFO" occur, writing words 1, 2, 3, 4. At step 3, another block of "Writes to TX-FIFO" occurs for words 61, 62, 63, 64. At step 5, a new block of writes begins (1, 2, 3, 4).
- Track 2 (TX-FIFO): Shows the FIFO fill level. At step 2, the level increases to 4 as words 1, 2, 3, 4 are written. It decreases as characters are transmitted. At step 3, it increases to 64 as words 61-64 are written, then decreases again. At step 5, it increases again as words 1-4 are written.
- Track 3 (UART transmitter): Shows "Character transmission". Transmission starts after step 2, sending "Char 1.1". It continues until step 4 where it finishes sending "Char 64.3" and "Char 64.4". After step 5, it starts transmitting the next set of characters, starting with "Char 1.1" and "Char 1.2".

The following comments see the numbering within Figure 6-44:
1. The Tx channel is configured for the desired configuration mode. Configuration is done by the software using writes to the configuration registers through the AHB bus.
2. Before writing data to the Tx FIFO, Tx transfer should be activated. See Section 6.2.4.9.4 for the procedure for relevant work mode and Section 6.2.4.9.3 for the packing mode for each of the configuration prior to Tx transfer activation. Once activated, the AHB master can write data to the Tx FIFO as long as it is not full. The write procedure also alternates between work modes, see relevant work mode in Section 6.2.4.9.4.
<!-- page 1785 -->

3. When a Tx transfer is deactivated, additional writes to Tx FIFO are ignored.
4. Once the Tx FIFO is emptied (all words were moved to the unpacking buffer), a new Tx transfer can be activated.
5. Upon the end of transmission of a Tx transfer and in case a new transfer is not yet activated, the Tx complete interrupt is fired.

In Figure 6-45, only the beginning of a Tx transfer is described. This is to explain in depth the different stages in a characters lifetime through the Tx channel.

#### Figure: Figure 6-45 UART Tx channel zoomed-in timeline diagram
*Description:* A detailed timing diagram showing how data propagates through different buffers and clock domains.
Tracks:
- AHB bus: Shows "configuration" at step 1. At step 2, "Word 1", "Word 2", "Word 3", and "Word 4" are written via the AHB bus.
- TX-FIFO: Holds "Word 1" and "Word 2" after they are written.
- Unpacking buffer: At step 3, "Word 1" is drawn from the TX-FIFO. Subsequently, "Word 2" and "Word 3" are drawn.
- TX-async-FIFO AHB domain: At step 4, the unpacked characters "Char 1.1", "Char 1.2", "Char 1.3", and "Char 1.4" from Word 1 are loaded. Then, characters "Char 2.1", "Char 2.2", "Char 2.3", and "Char 2.4" from Word 2 are loaded.
- TX-async-FIFO UART domain: At step 5, characters "Char 1.1" and "Char 1.2" are synchronized to the UART domain.
- UART transmitter: At step 6, the transmitter draws "Char 1.1" and starts "Character transmission". This is followed by "Char 1.2", "Char 1.3", "Char 1.4", and "Char 2.1".

The following comments see the numbering within Figure 6-45:
1. Tx channel configuration
2. AHB master writes data to Tx FIFO
3. An empty unpacking buffer draws a word from the non-empty Tx FIFO.
4. Valid characters (all characters are assumed valid except on transfer boundaries) are moved to the Tx async FIFO as long as it is not full.
5. Characters are synchronized between clock domains until valid on the UART domain side of the async FIFO. This might take a few clocks of each domain depending on ratio and phase of both clocks.
6. An empty transmitter draws a character from a non-empty async FIFO and transmits it through the selected serial interface.

#### 6.2.4.9.3 UART Tx channel data packing

The UART packing mode for the Tx channel can change the way characters are packed into words in the controller FIFOs and when data is transferred on the AHB bus. UART Tx channel can be used with two different packing configurations: 4-characters per word and 1-character per word.

Packing modes are channel independent, that is, the Tx channel can work in a different packing mode than the Rx channel.
<!-- page 1786 -->

##### UART Tx 4-character packing mode

This is the default (and backward compatible) packing mode for the Tx channel, enabled by clearing the TX_SC_ENABLE bit of the UART_DM_DMEN register to 0.

In this mode, four characters of every word written to the TX FIFO through the AHB bus is transmitted, unless amount of transmitted characters scheduled for current Tx transfer was exceeded (NO_CHARS_FOR_TX), see Figure 6-46. In that case, all characters beyond the transfer limits are ignored and not transmitted. It is not permitted to write more words to Tx-FIFO registers than the value in register field UART_DM_NO_CHARS_FOR_TX [TX_TOTAL_TRANS_LEN]/4 (rounded up).

#### Figure: Figure 6-46 UART Tx data packing: 4-character mode
*Description:* A block diagram representing a 32-bit word. The word is split into four 8-bit character fields: Data #1 in bits [7:0], Data #2 in bits [15:8], Data #3 in bits [23:16], and Data #4 in bits [31:24].

##### UART Tx single-character packing mode

This packing mode is designed to eliminate the need for Tx transfer initialization (via UART_DM_NO_CHARS_FOR_TX register). This mode is enabled by setting the TX_SC_ENABLE bit of the UART_DM_DMEN register to 1.

In this mode, only the LSB character of each word written to the Tx FIFO through the AHB bus is transmitted, see Figure 6-47. Therefore, data in the system memory should be prepared as follows:

#### Figure: Figure 6-47 UART Tx data packing: single character mode
*Description:* A block diagram representing a 32-bit word. The LSB byte (bits [7:0]) contains the "Data" character, while the remaining upper bytes (bits [15:8], [23:16], and [31:24]) are filled with zeroes (0x00) and ignored.

Any data in bits [31-8] is ignored.

When using this mode, the Tx FIFO holds the data as described above, meaning that its data capacity is reduced to one fourth of the normal capacity.

#### 6.2.4.9.4 UART Tx channel control sequences

Sequences differ significantly between work modes. The Tx channel is described according to its work modes via control sequence diagrams in Section [Wait, section reference missing in source?] and Section [Wait, section reference missing in source?]. Procedure descriptions are also included to explain abbreviations in the diagrams.

The common Tx procedure (valid for both working modes) is as follows:
1. Prior to control sequence, after completing channel configuration, software must reset and enable the Tx data channel. The following sequence should be executed:
   - Issue reset transmitter channel command via the UART_DM_CR register.
   - Issue enable transmitter command via the UART_DM_CR [UART_TX_EN] register field.
<!-- page 1787 -->

2. Set the TFWR value in UART_DM_TFWR register. In the software mode, this configuration is used to receive the watermark interrupt TXLEV. In BAM mode, this value is used to handle the 'space_avail_req' for eDML. The value of 0 is illegal in BAM mode.

##### UART Tx software mode sequence

The control sequence diagrams for Tx software mode are shown in Figure 6-48 and Figure 6-49. Each Tx packing mode requires a slightly different control sequence.

#### Figure: Figure 6-48 UART Tx software mode 4-character-packing control sequence
*Description:* A flowchart showing the control sequence for UART Tx software mode with 4-character packing.
1. Start: **TX channel configuration**
2. **Issue Reset+Enable commands**
3. **Write TX-transfer length (in bytes) to NO_CHARS_FOR_TX register**
4. **WAIT for TXLEV-IRQ**
5. **Execute ‘TXLEV’ writes of data (or less – if NO_CHARS_FOR_TX exhausted) to TX-FIFO**
6. Decision: **NO_CHARS_FOR_TX exhausted ?**
   - *If No:* Loop back to step 4 (**WAIT for TXLEV-IRQ**). Concurrently, "Data is transmitted through the serial interface".
   - *If Yes:* Proceed to step 7.
7. Decision: **Need indication for transmission finish ?**
   - *If Yes:* **Wait for TX-COMP irq**, then **Clear it !**
   - *If No:* **Wait for TX_READY irq**, then **Clear it !**
<!-- page 1788 -->

#### Figure: Figure 6-49 UART Tx software mode single-character-packing control sequence
*Description:* A flowchart showing the control sequence for UART Tx software mode with single-character packing.
1. Start: **Initialize UART_DM**
2. **Issue reset + enable commands**
3. **WAIT for TXLEV-IRQ**
4. **Execute ‘TXLEV’ writes (or less – if no more currently scheduled) of data (1 char per word) to TX-FIFO**
5. Loop back to step 3 (**WAIT for TXLEV-IRQ**). Concurrently, "Data is transmitted through the serial interface".

The Tx procedure for software working mode is as follows:
1. Set the UART_DM_NO_CHARS_FOR_TX register.
2. Write data to UART transmit FIFO registers: UART_DM_TF through UART_DM_TF_16. Use the TXLEV interrupt space available indication in TX FIFO (see Section 6.2.4.4.1 for more details).
3. Use either TX_READY or TX_COMP interrupt. Clear the chosen interrupt. After receiving the interrupt, new transfer can be scheduled (for the difference between TX_READY and TX_COMP interrupts see Section 6.2.4.4.1). The interrupt that is left unused must be masked.
<!-- page 1789 -->

##### UART Tx BAM mode sequence

The control sequence diagram for Tx BAM-mode is shown in Figure 6-50.

#### Figure: Figure 6-50 UART Tx BAM mode control sequence
*Description:* A flowchart showing the control sequence for UART Tx BAM mode.
1. Start: **Initialize BAM-Lite/eDML**
2. **Initialize UART_DM**
3. **Issue reset + enable commands**
4. **Issue TX-BAM start IFC command**
5. **UART_DM signals BAM with its data space amount**
6. **BAM writes data to UART_DM**
7. Simultaneously:
   - **Data is transmitted through the serial interface**
   - **BAM consumer procedure** (includes descriptor preparations/handling, transaction-end).

The Tx procedure for BAM working mode is as follows:
1. Execute Start TX BAM IFC channel command in UART_DM_CR register.
2. Use BAM consumer pipe to write data to UART. For BAM-Lite/eDML related procedures, see the Bus Access Manager (BAM) chapter.
3. Do not use UART interrupts for completion indication. Instead, use BAM interrupt. In order to receive the interrupt set the EOT and NWD bits on the last descriptor. The interrupt is issued after all the data is transmitted. For more information, see the section Pipe descriptors the Bus access manager (BAM) chapter.
<!-- page 1790 -->

#### 6.2.4.10 UART Rx channel operation

##### 6.2.4.10.1 UART Rx channel data flow

The Rx channel receives data one character at a time through the UART or UIM/SIM serial interfaces. It packs them into words and stores them in the Rx FIFO. Words are then read from the Rx FIFO through the AHB bus by an AHB master (SW/eDML) that stores them in the system memory, see Figure 6-51.

#### Figure: Figure 6-51 UART Rx channel data flow
*Description:* A block diagram showing the flow of data for the UART Rx channel. Data is received through the SIM, UIM interface, or UART interface. It passes to the Receiver block, which feeds into a Packing buffer. The packed data is then stored in the RX-FIFO and read out via the AHB bus.

The following data transformations occur inside UART for the Rx channel:
1. Data is packed from character format into word format.
2. Character data is transformed in two ways:
   - Inversion of each bit polarity (that is, logic 1 is replaced by logic 0). Configured for the IrDA interface by setting the INVERT_IRDA_RX bit of the UART_DM_IRDA register. For the SIM/UIM interface, this is done by setting the INV_D bit in UART_DM_SIM_CFG register.
   - Swapping of character bit order, making the MSB bit the first in order. This can be configured for the SIM/UIM interface by setting the SWAP_D bit in UART_DM_SIM_CFG register.

##### 6.2.4.10.2 UART Rx channel timeline

This section describes internal timelines of the UART controller for the Rx channel. These timelines may alter according to the different configuration modes (software or BAM mode).

Figure 6-52 describes the beginning of an Rx transfer. It explains in depth the different stages in a character lifetime through the Rx channel.

#### Figure: Figure 6-52 UART Rx channel zoomed-in timeline diagram
*Description:* A timing diagram showing how received characters propagate through the receiver logic and clock domains to the RX-FIFO.
Tracks:
- UART receiver: After configuration at steps 1 and 2, characters (Char 1 to Char 12) are received serially.
- RX-async-FIFO UART domain: Characters are pushed into the async FIFO (UART clock domain) at step 3.
- RX-async-FIFO AHB domain: Characters are synchronized to the AHB clock domain at step 4.
- Packing buffer: At step 5, characters are packed. The diagram shows characters accumulating (e.g., Char 1, then Char 1 & 2, then Char 1 & 2 & 3). Once a word is full (typically 4 characters), it is ready to be written.
- RX-FIFO: At step 6, packed words (Word 1 containing Char 1-4, Word 2 containing Char 5-8) are written to the RX-FIFO, increasing its fill level.


<!-- page 1791 -->

The following comments refer to the numbering used within Figure 6-52 (or the receiver block diagram):
1. Rx channel is configured for the desired configuration mode. Configuration is done by the software using writes to configuration registers through the AHB bus. When done, the Rx channel is prepared to receive incoming characters through the serial interface.
2. Communication on the serial interface is buffered in the receiver until a single character is received and validated by parity check.
3. Each character received is moved to the Rx async FIFO (if not full) for synchronization towards the AHB domain.
4. Characters are synchronized between clock domains until valid on the AHB domain side of the async FIFO. This might take a few clocks of each domain depending on the ratio and phase of both the clocks.
5. Valid characters are moved to the packing buffer (if it is ready to receive them).
6. When it is filled with four characters or an Rx flush sequence is initiated, the contents of the packing buffer (a single word with up to four valid characters) are written to the Rx FIFO.

Figure 6-53 describes a complete Rx transfer.

#### Figure 6-53: UART Rx channel zoomed-out timeline diagram
*Description:* A timeline diagram showing three parallel tracks: UART receiver, RX-FIFO, and AHB bus.
- **UART receiver track** shows:
  - Configuration phase (marked with '1').
  - Serial reception of characters (numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, ... 61, 62, 63, 64, 65, 66, ... 87, 88), representing a burst of incoming characters (marked with '2').
  - A second burst of incoming characters (numbered 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6) following a gap.
- **RX-FIFO track** shows:
  - Word 1 being populated.
  - Word 1 appearing in RX-FIFO after the characters are received and packed.
- **AHB bus track** shows:
  - Transfer activities corresponding to reading from RX-FIFO.
- **Timeline markers:**
  - 1: Rx channel configuration.
  - 2: Rx transfer activation and receipt of characters.
  - 3: AHB master reading words from RX FIFO.
  - 4: Rx transfer deactivation (timeout).
  - 5: Finish procedure and reading remaining data.
  - 6: New Rx transfer activation.

The following comments refer to the numbering used within Figure 6-53:
1. Rx channel configuration.
2. Rx transfer activation procedure is executed (work mode (software or BAM) dependent). Characters are received through the serial interface, packed and stored in the Rx FIFO as words.
3. AHB master reads the words from Rx FIFO after being notified of the contents of FIFO.
4. Rx transfer is deactivated by a transfer end event, in this case - characters stopped arriving and a timeout caused the deactivation. The transfer deactivation does not mean characters cannot be received, they will only be associated with the next transfer after its activation.
5. Executing an Rx transfer finish procedure and reading all of the data associated with that Rx transfer from the Rx FIFO.
6. After finishing reading previous transfer data, a new Rx transfer can be activated.

### 6.2.4.10.3 UART Rx channel data packing

The UART packing mode for the Rx channel can change the way characters are packed into words in the controller FIFOs and when data is transferred on the AHB bus. UART Rx channel can be used with two different packing configurations: 4-characters per word and 1-character per word.
<!-- page 1792 -->

Packing modes are channel independent, that is, the Rx channel can work in a different packing mode than the Tx channel.

#### UART Rx 4-character packing mode

This is the default (and backward compatible) packing mode for the Rx channel, enabled by clearing the `RX_SC_ENABLE` bit of the `UART_DM_DMEN` register to '0'.

In this mode, characters arriving through the serial interface are packed to words efficiently, each word written to the Rx FIFO contains four characters, unless the packing buffer was flushed for some reason and then some characters or even whole words might be invalid, see Figure 6-54. From the AHB master perspective, in software working mode, the presence of invalid characters is notified to software upon reading the `UART_DM_RX_TOTAL_SNAP` register. In BAM working mode, communication on the BASI interface insures only valid characters are read.

#### Figure 6-54: UART Rx data packing: 4-character mode
*Description:* A 32-bit register layout diagram showing how four 8-bit data characters are packed into a single word:
* Bits [31:24]: Data #4
* Bits [23:16]: Data #3
* Bits [15:8]: Data #2
* Bits [7:0]: Data #1

#### UART Rx single-character packing mode

This packing mode is designed to imitate the functionality of a legacy UART controller (integrated in a legacy SoC). This packing mode disables the functionality of the Rx packing buffer, and therefore every received character is immediately transferred to the Rx FIFO. This enables the AHB master to read every character that arrives without having to wait for the packing buffer to fill up for a flush.

This mode is enabled by setting the `RX_SC_ENABLE` bit of the `UART_DM_DMEN` register to 1.

In this mode, only the LSB character of each word written to the Rx FIFO contains a valid data character. Bits [9:8] contain additional data (parity/framing errors indications), see Figure 6-55. Extraction of valid data should be done by the software after the data was transferred to the system memory. Valid data is packed as shown in Figure 6-55.

#### Figure 6-55: UART Rx data packing: single character mode
*Description:* A 32-bit register layout diagram showing how a single character is packed into a word:
* Bits [31:24]: `0x00` (unused)
* Bits [23:16]: `0x00` (unused)
* Bits [15:10]: `0x00` (unused)
* Bits [9:8]: `extra bits` (containing parity/framing error indications)
* Bits [7:0]: `Data` (the single received character)

Similar to the Tx channel, the data capacity of the Rx FIFO in this mode is also reduced to one fourth of its normal capacity.
<!-- page 1793 -->

Bits [9:8] carry the following additional data:
* **Bit 8**: High when a parity/framing error was detected with this character, otherwise low.
* **Bit 9**: High when character received is suspicious of being the result of a break event (all zeros + zero parity + framing error).

### 6.2.4.10.4 UART Rx channel control sequences

Sequences differ significantly between work modes. The Rx channel is described according to its work modes via control sequence diagrams in Section and Section . Procedure descriptions are also included to explain abbreviations in the diagrams.

The common Rx procedure (valid for both working modes) is as follows:
1. Prior to control sequence, after completing the channel configuration, software must reset and enable the Rx data channel. The following sequence should be executed:
   * Issue reset receiver channel command via the `UART_DM_CR` register.
   * Issue enable receiver command via the `UART_DM_CR` [`UART_RX_EN`] register bit.
2. Set the `RFWR` value in the `UART_DM_RFWR` register. In software mode, this configuration is used to receive the watermark interrupt `RXLEV`. In BAM mode, this value is used to handle the 'avail_data_req' for eDML. The value of 0 is illegal in BAM mode.
<!-- page 1794 -->

#### UART Rx software mode sequence

The control sequence diagram for Rx software working mode is shown in Figure 6-56.

#### Figure 6-56: UART Rx software mode control sequence
*Description:* A flowchart outlining the UART Rx software mode control sequence, divided into "Transfer Initialization" and "Transfer In-Progress" phases.
```mermaid
graph TD
    %% Phase: Transfer Initialization
    Start([Initialize UART]) --> ResetCmd[Issue reset + enable commands]
    ResetCmd --> DecLength{Is expected/desired<br>Rx-transfer length known?}
    
    DecLength -- Yes --> WriteDMRX[Write length in bytes to DMRX register]
    DecLength -- No --> WriteDMRXMax[Write large value to DMRX register<br>all-ones]
    
    WriteDMRX --> DecStale{Use timeout-stale?}
    WriteDMRXMax --> DecStale
    
    DecStale -- Yes --> EnableStale[Issue enable T.O.-stale command]
    DecStale -- No --> WaitState[WAIT for RXLEV-IRQ / STALE-IRQ / SW-stale demand]
    EnableStale --> WaitState

    %% Phase: Transfer In-Progress
    WaitState --> DecSWStale{Issue SW stale?}
    DecSWStale -- Yes --> IssueSWStale[Issue SW-stale command] --> ReadFIFO[Read remaining bytes in RX-FIFO]
    
    WaitState --> DecStaleIRQ{Stale IRQ?}
    DecStaleIRQ -- Yes --> ReadSnap[Read SNAP register] --> ClearIRQ[Clear IRQ] --> ReadFIFO
    
    WaitState --> DecRXLEV{RXLEV-IRQ received?}
    DecRXLEV -- Yes --> ReadRXLEV[Execute RXLEV reads from Rx-FIFO] --> WaitState
```
*Note:* During the Wait State, data can be potentially received through the serial interface.

The procedure for Rx software working mode is as follows:
1. Configure `UART_DM_DMRX` register.
2. Configure timeout-stale feature, if required, in the `UART_DM_IPR` [`STALE_TIMEOUT`] register fields.
3. Read data from `UART_DM_RF` through `UART_DM_RF16` registers, using `RXLEV` interrupt as indication for data arrived.
<!-- page 1795 -->

4. If `RXSTALE` interrupt is received, read the `UART_DM_RX_TOTAL_SNAP` register. According to this value, software must calculate how many data reads have to be executed to complete reading that transfer. The value in the `UART_DM_RX_TOTAL_SNAP` register might be higher than the `UART_DM_DMRX` register value, if the `DMRX` value is not a multiple of 4.
5. SW force stale command via the `UART_DM_CR` register must be used only in extraordinary conditions (for example, abort of the transfer).
<!-- page 1796 -->

#### UART Rx BAM mode sequence

The control sequence diagram for Rx BAM working mode is shown in Figure 6-57 (note: the text has a typo referring to "Tx BAM working mode").

#### Figure 6-57: UART Rx BAM mode control sequence
*Description:* A flowchart detailing the UART Rx BAM mode control sequence, supporting both cyclic-queue and standard SW-configured BAM paths.
```mermaid
graph TD
    Start([Initialize BAM-Lite/eDML]) --> InitUART[Initialize UART]
    InitUART --> ResetCmd[Issue reset + enable commands]
    ResetCmd --> DecConfig{Use SW<br>configuration?}
    
    %% Left path: No SW configuration (Cyclic-queue)
    DecConfig -- No --> SetReAct[Set Rx-transfer re-activate bit]
    SetReAct --> EnableCyclic[Enable DMRX cyclic-queue]
    EnableCyclic --> WriteDMRX_L[Write length in bytes to DMRX register]
    WriteDMRX_L --> SetStaleReEnable_L[Set stale-re-enable bit]
    SetStaleReEnable_L --> EnableTO_L[Issue enable timeout-stale command]
    EnableTO_L --> StartIFC_L[Issue RX-BAM start IFC command]
    
    %% Right path: Use SW configuration
    DecConfig -- Yes --> WriteDMRX_R[Write length in bytes to DMRX register]
    WriteDMRX_R --> DecLength{Is expected/desired<br>Rx-transfer length known?}
    
    DecLength -- Yes --> DecStale_Y{Use Timeout-stale?}
    DecStale_Y -- Yes --> SetStaleReEnable_R[Set stale-re-enable bit] --> EnableTO_R1[Issue enable timeout-stale command] --> StartIFC_R[Issue RX-BAM start IFC command]
    DecStale_Y -- No --> StartIFC_R
    
    DecLength -- No --> DecStale_N{Use Timeout-stale?}
    DecStale_N -- Yes --> EnableTO_R2[Issue enable timeout-stale command] --> StartIFC_R
    DecStale_N -- No --> StartIFC_R

    %% BAM operations
    StartIFC_L --> BAMProc_L[BAM producer-procedure: Descriptor preparations & Handling transaction-end]
    StartIFC_R --> BAMProc_R[BAM producer-procedure: Descriptor preparations & Handling transaction-end]
    
    BAMProc_L --> UARTBAM_L[UART signals BAM with its data content amount]
    BAMProc_R --> UARTBAM_R[UART signals transaction-end to BAM]
    
    UARTBAM_L --> BAMRead_L[BAM reads data from UART]
    UARTBAM_R --> WaitEnd[Wait for BAM transaction-end signal] --> BAMRead_R[BAM reads data from UART]
    
    BAMRead_L --> SWStale_L{SW-stale demand?}
    SWStale_L -- Yes --> IssueSWStale_L[Issue SW-stale command]
    
    BAMRead_R --> SWStale_R{SW-stale demand?}
    SWStale_R -- Yes --> IssueSWStale_R[Issue SW-stale command]
```
*Note:* During the process, data can be potentially received through the serial interface.

The procedure for Rx BAM working mode is as follows:
1. Set the `UART_DM_RX_TRANS_CTRL` [`RX_TRANS_AUTO_RE_ACTIVATE`] register bit.
2. Set the `UART_DM_RX_TRANS_CTRL` [`RX_STALE_AUTO_RE_EN`] register bit.
3. Set the `UART_DM_RX_TRANS_CTRL` [`RX_DMRX_CYCLIC_EN`] register bit.
<!-- page 1797 -->

4. Set the value in the `UART_DM_DMRX` register to descriptor length size. In case the `UART_DM_DMRX` register value is not a multiple of 4, the descriptor size should be a value greater than a `UART_DM_DMRX` value and a multiple of 4. For example, if the `UART_DM_DMRX` register value is 5, the corresponding descriptor size should be 8.
5. Use BAM producer pipe to receive data from UART. For BAM-Lite/eDML related procedures see the *Bus Access Manager (BAM)* chapter.
6. Do not use any UART interrupt for completion indication. Use BAM interrupts instead. The UART controller issues EOT (end of transfer) signal to BAM either when the `UART_DM_DMRX` register value is reached, or timeout has expired, or SW Force Stale command is issued via the `UART_DM_CR` register. This causes an EOT interrupt (`TRNSFR_END_IRQ`) on the BAM producer pipe. For more information, see the section *BAM interrupts* in the *Bus Access Manager (BAM)* chapter.
7. SW Force Stale command via the `UART_DM_CR` register must be used only in extraordinary conditions (for example, abort of the transfer).

### 6.2.4.11 UIM operation

#### 6.2.4.11.1 UIM operation overview

UART0 and UART1 controllers are integrated with a single UIM controller. The UIM module is in charge of implementing a deactivation sequence on the UIM interface lines in case of a UIM card removal event or battery-alarm event (battery at low voltage or pulled out). The UIM controller holds a separate logic for each UIM IO interface assigned to a corresponding UART controller.

#### Figure 6-58: UART integration with UIM
*Description:* A block diagram showing the integration between UART0/UART1, the UIM controller, external DV pads, PMIC, and UIM cards.
```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph BLSP
        UART0[UART0]
        UART1[UART1]
        
        subgraph UIM_Controller["UIM Controller"]
            UIM_IO1["UIM IO Controller #1"]
            UIM_IO2["UIM IO Controller #2"]
        end
    end
    
    subgraph Pads["DV Pads"]
        Pads1[UIM-interface #1 pads]
        Pads2[UIM-interface #2 pads]
    end
    
    UIM_Card1[UIM Card #1]
    UIM_Card2[UIM Card #2]
    PMIC[PMIC]
    
    UART0 <-->|UIM data & clock<br>config & commands<br>status| UIM_IO1
    UART1 <-->|UIM data & clock<br>config & commands<br>status| UIM_IO2
    
    UIM_IO1 <--> Pads1 <--> UIM_Card1
    UIM_IO2 <--> Pads2 <--> UIM_Card2
    
    PMIC -->|vdd1| UIM_Card1
    PMIC -->|vdd2| UIM_Card2
```

Configuration and control of the UIM controller is done through the UART AHB bus to dedicated registers in its address space. Each UART controller holds the registers connected to its assigned UIM IO controller.
<!-- page 1798 -->

A serial interface is used to direct signals from a UART controller to the UIM card in normal working mode. When a deactivation event occurs, the UIM controller overrides this interface to execute the deactivation sequence.

The UIM controller provides an alarm interface with the chipset PMIC which is used for two purposes:
* To detect battery alarm events originating in the PMIC to notify MPM and interrupt controller and to execute the deactivation sequence
* To send out UIM controller messages to the PMIC to signal a request to cut off the power supply to a UIM card

#### 6.2.4.11.2 UIM control sequence

The control sequence diagram for the UIM-controller is shown in Figure 6-59.

#### Figure 6-59: UIM control sequence
*Description:* A flowchart detailing the state transitions and control flow of the UIM controller, including initialization, configuration, card presence detection, activation, active communication, and handling deactivation events.
```mermaid
graph TD
    HWReset([HW reset]) --> OverriddenState[Overridden state]
    OverriddenState --> DecConfig{Configuration<br>required?}
    
    DecConfig -- Yes --> ExecConfig[Execute a configuration-write]
    ExecConfig --> WaitConfig[WAIT for UIM-Write done] --> OverriddenState
    
    DecConfig -- No --> DecCardPresent{Card present?}
    
    DecCardPresent -- No --> WaitCard[WAIT for card present indication]
    WaitCard --> ExecActivation[Execute UIM-activation sequence]
    
    DecCardPresent -- Yes --> ExecActivation
    
    ExecActivation --> ConfigUART[Configure UART_DM for UIM work]
    ConfigUART --> ConfigTLMM[Configure TLMM for UIM-controller use of UIM interface pads]
    ConfigTLMM --> UIMCommState[UIM communication state]
    
    UIMCommState --> DecDeactEvent{Deactivation event<br>card-removal/battery-alarm<br>occurred?}
    DecDeactEvent -- Yes --> DeactExec[Deactivation sequence executed<br>should be enabled]
    DeactExec --> InterruptsFired[Relevant interrupts are fired]
    InterruptsFired --> ExecRecover[Execute a recover-command]
    ExecRecover --> CheckCard{Check card still present}
    
    UIMCommState --> HWDeact[Execute a HW deactivation command]
    HWDeact --> CheckCard
    
    CheckCard --> OverriddenState
    
    UIMCommState --> HandleInterrupts[Handle UIM interrupts]
```

The procedure for UIM control is as follows:
<!-- page 1799 -->

1. **Execute a configuration write**: Write to the `UART_DM_UIM_CFG` register. Configuration of the `UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_IMR` register can be executed here as well (does not require waiting for the `UIM_IO_WRITE_DONE` interrupt).
2. **Wait for UIM_IO_WRITE_DONE interrupt**:
   * `UIM_IO_WRITE_DONE` interrupt was detected.
   * `UIM_IO_WRITE_IN_PROGRESS` bit in the `UART_DM_UIM_IO_STATUS` register was deasserted.
3. **Wait 100 μs** before issuing another command to the UIM controller. This time is required for the command to setup inside the UIM controller, before issuing a new command.
4. **Check for card presence** via the `CARD_PRESENCE` bit in the `UART_DM_UIM_IO_STATUS` register. This value is directly linked to a correct configuration of the `UIM_PRESENT_POLARITY` bit in the `UART_DM_UIM_CFG` register according to the used UIM card slot.
5. **Wait for card present indication**:
   * Card insertion interrupt was detected. See Section 6.2.4.4.2.
   * Card presence bit `CARD_PRESENCE` in the `UART_DM_UIM_IO_STATUS` register was asserted.
6. **Execute UIM activation sequence**: A manual execution of the activation sequence (for reference, see the UIM specification: ISO_IEC_7816-1/2/3/4 ETSI_TS_102_221_V7.10.0) by software directly on the UIM interface IOs. This requires configuring the SoC TLMM so that the UIM interface IOs are not driven by the UIM controller. At the end of this sequence, UIM IOs should not be returned to UIM controller use until specified. See Section 6.2.4.11.3.
7. **Execute a recover command**: Write 1 to the `RECOVER_FROM_HW_DEACTIVATION` bit of the `UART_DM_UIM_CMD` register.
8. **Execute a HW deactivation command**: Write 1 to the `INITIATE_HW_DEACTIVATION` bit of the `UART_DM_UIM_CMD` register.
9. **Handle UIM interrupts**: When the UIM interrupt line is fired, do the following:
   * Read `UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_ISR` to conclude which event/events occurred.
   * Write 1 to matching bits in `UART_DM_UIM_IRQ_CLR`.

#### 6.2.4.11.3 UIM activation sequence

This section assumes that the UIM controller has made a deactivation and it controls the UIM lines. For reference, see ISO/IEC 7816-3 standard, Part 3, paragraph *activation, resets and class selection*, figure *activation and cold reset*. The purpose of the activation sequence is to recreate the referenced figure from that standard.

1. Switch on the power to UIM.
2. Drive SoC TLMM inputs of the `UIM_DATA` and `UIM_CLK` lines to zero. See Section 6.3 for more information.
3. Move control of the above UIM lines to the TLMM block by configuring the `TLMM_IE_CTRL_DISABLE` [`IE_CTRL_DISABLE`] register bit (see also Section 6.3.2). The purpose of steps 1 through 3 is to move the control on the UIM pads to software, while they stay in deactivated state.
<!-- page 1800 -->

4. Activate `UIM_CLK` in the UART controller.
5. Issue recover command to the UIM controller via the `RECOVER_FROM_HW_DEACTIVATION` bit of the `UART_DM_UIM_CMD` register. After this stage, the UIM controller should be transparent to `UIM_DATA` and `UIM_CLK`.
6. Move the `UIM_CLK` pad signal to UIM controller control, by configuring the `TLMM_IE_CTRL_DISABLE` [`IE_CTRL_DISABLE`] register bit. `UIM_CLK` should now be running on the `UIM_CLK` pad.
7. Move the `UIM_DATA` pad signal to UIM controller control by configuring the `TLMM_IE_CTRL_DISABLE` [`IE_CTRL_DISABLE`] register bit. Stable 1 should appear on the `UIM_DATA` pad.

### 6.2.4.12 UART error detection and handling

The UART controller might encounter the following errors:
* UART protocol exceptions (bad parity, faulty stop bit, break)
* Data transfer exceptions on the AHB bus (writing to a full FIFO, reading from an empty FIFO)
* Rx channel overrun (all internal buffers have been filled and characters keep being received)

#### 6.2.4.12.1 UART error detection

Table 6-67 lists the UART error detections.

#### Table 6-67: UART error detection

| Error (Rx channel) | Severity | Cause | Signaling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Parity** | Warning | Receiver detected an incorrect parity bit. | Interrupt.<br>Bit `PAR_FRAME_ERR_IRQ` of `UART_DM_ISR` register. |
| **Framing** | Warning | Receiver sampled a low Rx line on stop bit (should be high). | Interrupt.<br>Bit `PAR_FRAME_ERR_IRQ` of `UART_DM_ISR` register.<br>In single character packing, matching bit beside this character will be set. |
| **Break** | Warning | Receiver sampled an `0x00` character with invalid stop bit. | Interrupt.<br>Bits `RXBREAK_CHANGE` or `RX_BREAK_START` of `UART_DM_ISR` register. |
| **Data-read** | Info | AHB master executed a read transfer from the RX FIFO while it was empty. | Interrupt.<br>Bit `RX_RD_ERROR_IRQ` of `UART_DM_ISR` register. |
| **Overrun** | Warning | A character arrived while RX FIFO, while all of UART internal buffers (RX FIFO, packing buffer, async FIFO) were full. | Status.<br>Bit `UART_OVERRUN` of the `UART_DM_SR` register. |




<!-- page 1801 -->

#### Table 6-67 UART error detection

| Error | Severity | Cause | Signaling |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tx channel** | | | |
| Parity | Warning | Incorrect parity was detected after transmission through the SIM/UIM interface. | Interrupt. Bit `TX_ERROR` of `UART_DM_ISR` register. |
| Data-write | Info | AHB master executed a write transfer to the Tx FIFO while it was full. | Interrupt. Bit `TX_WR_ERROR_IRQ` of `UART_DM_ISR` register. |


### 6.2.4.12.2 UART error handling

Table 6-68 lists the UART error handlers.

#### Table 6-68 UART error handling

| Error | Internal effect | SW reaction (recovery) | How to avoid? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Rx channel** | | | |
| Parity / Framing | Character will be removed, if bit `RX_ERROR_CHAR_OFF` of `UART_DM_MR2` register is set.<br><br>Bit `PAR_FRAME_ERR` of `UART_DM_SR` register is set.<br><br>In single character packing mode, the matching bit associated with this character will be high. | Expect a missing character, if it was removed.<br><br>Clear by executing reset par frame err interrupt channel command. | |
| Break | A single 0x00 character will be removed, if bit `RX_BREAK_ZERO_CHAR_OFF` of `UART_DM_MR2` register is set.<br><br>Bits `RX_BREAK` and `RX_BREAK_START_LAST` of `UART_DM_SR` register are set. | Expect invalid data surrounding the break event.<br><br>Clear by executing Reset break change interrupt, Reset error status, Reset break start interrupt, Reset break end interrupt channel commands via the `UART_DM_CR` register. | |
| Data-read | None except the interrupt assertion. | Read again after confirming data exists.<br><br>Clear by executing Clear `RX_RD_ERROR_IRQ` channel command via the `UART_DM_CR` register. | Use the described control procedure according to work mode in Section 6.2.4.7. |
| Overrun | The last received character is lost. | Expect a missing characters.<br><br>Clear by executing reset error status channel command via the `UART_DM_CR` register. | Servicing UART should be more frequent. Change FIFOs division to deepen Rx FIFO.<br><br>Use serial interface flow control (rfr_n). |
<!-- page 1802 -->

| Error | Internal effect | SW reaction (recovery) | How to avoid? |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Tx channel** | | | |
| Parity | None except the interrupt assertion. | Data might be required to be re-transmitted.<br><br>Clear by executing reset Tx error channel command via the `UART_DM_CR` register. | |
| Data-write | Word does not enter the Tx FIFO. | Data must be re-written after confirming.<br><br>Clear by executing clear `RX_RD_ERROR_IRQ` channel command via the `UART_DM_CR` register. | Use the described control procedure according to work mode in Section 6.2.4.7. <br><br>Check `TXRDY` bit of `UART_DM_SR` register before reading. |

### 6.2.5.3 UART register definitions

#### 6.2.5.3.1 0x0000 0000 UART_DM_MR1

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK`
* **Reset state:** `0x00000000`

The `UART_DM_MR1` register is the UART mode register #1. It is used, along with `UART_DM_MR2`, to configure the operational mode of the UART.

##### UART_DM_MR1 fields

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:8 | `AUTO_RFR_LEVEL1` | These bits are used, along with field `AUTO_RFR_LEVEL0` to program the level in the receive FIFO at which the ready-for-receive signal (`RFR_N`) toggles, if programmed to do so (see `RX_RDY_CTL` field of this register).<br><br>When Rx-FIFO level is greater than the value in fields `AUTO_RFR_LEVEL1` and `AUTO_RFR_LEVEL0`, signal indicates not-ready (`RFR_N` high). Otherwise signal indicates Ready `RFR_N` low.<br><br>Configured value must be higher/equal to `RFWR` value, otherwise the watermark is never reached.<br><br>Value of this register is in words and can be programmed from 1 to $2^{\text{RAM\_ADDR\_WIDTH}}$.<br><br>Only RAM_ADDR_WIDTH + 1:8 bits of this field are generated. |
| 7 | `RX_RDY_CTL` | Setting (1) this bit enables the automatic ready-for-receiving (`RFR_N`) control for the receiver. `RFR_N` is turned off, or set (1), when a valid start bit is received and the Rx channel FIFO is at the level programmed in bits [31:8,5:0] of this register. When the FIFO level falls back to the programmed level, the `RFR_N` signal is turned on, or clear (0). When this feature is off, the `RFR_N` signal can be used by normal signal port bit manipulation (see `UART_DM_CR` register). |
<!-- page 1806 -->

##### UART_DM_MR1 fields (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 6 | `CTS_CTL` | When this bit is set(1), the transmitter checks the `CTS_N` input to determine whether to begin transmission of a new character. If `CTS_N` is low, the character is sent. Otherwise the transmitter continues marking until `CTS_N` goes low, then the next character is transmitted. A change on `CTS_N` during the transmission of a character has no effect on that character.<br><br>When this bit is cleared (0), the `CTS_N` input for the channel has no effect on the transmitter. |
| 5:0 | `AUTO_RFR_LEVEL0` | See the description of field `AUTO_RFR_LEVEL1`. |


#### 6.2.5.3.2 0x0000 0004 UART_DM_MR2

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK`
* **Reset state:** `0x00000000`

See description of `UART_DM_MR1` register.

##### UART_DM_MR2 fields

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 10 | `RFR_CTS_LOOPBACK` | Enables internal loopback between `RFR_N` of Rx channel and `CTS_N` of Tx channel if set. For this feature to be enabled, data loopback must also be enabled (`LOOPBACK` bit of this register). |
| 9 | `RX_ERROR_CHAR_OFF` | When this bit is set, characters received with parity or framing errors get discarded and not moved to the Rx channel. Otherwise they enter Rx channel as any valid character. |
| 8 | `RX_BREAK_ZERO_CHAR_OFF` | When this bit is set, the zero character received at rx_break event get discarded and not moved to the Rx channel. Otherwise it enters Rx channel as any valid character. |
| 7 | `LOOPBACK` | When set, the data output of transmitter is fed back to the data input of the receiver, that is, Tx pad is connected to the Rx pad. Might be used with flow-control loopback (`RFR_CTS_LOOPBACK` bit above). |
| 6 | `ERROR_MODE` | This bit controls the operation of the two status register bits for the Rx channel (parity or framing error and received break, see `UART_DM_SR` register).<br><br>* When clear (0), the UART operates in character mode and the status bits apply only to the last character received.<br><br>* When set (1), the UART operates in block mode and both bits are sticky, that is, they go high once an error/break-event is detected and go low only after reset error status command is issued (see `UART_DM_CR` register). |
| 5:4 | `BITS_PER_CHAR` | These bits determine how many data bits are transmitted or received per character, not including the start, stop, and parity bits.<br><br>* `0x0`: `ENUM_5_BITS` (5 bits)<br>* `0x1`: `ENUM_6_BITS` (6 bits)<br>* `0x2`: `ENUM_7_BITS` (7 bits)<br>* `0x3`: `ENUM_8_BITS` (8 bits) |
<!-- page 1807 -->

##### UART_DM_MR2 fields (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3:2 | `STOP_BIT_LEN` | This field programs the duration of the stop bit that is appended to each transmitted character. The stop bit duration can be 9/16, 1, 1+ 9/16, and 2 bit times. The receiver only samples the stop bit once, regardless of the programmed stop bit length. This configuration only applies to UART/IrDA interfaces, for SIM interface see `SIM_STOP_BIT_LEN` field of `UART_DM_SIM_CFG` register.<br><br>* `0x0`: `ENUM_0_563` (0.563 (9/16) bit times)<br>* `0x1`: `ENUM_1_000_BIT_TIME` (1.000 bit time)<br>* `0x2`: `ENUM_1_563` (1.563 (1+9/16) bit times)<br>* `0x3`: `ENUM_2_000_BIT_TIMES` (2.000 bit times) |
| 1:0 | `PARITY_MODE` | These bits determine the parity mode that is used. The user can select between odd, even, space, or no parity.<br><br>* `0x0`: `NO_PARITY` (no parity - last data-bit is followed by a stop-bit)<br>* `0x1`: `ODD_PARITY` (odd parity: parity-bit ensures number of ones in data-bits + parity-bit is odd)<br>* `0x2`: `EVEN_PARITY` (even parity: parity-bit ensures number of ones in data-bits + parity-bit is even)<br>* `0x3`: `SPACE_PARITY` (space parity: parity is always 0) |

#### 6.2.5.3.6 0x0000 0018 UART_DM_IPR

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK`
* **Reset state:** `0xFFFFFF9F`

The `UART_DM_IPR` register is the UART interrupt programming register.

##### UART_DM_IPR fields

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:7 | `STALE_TIMEOUT_MSB` | The stale character time-out duration field contains a number from 1 to $2^{30} - 1$. This number determines the character times that must elapse before a stale event is generated. This character time is defined as 10 times the bit rate. It is reset whenever a data bit is received. Never set this fields to 0 while Rx channel is operational. Do not reconfigure while an Rx transfer is active.<br><br>Note the discontinuity in the bit assignments. |
| 6 | `SAMPLE_DATA` | Currently not in use.<br><br>Setting (1) to this bit enables the sample data mode. In this mode, start bit is sampled along with the data of the UART character.<br><br>Works only in packet mode (See the CR register, `CHANNEL_COMMAND` bit for more information). |
| 5 | _Reserved_ | |
| 4:0 | `STALE_TIMEOUT_LSB` | This bit field is the LSbits of the `STALE_TIMEOUT` bit field. |


#### 6.2.5.3.7 0x0000 001C UART_DM_TFWR

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK`
* **Reset state:** `0x00000000`

The `UART_DM_TFWR` register is the UART transmit FIFO watermark register.
<!-- page 1809 -->

##### UART_DM_TFWR fields (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | `TFW` | These bits contain a number, between 0 and $2^{\text{RAM\_ADDR\_WIDTH}} - 1$ that determines the level of the transmit (Tx) FIFO at which `space_avail_req` signal is asserted in BAM mode or Tx LEV interrupt is asserted in non-BAM mode. The signal/interrupt is asserted when the FIFO level (number of Tx words in the FIFO) is less than or equal to the value in `TFWR`. Notice that the value is in words. See `UART_DM_ISR` register for `TXLEV` interrupt description.<br><br>Only RAM_ADDR_WIDTH -1:0 bits are generated. |


#### 6.2.5.3.8 0x0000 0020 UART_DM_RFWR

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK`
* **Reset state:** Undefined

The `UART_DM_RFWR` register is the UART receive FIFO watermark register.

##### UART_DM_RFWR fields

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | `RFW` | These bits contain a number, between 0 and $2^{\text{RAM\_ADDR\_WIDTH}} - 1$, that determines the level of the receive (Rx) FIFO at which `data_avail_req` signal is asserted in BAM mode or `RXLEV` interrupt is asserted in non-BAM mode. The signal/interrupt is asserted when the FIFO level (number of words in the Rx FIFO) is greater than the value in `RFWR`. Configured value should be lower/equal than `AUTO_RFR_LEVEL` value, otherwise the watermark will never be reached. Notice that the value is in words. See `UART_DM_ISR` register for `TXLEV` interrupt description.<br><br>Only RAM_ADDR_WIDTH -1:0 bits are generated. |

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK`
* **Reset state:** `0x00000000`

| 31:8 | _Reserved_ | |

#### 6.2.5.3.10 0x0000 0034 UART_DM_DMRX

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK`
* **Reset state:** `0x00000000`

Initializes Rx transfer and configures maximal length in bytes of the transfer.

##### UART_DM_DMRX fields

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:25 | _Reserved_ | |
| 24:0 | `RX_DM_CRCI_CHARS` | A write to `RX_DM_CRCI_CHARS` initializes Rx transfer in SW (FIFO) mode, with written value configuring the maximal length in bytes of the transfer. In BAM-mode, only the value held in this register impacts the data-flow and not the write-event. A write-value of 0 is not valid.<br><br>Read of `UART_DM_DMRX` register returns the number of characters that were received since the end of the last Rx transfer. To read back the last value written to this register use `UART_DM_DMRX_DBG` register.<br><br>See `UART_DM_BCR` register description for additional constraints on the value to be written to this register. |

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** `GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK`
* **Reset state:** `0x00000000`

The `UART_DM_DMEN` register defines the DMA used by the controller and the data packing mode for Tx and Rx channels.


<!-- page 1811 -->

### UART_DM_DMEN (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 5 | RX_SC_ENABLE | <ul><li>Set (1) for work in single character mode for Rx channel (every character received is zero-padded into a word).</li><li>Clearing this bit requires resetting the receiver.</li></ul> |
| 4 | TX_SC_ENABLE | <ul><li>Set (1) for work in single character mode for Tx channel (Only LSB byte of each word gets transmitted).</li><li>Clearing this bit requires resetting the transmitter.</li></ul> |
| 3 | RX_BAM_ENABLE | <ul><li>Set (1) this bit to enable Rx BAM interface (BAM-mode).</li><li>Clear (0) this bit to disable Rx BAM interface (SW/FIFO mode). Clearing this bit requires resetting the receiver (see UART_DM_CR register).</li></ul> |
| 2 | TX_BAM_ENABLE | <ul><li>Set (1) this bit to enable Tx BAM interface (BAM-mode).</li><li>Clear (0) this bit to disable Tx BAM interface (SW/FIFO mode). Clearing this bit requires resetting the transmitter (see UART_DM_CR register).</li></ul> |
| 1 | RESERVED_1 | |
| 0 | RESERVED_2 | |

#### 6.2.5.3.13 0x0000 0040 UART_DM_NO_CHARS_FOR_TX

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

Initialization of Tx transfer in SW/FIFO mode.

##### UART_DM_NO_CHARS_FOR_TX

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:0 | TX_TOTAL_TRANS_LEN | The total number of characters for transmission. Before writing a new value, the Tx FIFO must be empty as indicated by TX_READY interrupt (see UART_DM_ISR register for description) or after a TX-channel reset. It is used by the Tx channel in SW/FIFO mode to calculate the number of characters that must be transmitted in the last word. Any additional writes to the Tx FIFO beyond TX_TOTAL_TRANS_LEN characters are discarded. A TX_READY interrupt is triggered after TX_TOTAL_TRANS_LEN number of characters were moved from the Tx FIFO to the unpacking buffer (not all may have been transmitted at that point though). |

#### 6.2.5.3.14 0x0000 0044 UART_DM_BADR

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

Configures FIFO division between Rx FIFO and Tx FIFO.
<!-- page 1812 -->

### UART_DM_BADR (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:2 | RX_BASE_ADDR | Rx FIFO base address. Both FIFOs use the same RAM ($2^{RAM\_ADDR\_WIDTH}$, 32-bit entries). This register controls the division of the memory between the Rx and Tx FIFOs. The division must be a multiple of 4 entries for legacy reasons, therefore bits 1:0 of this register are not used.<br>The size of the Tx FIFO equals RX_BASE_ADDR. The size of the Rx FIFO is $2^{RAM\_ADDR\_WIDTH}$ - RX_BASE_ADDR.<br><ul><li>The default is RX_BASE_ADDR = $2^{RAM\_ADDR\_WIDTH - 1}$</li><li>Only RAM_ADDR_WIDTH -1:2 bits are generated.</li></ul> |

#### 6.2.5.3.25 0x0000 0080 UART_DM_SIM_CFG

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

The UART_DM_SIM_CFG register is used to configure the SIM interface for the UART. This register is generated only when SIM_GLUE_GEN generic equals 1.
<!-- page 1816 -->

### UART_DM_SIM_CFG (continued)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | UIM_TX_MODE | When this bit is set (1), any retransmission signal from the UIM card is ignored (the transmission portion of the SIM interface operates in block mode T=1).<br>When clear (0), retransmission is executed upon request (the transmission portion of the SIM interface operates in asynchronous transfer mode T=0).<br>Note: The operation of this function is conditional upon SIM_SEL field being set (1) to designate the UIM_IF mode of operation. |
| 16 | UIM_RX_MODE | When this bit is set (1), error-signal indication is not generated by the receiver (the receive portion of the SIM interface operates in block mode T=1).<br>When clear (0), error signal is generated when a character error is detected (the receive portion of the SIM interface operates in asynchronous transfer mode T=0).<br>Note: The operation of this function is conditional upon SIM_SEL field being set (1) to designate the UIM_IF mode of operation. |
| 15:8 | SIM_STOP_BIT_LEN | In UIM_IF mode, this field programs the duration of the stop bit that is appended to each transmitted character. The stop bit duration can be 1 to 254 bit times. The receiver only samples the stop bit once, regardless of the programmed stop bit length.<br>0x1: ENUM_1_BIT_TIMES (1 bit times)<br>0x2: ENUM_2_BIT_TIMES (2 bit times)<br>11 111110: (254 bit times) |
| 7 | SIM_CLK_ON | When this bit is set(1), the UIM_CLK is turned on at either the TD8 or TD4 frequency, as indicated by bit6 (UIM_CLK_TD8_SEL).<br>When this bit is cleared, the UIM_CLK is stopped either LOW or HIGH, as indicated by bit 5 (UIM_CLK_STOP_HIGH). |
| 6 | SIM_CLK_TD8_SEL | This bit selects the UIM_CLK frequency at which the UIM_CLK is turned on.<br>0x1: TD8 (UIM_CLK runs at the TD8 frequency (same frequency as SIM-SRC_CLK))<br>0x0: TD4 (UIM_CLK runs at the TD4 frequency (1/2 the frequency of SIM-SRC_CLK)) |
| 5 | SIM_CLK_STOP_HIGH | This bit indicates at what point - high or low - the UIM_CLK stops.<br>0x1: HIGH (high)<br>0x0: LOW (low) |
| 4 | RESERVED | |
| 3 | MASK_RX | Setting (1) this bit masks off any 0 on the Rx line, which prevents the receiver from seeing the START bit. Set (1) this bit if you do not want to receive the data you transmit. |
| 2 | SWAP_D | Setting (1) this bit causes the UIM_IF to swap the 8 data bits (making MSB into LSB, bit 6 into bit 1, and so on) before it is read by the microprocessor. |
| 1 | INV_D | Set (1) this bit to cause the UIM_IF to invert the 8 data bit before it is read by the microprocessor. |
| 0 | SIM_SEL | When set (1), UART operates in SIM/UIM interface mode. When cleared (0), SIM/UIM interface is disabled. |
<!-- page 1817 -->

#### 6.2.5.3.26 0x0000 00A0 UART_DM_CSR

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

The UART_DM_CSR register is the UART clock selection register. This register is used to determine the bit rate for the transmitter and receiver. The transmitter and receiver can be clocked at different rates.

Data rate of receiver/transmitter is UART-CLK frequency divided by the integer matching the configured value below:
* 0xF = 16
* 0xE = 32
* 0xD = 48
* 0xC = 64
* 0xB = 96
* 0xA = 128
* 0x9 = 192
* 0x8 = 256
* 0x7 = 384
* 0x6 = 512
* 0x5 = 768
* 0x4 = 1536
* 0x3 = 3072
* 0x2 = 6144
* 0x1 = 12288
* 0x0 = 24576

#### 6.2.5.3.27 0x0000 00A4 UART_DM_SR

* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** Undefined
<!-- page 1818 -->

### UART_DM_SR (continued)

The UART_DM_SR register is the UART status register. This register is used to obtain the current state of the UART subsystem. This register is updated asynchronously.

##### UART_DM_SR

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11:10 | TRANS_END_TRIGGER | RX-transfer-end event type. Stores trigger for last transfer end: 00 for no trigger, 01 for DMRX-event, 10 for timeout stale, 11 for SW stale. |
| 9 | TRANS_ACTIVE | Transfer active bit |
| 8 | RX_BREAK_START_LAST | When break start is detected, this bit is set (1). When break end is detected, this bit is reset (0). |
| 7 | HUNT_CHAR | When set (1), this bit indicates that the programmed character in the UART_DM_HCR register was received. If programmed, this condition causes the RXHUNT bit to be set (1) in the UART_DM_ISR register. This bit is cleared by issuing a reset error status command. |
| 6 | RX_BREAK | When set (1), this bit indicates that an all-zero character of the programmed length was received without a stop bit. If a break begins in the middle of a character, it is detected if the condition remains until the end of the next character time. Only one all zero character is written into the FIFO upon receiving the break. After the Rx input returns high for at least half a bit time, then more characters are accepted by the receiver. Whenever the break condition starts or stops as defined above, the RXBREAK bit is set (1) in the UART_DM_ISR register. This bit is appended to the character in the receive FIFO. |
| 5 | PAR_FRAME_ERR | A parity error occurs if parity is programmed to be checked and an incoming character is received with incorrect parity. A framing error occurs when the Rx input is low while the stop bit is being sampled. This bit is sampled in the middle of the first stop bit position, regardless of the programmed length of the stop bit. This error bit is appended to the character in the receive FIFO. |
| 4 | UART_OVERRUN | An overrun error occurs if one or more incoming characters are lost. This happens when the receive FIFO is full, the packing buffer is full and another character has been received in the shift register. The character in the receive shift register is lost. Upon overrun, this status bit remains high until cleared by a reset error status command. |
| 3 | TXEMT | This bit is set (1) when the transmitter under-runs. It is set after the transmission of the stop bit at the end of a character, if there are no characters waiting to be sent. It is reset when a character is written to the transmit FIFO. |
| 2 | TXRDY | This bit indicates that the transmit FIFO has space in it. It is reset when the FIFO becomes full and set when space becomes available again. Any characters that are written to the FIFO while this bit is low is lost. |
| 1 | RXFULL | This bit is set (1) when the receive FIFO becomes full. It is reset when the CPU reads a word. |
| 0 | RXRDY | This bit is set (1) when there is a word in the receive FIFO waiting to be read. It is reset when the last word currently stored in the FIFO is read. |
<!-- page 1819 -->

#### 6.2.5.3.28 0x0000 00A8 UART_DM_CR

* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** Undefined

The UART_DM_SR register is the UART status register. This register is used to obtain the current state of the UART subsystem. This register is updated asynchronously.

> [!CAUTION]
> Do not reset the transmitter or receiver and disable it at the same time.

Channel commands:
* **0x00** Null command: Does nothing.
* **0x01** Reset receiver: Resets the receiver as if a hardware reset were issued. The receiver is disabled and the FIFO, packing buffer, and shift registers are flushed.
* **0x02** Reset transmitter: Resets the transmitter as if a hardware reset were issued. The transmitter signal goes high (marking) and the FIFO, unpacking register, and shift registers are flushed.
* **0x03** Reset error status: Clears the overrun error and hunt char received status bits in both the character and block error modes. In the block error mode, it clears the error status and received break.
* **0x04** Reset break change interrupt: Clears the break change interrupt status bit.
* **0x05** Start break: Forces the transmitter signal low. The transmitter must be enabled. If the transmitter is busy, the break is started when all characters in the transmit FIFO and the transmit shift register have been completely sent.
* **0x06** Stop break: If executed while channel is breaking, this command causes the transmitter signal to go high. The signal remains high for at least one bit time before sending out a new character.
* **0x07** Reset CTS_N: Clears ISR bit 5.
* **0x08** Reset stale interrupt: Clears the stale interrupt.
* **0x09** Packet mode: Turns on the sample data mode, which causes the receiver to sample the receive data stream at 16 times the programmed baud rate. The data is sampled with the start of the start bit, or the first data bit, and continued until the marking state. To exit this state, write 1100 in the command field.
* **0x0A** test_parity_on: Internal use only.
* **0x0B** test_frame_on: Internal use only.
* **0x0C** Mode reset: Turns off the sample data mode.
* **0x0D** Set RFR: Asserts the ready for receiving signal (actual flow-control port is active-low (rfr_n) and will go low following this command).
* **0x0E** Reset RFR: Deasserts the ready for receiving signal (actual flow-control port is active-low (rfr_n) and will go high following this command).
<!-- page 1820 -->

### UART_DM_CR (continued)

* **0x0F** uart_reset_int: Internal use only
* **0x10** Reset TX_ERROR: Clears TX_ERROR
* **0x11** Clear TX_DONE: Clears the TX_DONE interrupt (ISR bit 9)
* **0x12** Reset break start interrupt: Clears the break start interrupt status bit.
* **0x13** Reset break end interrupt: Clears the break end interrupt status bit.
* **0x14** Reset par_frame_err interrupt: Clears the par_frame_err interrupt status bit.
* **0x15** Start Rx BAM IFC: Initialize producer sidebands towards BAM after reset.
* **0x16** Start Tx BAM IFC: Initialize consumer sidebands towards BAM after reset.
* **0x17** WWT counter enable: Enable WWT counter and IRQ.
* **0x18** WWT counter disable: Disable WWT counter and IRQ.
* **0x19** Clear TX_WR_ERROR IRQ: Clears Tx write error interrupt status bit.
* **0x1A** Clear RX_RD_ERROR IRQ: Clears Rx read error interrupt status bit.
* **0x1B** Clear TX_COMP IRQ: Clears Tx complete interrupt status bit.
* **0x1C** Clear WWT IRQ: Clears WWT timeout interrupt status bit.

General commands:
* **0x0** Null command: Does nothing.
* **0x1** CR protection enable: Enables CR HW protection. When two consecutive writes to the CR are detected, the second write is delayed until the command of the first write is finished. The delay is done by deasserting the AHB ready and this ensures that the first command completes and the second one is executed right afterward.
* **0x2** CR protection disable: Disables CR HW protection. SW is responsible for managing delay between writes to the CR register.
* **0x3** Reset Tx-ready interrupt: Clears the TX_READY interrupt.
* **0x4** SW force stale: Causes a stale event (even if stale events are disabled).
* **0x5** Enable stale event: Enables the stale event mechanism
* **0x6** Disable stale event: Enables the stale event mechanism
* **0x7** - RESERVED

##### UART_DM_CR Register Bits

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11 | CHANNEL_COMMAND_MSB | This is the msb of the CHANNEL_COMMAND bitfield. |
| 10:8 | GENERAL_COMMAND | Writing the appropriate value to these bits executes the commands that are listed in the register description. |
| 7:4 | CHANNEL_COMMAND_LSB | Writing the appropriate value to these bits along with bit 11, executes the channel-command as listed in the register description. |
| 3 | UART_TX_DISABLE | This command terminates the operation of the transmitter after any character in the transmit shift register is sent. |


<!-- page 1821 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | UART_TX_EN | This command enables the operation of the transmitter. |
| 1 | UART_RX_DISABLE | This command immediately terminates the operation of the channel receiver and any incoming characters are lost. None of the receiver status bits are affected by this command and characters that are already in the receive FIFO remain there. |
| 0 | UART_RX_EN | This command enables the channel receiver. |

### 6.2.5.3.29 UART_DM_MISR (0x0000 00AC)

* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 16:0 | UART_MISR | The UART_DM_MISR register is the masked interrupt status register. A read from this register returns the AND of the UART_DM_ISR and the UART_DM_IMR registers. This register is updated asynchronously. This bit field is misr <= (isr(16 DOWNTO 7) AND imr(16 DOWNTO 7)) & 0 & (isr(5 DOWNTO 0) AND imr(5 DOWNTO 0)). |

### 6.2.5.3.30 UART_DM_IMR (0x0000 00B0)

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

The UART_DM_IMR register is the UART interrupt mask register. This register is used to enable the corresponding functions in the UART_DM_ISR register. Setting (1) a bit in the UART_DM_IMR register causes an interrupt to be generated, if the corresponding bit in the UART_DM_ISR register is set. Clearing (0) a bit in the UART_DM_IMR register causes the setting of the corresponding bit in the UART_DM_ISR register to have no effect on the interrupt signal. (See UART_DM_ISR register)

Bit 6 of the UART_DM_IMR register, CURRENT_CTS, is slightly different. If the current value of the CTS is one (1), no interrupt is generated. However, the user can use bit 6 in this register to mask the CTS value when reading the UART_DM_MISR register or as a general-purpose bit.
<!-- page 1822 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | WWT_IRQ | Masking bit of the matching field interrupt bit (See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions). |
| 15 | TXCOMP_IRQ | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |
| 14 | RX_RD_ERROR_IRQ | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |
| 13 | TX_WR_ERROR_IRQ | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |
| 12 | PAR_FRAME_ERR_IRQ | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |
| 11 | RXBREAK_END | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |

| 8 | TX_ERROR | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |
| 7 | TX_READY | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |
| 6 | CURRENT_CTS | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |

| 4 | RXLEV | See UART_DM_ISR for field descriptions. |

### 6.2.5.3.31 UART_DM_ISR (0x0000 00B4)

* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** Undefined

The UART_DM_ISR register is the UART interrupt status register. This register provides the current status of the possible interrupt conditions. If one of these bits is set (1), and the corresponding bit in the UART_DM_IMR register is set (1), an interrupt is generated (with the exception of bit 6, CURRENT_CTS). If the corresponding bit in the UART_DM_IMR register is clear (0), setting one of these bits has no effect on the UART interrupt request signal. This register is updated asynchronously.
<!-- page 1823 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 16 | WWT_IRQ | WWT timeout reached interrupt. Fired after WWT timer was enabled and no data was received during the configured time that follows. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = CLEAR_WWT_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 15 | TXCOMP_IRQ | Tx complete interrupt. Fired when Tx channel finished transmitting all of Tx transfer's data and no new transfer was initiated. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = CLEAR_TX_COMP_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 14 | RX_RD_ERROR_IRQ | Rx FIFO empty read error. Fired when AHB master is trying to read from an empty Rx FIFO. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = CLEAR_RX_RD_ERROR_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 13 | TX_WR_ERROR_IRQ | Tx FIFO full write error. Fired when AHB master is trying to write into a full Tx FIFO. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = CLEAR_TX_WR_ERROR_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 12 | PAR_FRAME_ERR_IRQ | This bit is asserted in the same condition at which PAR_FRAME_ERR status bit is asserted (See UART_DM_SR register). Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = RESET_PAR_FRAME_ERR_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 11 | RXBREAK_END | This bit is set (1) if the end of a break condition is detected. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = RESET_BREAK_END_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 10 | RXBREAK_START | This bit is set (1) if the start of a break condition is detected. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = RESET_BREAK_START_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 9 | TX_DONE | This bit is used only in UIM/SIM_IF mode. Set (1) this bit when the last byte in the transmitter has been sent. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = CLEAR_TX_DONE_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). This bit is generated only when SIM_GLUE_GEN generic equals 1. |
| 8 | TX_ERROR | Only used in UIM_IF mode. Set (1) this bit to indicate that there has been parity error during transmission. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = CLEAR_TX_ERROR_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). This bit is generated only when SIM_GLUE_GEN generic equals 1. |
| 7 | TX_READY | This bit, when set(1), indicates that:<br>1. Tx FIFO is empty.<br>2. The value written in NO_CHARS_FOR_TX register equals the number of bytes written to the Tx FIFO since the register was updated.<br>Note: There may be characters in the unpack buffer or in the shift register.<br>Cleared by issuing GENERAL_COMMAND = RESET_TX_READY_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register) |
| 6 | CURRENT_CTS | This bit indicates the current state of the CTS input, high (1) meaning peer is not ready for data reception, low (0) meaning peer is ready. The toggling of this bit does not generate an interrupt. |
| 5 | DELTA_CTS | This bit, when set (1), indicates that the CTS input has changed states. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = RESET_CTS_N (UART_DM_CR register). |
<!-- page 1824 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | RXLEV | This bit is set when a word is loaded into the receive FIFO that brings the total number of words in the FIFO above the programmed watermark level in the FIFO watermark register (UART_DM_RFWR). This bit is cleared after enough words have been read to bring the level equal to or below the programmed watermark level. |
| 3 | RXSTALE | This bit indicates that an Rx transfer has finished. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = RESET_STALE_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 2 | RXBREAK_CHANGE | This bit is set (1) if the start or end of a break condition is detected. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = RESET_BREAK_CHANGE_IRQ (UART_DM_CR register). A detected break is defined as an all-zeros character with an invalid stop bit AND LOW PARITY. The end of a break is defined as a mark condition (1) at least 1/2 bit width. A detected break occupies one position in the Rx FIFO. |
| 1 | RXHUNT | This bit is set (1) when an incoming character matches the value programmed into the UART_DM_HCR register. Cleared by issuing CHANNEL_COMMAND = RESET_ERROR_STATUS (UART_DM_CR register). |
| 0 | TXLEV | This bit is set (1) when a word that is transferred from the transmit FIFO to the transmit shift register brings the total number of words in the FIFO below or equal to the programmed watermark level in the UART_DM_TFWR register. This bit is cleared (0) after enough words have been written to the FIFO to bring the level above the programmed watermark level. Since this bit does not have a Clear command, during interrupt handling this bit must be masked (using the matching bit in UART_DM_IMR) until writing additional data for transmission is required. After data is written, this interrupt-bit should be unmasked. |

### 6.2.5.3.32 UART_DM_IRDA (0x0000 00B8)

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
* **Reset state:** 0x00000000

The UART_DM_IRDA register enables the IRDA function, selects a loopback, and allows inversion of Rx and Tx data. This register also controls the IRDA transceiver that optionally interfaces between the UART and the DP_RX_DATA and DP_TX_DATA pins.

The UART proper is a standard Rx/Tx configuration that converts the serial pin input and output lines to 8-bit data for the microprocessor. The configuration contains receive and transmit blocks, a control block, a bit rate generator for Rx and Tx, and FIFO interfaces with the microprocessor data bus. The IRDA register provides the means of switching IRDA circuits into the serial I/O lines and the IRDA function is normally switched out. The IRDA modulator/demodulator may be enabled or disabled under microprocessor control. When enabled, the Rx and Tx data paths have individual inversion select bits, so external true or inverted drivers may be used in the signal path.

The register is generated only when IRDA_IFC_GEN generic equals 1.
<!-- page 1825 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 4 | MEDIUM_RATE_EN | Set (1) for 1/4 bit-time pulse length (medium rate)<br>Clear (0) for 3/16 bit-time pulse length (low rate) |
| 3 | IRDA_LOOPBACK | This bit loops the IRDA modulated Tx line back into the IRDA Rx line. The normal UART loopback mode must be off in order to see this effect. |
| 2 | INVERT_IRDA_TX | This bit inverts the polarity of the IRDA modulated signal on the DP_TX_DATA pin.<br>Set (1) this bit for an inverted polarity.<br>Clear (0) this bit for a non-inverted polarity. |
| 1 | INVERT_IRDA_RX | This bit inverts the polarity of the IRDA received signal on the DP_RX_DATA pin.<br>Set (1) this bit for inverted the polarity.<br>Clear (0) this bit for non-inverted polarity. |
| 0 | IRDA_EN | Set (1) this bit to enable the IRDA transceiver.<br>Clear (0) this bit to bypass the IRDA transceiver and ignore the other bits of this register. |

### 6.2.5.3.72 UART_DM_UIM_CFG (0x0000 0180)

**Type:** RW
**Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
**Reset state:** 0x00001703

Configuration register for UIM-controller (linked with this UART_DM). Reset value relevant to UIM-controller HW-reset and not a UART_DM HW-reset. Writing to this register requires waiting until UIM-WRITE is done (indication by status-bit or interrupt) before attempting an additional write/read one of UIM_CFG/UIM_CMD registers.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 15 | BATT_ALARM_QUICK_DROP_EN | When set, deactivation sequence resulted from battery-alarm will drop all UIM-lines immediately. Otherwise, lines will be dropped gradually. |
| 14 | TESTBUS_EN | When set, UIM-controller will output testbus signals on the testbus port. Otherwise, testbus port will be driven with zeros. |
| 13 | SW_RESET | When set, UIM-controller will be at reset state. |
| 12 | MODE18 | Configures PAD's working reference voltage (set to 0 for 3 V, 1 for 1.8 V). |
| 11 | RESERVED_1 | |
| 10 | PMIC_ALARM_EN | Enables messaging on the alarm-line to notify PMIC to drop card's voltage supply. Set to enable messaging, clear to disable. |
| 9 | BATT_ALARM_TRIGGER_EN | Enables triggering of deactivation sequence when battery-alarm detected. Set to enable triggering, clear to disable. |
| 8 | UIM_RMV_TRIGGER_EN | Enables triggering of deactivation sequence when card-removal detected. Set to enable triggering, clear to disable. |
| 7 | RESERVED_2 | |
| 6 | UIM_CARD_EVENTS_ENABLE | When cleared, UIM-controller will not react to any card-event (insertion/removal). When set, UIM-controller reacts to these events and considered active. This bit should be set only after/during UIM_PRESENT_POLARITY bit is configured so UIM-controller will not interpret card-events incorrectly due to a wrong polarity configuration (the reset-value of the polarity might not match the actual one). |
| 5 | UIM_PRESENT_POLARITY | Determines value interpretation of uim_present signal. Setting this bit to 1 indicates that a uim-card present in the uim-slot will return the value 1 on uim_present line & 0 when a card is not present. Setting this bit to 0 indicates that a uim-card present in the uim-slot will return the value 0 on uim_present line & 1 when a card is not present. |
| 4:0 | EVENT_DEBOUNCE_TIME | Configures debounce-time of card-removal/insertion events (in sleep-clk cycles). |
<!-- page 1839 -->

### 6.2.5.3.73 UART_DM_UIM_CMD (0x0000 0184)

**Type:** W
**Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
**Reset state:** Undefined

Command register for UIM-controller (linked with this UART_DM). Writing to this register requires waiting until UIM-WRITE is done (indication by status-bit or interrupt) before attempting an additional write/read one of UIM_CFG/UIM_CMD registers.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | RECOVER_FROM_HW_DEACTIVATION | Writing 1 to this bit will cause the UIM-io-ctrl to exit override state and reflect UIM signals from UART_DM to the UIM card. Setting both bits of this register to 1 will cause neither of the commands to be executed. |
| 0 | INITIATE_HW_DEACTIVATION | Initiates a hardware deactivation sequence when writing 1 to this bit. This executes the sequence on the uim_data, uim_clk & uim_rst_n lines and alerts the PMIC to cut the power-supply to the card afterwards. Setting both bits of this register to 1 will cause neither of the commands to be executed. |

### 6.2.5.3.74 UART_DM_UIM_IO_STATUS (0x0000 0188)

**Type:** R
**Clock:** GCC_APSS_AHB_CLK
**Reset state:** 0x00000002

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 2 | UIM_IO_WRITE_IN_PROGRESS | Asserted after UIM-write (UIM_CFG/UIM_CMD register write) while write is being propagated into the UIM-IO-controller. An additional read/write to UIM_CFG/UIM_CMD register should be done while high. Deasserted when write finishes propagating. |
| 1 | UIM_DEACTIVATION_STATUS | Indicates whether a hardware deactivation sequence was performed and sequence recovery hasn't been executed yet. This bit is set when the sequence is initiated either by a hardware trigger (batt_alarm, card-removal) or a software trigger ('initiate_shutdown_sequence' bit in CMD register). Cleared after executing a 'recover_from_hw_deactivation' command. |
| 0 | CARD_PRESENCE | Indication on card presence in slot. High when card present, low otherwise. |
<!-- page 1840 -->
