### 6.5.4.10 Infinite mode write and read data sequences

The infinite mode write and read data sequences can be used for application-specific use cases like a permanent chip-to-chip connection, when a logical pipe is established between two chips. The infinite mode allows transferring unlimited amount of data. The SDCC flow control is activated every time when the logical pipe is idle and no data is transferred.

> [!NOTE]
> This mode of operation is not expected to be used for normal data transfers (writes and reads) to SD card and MMC, and standard eMMC and SDIO device.

#### 6.5.4.10.1 Infinite mode write data sequence

1. Set `SDCC_MCI_CLK[FLOW_ENA]` bit to `0x1`.
2. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CDR_EN]` bit in case automatic tracking is enabled.
3. Write the data transaction time limit into `SDCC_MCI_DATA_TIMER` register.
    a. The value is 250 ms multiplied by the actual frequency of MCLK.
4. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_LENGTH` register.
5. Send write data command to the card/device to start a write data transaction. The possible commands are:
    a. SD commands: `CMD25`
    b. eMMC commands: `CMD25`
    c. SDIO commands: `CMD53`, `CMD54` (QCT-specific command)
6. Check that a valid response was received.
7. Set appropriate bit fields and write to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` register:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[ENABLE]` bit to `0x1`.
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DIRECTION]` bit to `0x0`.
    c. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[MODE]` bit to `0x0`.
    d. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DM_ENABLE]` bit to `0x0`.
    e. Write the block size used in data transaction into `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[BLOCKSIZE]` bit field.
    f. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DATA_PEND]` bit to `0x0`.
    g. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[INFINITE_TRANSFER]` bit to `0x1`.
    h. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[AUTO_PROG_DONE]` bit to `0x0`.
8. Execute step 8a through 8d until data is written into the FIFO or until one of the following error events is detected:
    a. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_CRC_FAIL]` bit is set to `0x1`, then the card/device detects a CRC error during the data transfer.
<!-- page 2056 -->

    b. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_TIMEOUT]` bit is set to `0x1`, then the card/device did not complete programming of the transmitted data within the time period specified in `SDCC_MCI_DATA_TIMER` register.
    c. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[TX_UNDERRUN]` bit is set to `0x1`, then the SDCC tried to send data to the card when no data was available for transmission. This bit is never expected to be set if `SDCC_MCI_CLK[FLOW_ENA]` bit is set to `0x1`.
    d. Write the data into the SDCC FIFO:
        i. Write 1 word to FIFO address if `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[TXFIFO_FULL]` bit is `0x0`.
        ii. Write 8 words to FIFO address if `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[TXFIFO_EMPTY]` or `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[TXFIFO_HALF_FULL]` bit is `0x1`.
9. To terminate infinite mode write data transaction, write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[ENABLE]` bit without modifying other bits of `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` register.
10. Send `CMD12` to the card/device.
11. Wait until `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[PROG_DONE]` bit is set to `0x1`. This can be done using polling or interrupt.
12. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` to reset DPSM.

#### 6.5.4.10.2 Infinite mode read data sequence

1. Set `SDCC_MCI_CLK[FLOW_ENA]` bit to `0x1`.
2. Write the data transaction time limit into `SDCC_MCI_DATA_TIMER` register.
    a. The value is 100 ms multiplied by the actual frequency of MCLK.
3. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_LENGTH` register.
4. Set appropriate bit fields and write to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` register:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[ENABLE]` bit to `0x1`.
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DIRECTION]` bit to `0x1`.
    c. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[MODE]` bit to `0x0`.
    d. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DM_ENABLE]` bit to `0x0`.
    e. Write the block size used in data transaction into `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[BLOCKSIZE]` bit field.
    f. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DATA_PEND]` bit to `0x0`.
    g. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[INFINITE_TRANSFER]` bit to `0x1`.
    h. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[AUTO_PROG_DONE]` bit to `0x0`.
5. Send read data command to the card/device to start a read data transaction. The possible commands are:
    a. SD commands: `CMD18`
    b. eMMC commands: `CMD18`
    c. SDIO commands: `CMD53`, `CMD54` (QCT-specific command)
<!-- page 2057 -->

6. Check that a valid response was received.
7. Execute step 7a through 7d until the infinite mode read data transaction is terminated or one of the following error events is detected:
    a. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_CRC_FAIL]` bit is set to `0x1`, then a CRC error was detected on received data.
    b. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_TIMEOUT]` bit is set to `0x1`, then the card/device did not start sending a new block of data within the time period specified in `SDCC_MCI_DATA_TIMER` register.
    c. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RX_OVERRUN]` bit is set to `0x1`, then the data was received and written into the FIFO when it was full. This bit is never expected to be set if `SDCC_MCI_CLK[FLOW_ENA]` bit is set to `0x1`.
    d. Read the data from the SDCC FIFO:
        i. Read 1 word from FIFO address if `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXFIFO_EMPTY]` bit is `0x0` or if `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXDATA_AVLBL]` bit is `0x1`.
        ii. Read 8 words from FIFO address if `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXFIFO_FULL]` or `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXFIFO_HALF_FULL]` bit is `0x1`.
8. To terminate infinite mode read data transaction, write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[ENABLE]` bit without modifying other bits of `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` register.
9. Send `CMD12` to the card/device.
10. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` to reset DPSM.

### 6.5.4.11 eMMC boot sequence

1. Send `CMD0` with the argument `0xF0F0F0F0`.
2. Write boot acknowledge time limit to `SDCC_MCI_BOOT_ACK_TIMER` register.
    a. The value is 50 ms multiplied by the actual frequency of MCLK.
3. Write boot time limit into `SDCC_MCI_CCS_TIMER` register.
    a. The value is 1 second multiplied by the actual frequency of MCLK.
4. Program `SDCC_MCI_CLK` register according to the contents of eMMC `EXT_CSD` register (SDR or DDR mode, SD data bus width).
5. Set `SDCC_MCI_CLK[FLOW_ENA]` bit to `0x1`.
6. Write the data transaction time limit into `SDCC_MCI_DATA_TIMER` register.
    a. The value is 100 ms multiplied by the actual frequency of MCLK.
7. Write the total length of boot transaction in bytes into `SDCC_MCI_DATA_LENGTH` register. The value of `SDCC_MCI_DATA_LENGTH` register is an integer multiple of the value in `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[BLOCKSIZE]` bit field.
8. Set appropriate bit fields and write to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` register:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[ENABLE]` bit to `0x1`.
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DIRECTION]` bit to `0x1`.
<!-- page 2058 -->

    c. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[MODE]` bit to `0x0`.
    d. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DM_ENABLE]` bit to `0x0` (FIFO mode is used).
    e. Write the block size used in boot transaction into `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[BLOCKSIZE]` bit field.
    f. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[DATA_PEND]` bit to `0x0`.
    g. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[INFINITE_TRANSFER]` bit to `0x0`.
    h. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[AUTO_PROG_DONE]` bit to `0x0`.
    i. Set `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL[RX_DATA_PEND]` bit to `0x1`.
9. Set appropriate bit fields and write to `SDCC_MCI_BOOT` register:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_BOOT[BOOT_MODE]` bit to `0x1` if normal boot mode is used.
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_BOOT[BOOT_MODE]` bit to `0x0` if alternative boot mode is used.
    c. Set `SDCC_MCI_BOOT[BOOT_ACK_EN]` bit to `0x1` to wait for boot acknowledge pattern from the eMMC device. The device sends a boot acknowledge pattern if bit 6 of byte 179 of `EXT_CSD` register is `0x1`.
    d. Set `SDCC_MCI_BOOT[BOOT_EN]` bit to `0x1`.
10. If alternative boot mode is used, then send `CMD0` with the argument `0xFFFFFFFA`. Check that a valid response was received.
11. Execute step 11a through 11f until all data is received and read from the FIFO or one of the following error events is detected:
    a. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_CRC_FAIL]` bit is set to `0x1`, then a CRC error was detected on received boot data.
    b. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_TIMEOUT]` bit is set to `0x1`, then the card/device did not start sending a new block of boot data within the time period specified in `SDCC_MCI_DATA_TIMER` register.
    c. If the `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RX_OVERRUN]` bit is set to `0x1`, then the data was received and written into the FIFO when it was full. This bit is never expected to be set if `SDCC_MCI_CLK[FLOW_ENA]` bit is set to `0x1`.
    d. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[BOOT_ACK_ERR]` bit is set to `0x1`, then boot acknowledge response from the device was not detected or a wrong pattern was detected.
    e. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[BOOT_TIMEOUT]` bit is set to `0x1`, then the device did not start sending boot data within the time period specified in `SDCC_MCI_CCS_TIMER` register.
    f. Read the data from the SDCC FIFO:
        i. Read 1 word from FIFO address if `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXFIFO_EMPTY]` bit is `0x0` or if `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXDATA_AVLBL]` bit is `0x1`.
        ii. Read 8 words from FIFO address if `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXFIFO_FULL]` or `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXFIFO_HALF_FULL]` bit is `0x1`.
12. Wait until `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATAEND]` bit is set to `0x1`. This can be done using polling or interrupt.
13. Wait until `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[RXACTIVE]` bit is `0x0`.
<!-- page 2059 -->

14. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_BOOT` register.
15. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` register.

### 6.5.4.12 UHS-I voltage switch sequence

Figure 6-82 presents UHS-I voltage switch sequence.

#### Figure 6-82: UHS-I voltage switch sequence
*Description:* A command and response flow diagram showing the initialization and voltage switch sequence.
- **Repeat ACMD41:**
  - Send `CMD55`, receive response `R1`.
  - Send `CMD41` (with Bit 30: HCS = 1, Bit 24: S18R = 1), receive response `R3` (showing Bit 31: busy, Bit 30: CCS invalid, Bit 24: S18A invalid).
- **The last ACMD41:**
  - Send `CMD55`, receive response `R1`.
  - Send `CMD41`, receive response `R3` (showing Bit 31: ready, Bit 30: CCS = 1, Bit 24: S18A = 1).
- **Voltage Switch:**
  - Send `CMD11`, receive response `R1`.
  - Perform the physical voltage switch.
- **Card identification:**
  - Send `CMD2`, receive response `R2`.

1. Follow SD card initialization sequence as defined in *SD Specifications, Part 1: Physical Layer Simplified Specification, Section: Bus Signal Voltage Switch Sequence*.
    a. Send ACMD41 (`CMD55` + `CMD41`) with bit 30 and bit 24 set to `0x1` for `CMD41` in `SDCC_MCI_ARGUMENT` register until bit 31 in `SDCC_MCI_RESP0` register is `0x1`, which means the card accepted voltage range and completed internal initialization process.
    b. If bit 24 of `SDCC_MCI_RESP0` register is set to `0x1`, then it means that S18A bit of card response is `0x1` – the card is ready to start voltage switch sequence.
2. Send `CMD11` with argument of `0x0`.
3. Switch VDDPX_SDCn (n = 1 to 2) from 3 V to 1.8 V to change the VDD of the SD I/O pads.
4. Write `0x1` to `SDCC_MCI_CLK[IO_PAD_PWR_SWITCH]` bit.
5. Write `0x1` to `SDCC_MCI_CLK[PWRSAVE]` bit to stop SD clock output.
6. Wait 5 ms for the voltage regulator in the card to become stable.
7. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_CLK[PWRSAVE]` bit to enable SD clock output.

#### 6.5.4.12.1 SDCDC calibration

The programmable delay line (SDCDC) is required for supporting of UHS-I cards in SDR104 timing mode (see *SD Specifications, Part 1: Physical Layer Simplified Specification, Section: Tuning Command*).

#### 6.5.4.12.2 SDCDC initialization

1. Set `SDCC_MCI_CLK[PWRSAVE]` bit to `0x0` during reset.
2. Write `0x1` to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[DLL_RST]` bit.
3. Write `0x1` to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[PDN]` bit.
<!-- page 2060 -->

4. Write `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[MCLK_FREQ]` bit field with appropriate frequency.
5. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[DLL_RST]` bit.
6. Write `0x0` to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[PDN]` bit.
7. Write `0x1` to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[DLL_EN]` bit.
8. Write `0x1` to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit.
9. Wait until `SDCC_MCI_DLL_STATUS[DLL_LOCK]` bit is `0x1`.
10. If `SDCC_MCI_CLK[PWRSAVE]` bit is needed, it can be set to `0x1`.

#### 6.5.4.12.3 SDCDC low-power mode

To put the SDCDC in the lowest power consumption mode:
- Write `0x1` to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[PDN]` bit.

#### 6.5.4.12.4 SDCDC configuration

1. Set appropriate bit fields and write to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG` register:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CDR_EN]` bit to `0x0`.
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CDR_EXT_EN]` bit to `0x1`.
    c. Program the MCLK value to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[MCLK_FREQ]` bit field.
    d. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit to `0x0`.
    e. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[DLL_EN]` bit to `0x1`.
2. Wait until `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit is `0x0`.
3. Write the selected DLL clock output phase (0 – 15) to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CDR_SELEXT]` bit.
4. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit to `0x1`.
5. Wait until `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit is `0x1`.
6. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CDR_EN]` bit to `0x1` and to enable CDR mode (needed for read data transactions).


<!-- page 2061 -->
##### 6.5.4.12.5 Tuning sequence

Figure 6-83 presents UHS-I initialization sequence.

#### Figure 6-83: UHS-I initialization sequence

*Description:* A flowchart detailing the UHS-I initialization and tuning sequence. The flowchart is divided into two columns:

1.  **Voltage Switch Sequence (Left Column):**
    *   Starts with **CMD0**, followed by **CMD8**.
    *   Sends **ACMD41** with parameters `HCS = 1` and `S18R = 1`.
    *   **Check busy**: Checks the busy status (D31).
        *   If `D31 = 0` (busy), loops back to check busy.
        *   If `D31 = 1` (completed), proceeds to **Check CCS**.
    *   **Check S18R**:
        *   If `S18A = 0` (no switch), branches to **CMD2** in the right column.
        *   If `S18A = 1` (switch), sends **CMD11**.
    *   **Check Response** for CMD11:
        *   If **No response**, triggers **Error?** check.
            *   If **Yes** (error), leads to **Power cycle**.
        *   If **Get response**, proceeds to **Voltage switch sequence**.
    *   **Voltage switch sequence** is performed, followed by **Switch to SDR12 timing**.
    *   **Error?** check:
        *   If **Yes** (Switch error), leads to **Power cycle**.
        *   If **No**, branches to **CMD2** in the right column.

2.  **Card Initialization & Tuning (Right Column):**
    *   Starts with **CMD2**, followed by **CMD3**, then **CMD7**.
    *   Sends **ACMD6** to configure **4-bit mode**.
    *   **UHS-I card?** check:
        *   If **No**, transitions to **1.8 V Signaling / UHS-I Mode** (end of sequence).
        *   If **Yes**, sends **CMD6** for **Function group 3** (Driver strength).
    *   Sends **CMD6** for **Function group 1, 4** (Current limit).
    *   Sends **CMD19** for **Tuning**.
    *   **Tuning Complete?** check:
        *   If **Yes**, transitions to **1.8 V Signaling / UHS-I Mode** (end of sequence).
        *   If **No**, loops back to **CMD19** (Tuning) or leads to error handling (implied).

Tuning sequence (software-based calibration of SDCDC) can be done at any time after the SD3.0 UHS-I card completed voltage switch sequence and switched to UHS-I mode, and before executing read data transfers in SDR50 or SDR104 timing mode. For eMMC4.5 device tuning can be done at any time after switching to HS200 mode, and before executing read data transfers in HS200 timing mode.
<!-- page 2062 -->
Tuning sequence steps:
1. Set appropriate bit fields and write to `SDCC_MCI_CLK` register:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_CLK[PWRSAVE]` bit to `0x0` (as DLL requires clock during phase switch).
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_CLK[SELECT_IN]` bit field to `0x4` to enable asynchronous FIFO for the sampled input data.
    c. Set `SDCC_MCI_CLK[SDC4_MCLK_SEL]` bit field to `0x2` to select a free running MCLK as an input to SDCDC.
    d. Preserve all other bits of `SDCC_MCI_CLK` register unmodified.
2. Set the selected DLL clock output phase value to 0 (in `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CDR_SELEXT]` bit).
3. Configure the DLL as specified in Section 6.5.4.12.4 with the selected DLL clock output phase.
4. Send **CMD19** to the SD3.0 card or **CMD21** to eMMC4.5 device.
    > [!NOTE]
    > Do not wait for `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[CMD_RESPONSE_END]` bit and ignore `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[CMD_CRC_FAIL]` bit.
5. Wait until one of the following event bits of `SDCC_MCI_STATUS` register is set:
    a. `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_CRC_FAIL]`
    b. `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_TIMEOUT]`
    c. `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATAEND]`
6. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_CRC_FAIL]` bit or `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATA_TIMEOUT]` bit is set to 1, then the selected DLL clock output phase cannot be used as sampling setting for:
    a. SD3.0 UHS-I card read operation in SDR50 or SDR104 timing mode.
    b. eMMC4.5 device read operation in HS200 timing mode.
    Go to step 9.
7. If `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[DATAEND]` bit is set to `0x1`, then read 64 bytes from `SDCC_MCI_FIFOn` register (n = 0 to 15).
8. Compare the received data with the tuning data pattern as defined in SD3.0 specification (see Table 6-97).

##### Table 6-97 Tuning data pattern for SD3.0 cards and eMMC4.5 devices in 4-bit mode

| Word index | Data pattern |
| :--- | :--- |
| 0 | `0x00FF 0FFF` |
| 1 | `0xCCC3 CCFF` |
| 2 | `0xFFCC 3CC3` |
| 3 | `0xFEEF FFEF` |
| 4 | `0xDDFF FDFF` |
<!-- page 2063 -->
##### Table 6-97 Tuning data pattern for SD3.0 cards and eMMC4.5 devices in 4-bit mode (cont.)

| Word index | Data pattern |
| :--- | :--- |
| 5 | `0xBFFF BFFF` |
| 6 | `0xFFF7 FFFB` |
| 7 | `0xFEDB 7F77` |
| 8 | `0x0FFF 0FFF` |
| 9 | `0xC3CC CFF0` |
| 10 | `0xFCCC 33CC` |
| 11 | `0xEEFF FEFF` |
| 12 | `0xDFFF DFFF` |
| 13 | `0xFFFB FFFD` |
| 14 | `0xFF7F FFBB` |
| 15 | `0xEDB7 F77F` |

9. If there is any mismatch in data comparison, then the selected DLL clock output phase cannot be used as sampling setting for SD3.0 UHS-I card read operation (SDR50 or SDR104 timing mode) or eMMC4.5 device read operation (HS200 timing mode).
10. If the received data matches the tuning pattern as defined in SD3.0 or eMMC4.5 specification, then the selected DLL clock output phase can be used as a candidate for sampling setting for SD3.0 UHS-I card or eMMC4.5 device read operation.
11. Advance the DLL clock output phase by 1.
12. If the selected DLL clock output phase value is less than 16, then go back to step 2.
13. Find out the greatest range of consecutive selected DLL clock output phases that can be used as sampling setting for SD3.0 UHS-I card or eMMC4.5 device read operation.
14. Select the ¾ of the range and configure the DLL as specified in Section 6.5.4.12.4 with the selected DLL clock output phase. The valid window is cyclic, meaning that delays 0 and 15 are next to each other.

#### 6.5.4.12.6 Automatic calibration

The output timing of SD3.0 UHS-I card can change as a result of voltage and temperature variations. The DLL clock output phase must be adjusted from time to time to provide the best sampling setting.

Options:
*   Tuning sequence of SDCDC every period (for example: every 1 second), see Section 6.5.4.12.5.
*   Automatic calibration sequence of SDCDC.

To enable automatic calibration of SDCDC, perform the following steps:
1.  Run tuning sequence one time after the SD3.0 UHS-I card completed voltage switch sequence and switched to UHS-I mode, see Section 6.5.4.12.5.
<!-- page 2064 -->
2.  Set appropriate bit fields and write to `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG` register:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CDR_EN]` bit to `0x1`.
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CDR_EXT_EN]` bit to `0x0`.
    c. Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit to `0x0`.
    d. Preserve read value of all other bits of `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG` register.
3.  Wait until `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit is `0x0`.
4.  Set `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit to `0x1`.
5.  Wait until `SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG[CK_OUT_EN]` bit is `0x1`.
6.  When performing read data sequence set `SDCC_MCI_CMD[AUTO_CMD19]` bit to `0x1` when sending **CMD17** or **CMD18** to the SD3.0 UHS-I card in SDR50 or SDR104 timing mode.
7.  Ensure that `SDCC_MCI_CMD[AUTO_CMD19]` bit is set to `0x0` in all other cases.

### 6.5.4.13 Standard SD host controller mode

To set the SDCC to SD standard host controller (HC) mode set `SDCC_MCI_HC_MODE[HC_MODE_EN]` bit to `0x1`. In this mode only HC mode software procedures apply.

For more information regarding HC software procedures, see *SD Specifications, Part A2, SD Host Controller Standard Specification*.

#### 6.5.4.13.1 SDHCI operational modes

Table 6-98 lists the SDHCI operational modes and how the intended mode to be selected for the SDHCI driver.

##### Table 6-98 SDHCI operation modes

| SDCC_HC_REG_3C_3E<br>[HST_CTL2_UHS_MODE_SEL] | SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC<br>[HC_SELECT_IN] | Operation | Supported modes | SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC<br>[SDC4_MCLK_SEL] |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `0x0`, `0x1`, `0x2` | `0x2` | Feedback clock samples data in rising edge | SDR12, SDR25, SDR50, DS, HS | NA |
| `0x4` | `0x3` | DDR - Feedback clock samples data in both edges | DDR50 | NA |
| `0x3` | `0x4` | DLL is used for generating sampling clock | SDR104, HS200 | `0x2` (Value 2 (default)) |
<!-- page 2065 -->
#### 6.5.4.13.2 SDHCI power interrupt

To modify the bus power state or the pad voltage state, the software must write to the HC address space. For the change to occur in PMIC, the SDCC core generates a special interrupt (`SDCC_PWR_CMD_IRQ`) using a separate IRQ line and special IRQ routine. Following this interrupt, the software must generate appropriate PMIC writes and configure the VREGs.

#### 6.5.4.13.3 SDHCI software power control concept

Software power control registers:
*   `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CTL_REG`
*   `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_STATUS_REG`
*   `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_MASK_REG`
*   `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CLEAR_REG`

The power control functionality can be executed by a software module external to the SDCC driver - SDCC power control software. The `SDCC_PWR_CMD_IRQ` interrupt is triggered whenever the standard SDCC driver issues a command, which requires PMIC access. Such commands are:
1.  Writing to Bus Power Control register (see `SDCC_HC_REG_28_2A`).
2.  Writing to I/O Pad Signaling Level register (see `SDCC_HC_REG_3C_3E`).
3.  SDCC software reset, which requires the bus to turned OFF and the I/O signaling level to be 3.0 V.

The interrupt service routine calls the SDCC power control software, which extracts information from the SDCC core about the required action and executes the necessary PMIC control transactions.

#### 6.5.4.13.4 SDHCI software reset when power is on

The steps to complete clean software reset for all while power is on, is as follows:
1.  Write `0x1` to `SDCC_HC_REG_2C_2E[SW_RST_FOR_ALL]` bit (while SD bus power is on).
2.  Receive power interrupt with `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_STATUS_REG[BUS_OFF]` bit set to `0x1`.
3.  Mask interrupt by writing `0x0` to `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_MASK_REG` register.
4.  Handle power interrupt (lower SD BUS power, TLMM PAD disable).
5.  Clear `BUS_OFF` interrupt by writing `0x1` to `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CLEAR_REG[BUS_OFF]` bit.
6.  Read `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_STATUS_REG[BUS_OFF]` bit again to ensure the bit was cleared. In case the bit is still `0x1`, repeat steps 5 and 6 for five times.
7.  Unmask power interrupt by writing `0xF` to `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_MASK_REG` register.
<!-- page 2066 -->
8.  Acknowledge BUS_OFF by writing `0x1` to `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CTL_REG[BUS_ON_OFF_SUCCESS]` bit for success, or `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_PWRCTL_CTL_REG[BUS_ON_OFF_FAIL]` bit if power-off sequence failed.
9.  Poll on `SDCC_HC_REG_2C_2E[SW_RST_FOR_ALL]` for `0x0`.

#### 6.5.4.13.5 SDHCI internal power features

The following bits are used to gate off the clocks whenever possible to help save power between transactions:
1.  `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC[PWRSAVE]`
    *   This bit is used to gate off the SD clock between transactions.
    *   In functional mode, it should be set to `0x1`.
2.  `SDCC_HC_REG_2C_2E[CLK_CTL_INTERNAL_CLK_EN]`
    *   This bit enables the internal MCLK. When this bit is set to `0x1`, the MCLK does not stop between transactions.
    *   In functional mode this bit should be set to `0x0`.
3.  `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC[HC_HCLKON_SW_EN]`
    *   This bit enables the internal HCLK. When this bit is set to `0x1`, the HCLK will not be gated.
    *   In functional mode, it should be set to `0x0`.
4.  `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC3[PWRSAVE_DLL]`
    *   This bit is used to gate off the DLL input clock between transactions.
    *   In functional mode, it should be set to `0x0`.
5.  `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC3[HCLK_IDLE_GATING]`
    *   This bit further gates HCLK between transactions.
    *   In functional mode, it should be set to `0x1`.
6.  `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC3[MCLK_IDLE_GATING]`
    *   This bit further gates MCLK between transactions.
    *   In functional mode, it should be set to `0x1`.

> [!NOTE]
> These bits do not have much impact on the power consumption of the transaction itself, but ensure that the SDCC will be well gated between transactions. In sleep mode, it is always better to turn off the clock at the GCC level to save more power.
>
> For more information about standard host controller power reduction modes, see *SD Specifications, Part A2, SD Host Controller Standard Specification*.

#### 6.5.4.13.6 SDHCI high priority interrupt

1.  Clearing Transfer Mode register (`SDCC_HC_REG_C_E`).
2.  Perform Software Reset For DAT Line (`SDCC_HC_REG_2C_2E[SW_RST_DAT_LINE]`).
<!-- page 2067 -->
3.  Send **CMD12** with the appropriate fields:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_CMD[CMD_INDEX]` to `0xC` (12).
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_ARGUMENT[CMD_ARG]` to `0x0`.
    c. Set `SDCC_MCI_CMD[MCIABORT]` bit to `0x1`.
    d. The `SDCC_HC_REG_C_E[CMD_TYPE]` bit is `0x3`.
4.  Send **CMD12** or **CMD13** (according to the card HPI command support) with the appropriate fields:
    a. Set `SDCC_MCI_CMD[CMD_INDEX]` to `0xC` (12) or `0xD` (13).
    b. Set `SDCC_MCI_ARGUMENT[CMD_ARG]` to `0x1`.
    c. The `SDCC_HC_REG_C_E[CMD_TYPE]` bit is `0x3`.
5.  Initialize ADMA.
6.  Perform Rx data transaction from the eMMC.

#### 6.5.4.13.7 SDHCI abort sequence

Supported sequence:
*   Perform Software Reset For DAT Line (`SDCC_HC_REG_2C_2E[SW_RST_DAT_LINE]`).
*   Send abort command (**CMD12**).

> [!NOTE]
> For more information, see the *SD Specifications, Part A2, SD Host Controller Standard Specification*.

#### 6.5.4.13.8 SDHCI bus testing procedure

*   This procedure is defined in eMMC specification where the bus is tested for availability of all 8 (SDCC1) / 4 (SDCC2) data lines. The feature involves data traffic in both directions without CRC bits.
*   To enable this feature set `SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_FUNC[MODE]` bit to `0x1`.

### 6.5.5.3 SDCC register definitions

#### 6.5.5.3.1 SDCC_MCI_POWER (Offset: 0x0)

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

(ARM name: MCIPower).

This register must be updated to the MCLK domain so subsequent writes to this register will be ignored until 3 MCLK and 3 HCLK have passed.

Software should wait until the `SDCC_MCI_STATUS2[MCLK_REG_WR_ACTIVE]` bit is 0, after writing to `SDCC_MCI_POWER` register and before accessing this register again.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 11 | DML_SW_RST_WAIT_IDLE_DIS | If this bit is set, then `SDCC_MCI_POWER[SW_RST_REQ]` procedure before `BAM_TRANS_RESET` is not executed automatically. |
| 10 | SW_RST_WAIT_IDLE_DIS | If this bit is set, then `SDCC_MCI_POWER[SW_RST_REQ]` procedure is not executed automatically. |
| 9 | SW_RST_REQ | Before executing `SDCC_MCI_POWER[SW_RST]` or `SDCC_MCI_POWER[SW_RST_CONFIG]`, this bit should be set and software must polls on it until it is being cleared. The bit is cleared after AXI master has finished processing the outstanding transactions and it is in IDLE state. |
| 8 | SW_RST_CONFIG | Software reset bit for the core without resetting configuration registers (`SDCC_MCI_POWER`, `SDCC_MCI_CLK`, `SDCC_MCI_INT_MASKn`). In that case, software resets the internal state machines, data path, and so on, and proceeds to the next transaction without reconfiguring the SDCC registers. |
| 7 | SW_RST | Software reset bit for the core. The impact of this reset bit is similar to the impact of the reset from software register in CLK_CTRL block. All software registers and all internal logic are reset. |
| 6 | OPEN_DRAIN | MCICMD Output Control. This bit is reserved for the use mentioned in the Description but it is not tested. The open drain mode is preserved such that when enabled, the command output is driven low when the logic is low and undriven (so that the pull-up can pull high) when the logic is high. Whether this gets used in the system is up to SW/system but the hardware does support this mode. |
| 0 | CONTROL | This register is used to control the operation of the memory controller.<br>Value 0: power-off<br>Value 1: power-on |
<!-- page 2073 -->

#### 6.5.5.3.2 SDCC_MCI_CLK (Offset: 0x4)

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State:** 0x01008000

(ARM name: MCIClock).

This register must be updated to the MCLK domain so subsequent writes to this register will be ignored until 3 MCLK and 3 HCLK have passed. Software should wait until the `SDCC_MCI_STATUS2[MCLK_REG_WR_ACTIVE]` bit is 0, after writing to `SDCC_MCI_POWER` register and before accessing this register again.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | PWRSAVE_DLL | When this bit is set, DLL gets clock during transactions but not in idle. When this bit is cleared, DLL gets clock all the time so sdc4_dll_lock will not be de-asserted. |
| 30 | SDIO_TRANS | When this bit is set in SDIO transaction, `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[START_BIT_ERR]` status bit will not be raised. The reason is that interrupt period, which is de-asserted only after the Rx command, can cause to wrong `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[START_BIT_ERR]` status bit detection. The `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[START_BIT_ERR]` bit does not appear when `SDCC_MCI_CLK[SDIO_TRANS]` is set. |
| 29 | HCLK_IDLE_GATING | Additional CGC for HCLK was added which gates the HCLK for status bits. If this bit is set, then HCLK is gated for these registers during IDLE. |
| 28 | MCLK_IDLE_GATING | Additional CGC for MCLK was added, which gates the MCLK for status bits. If this bit is set, then MCLK is gated for these registers during IDLE. |
| 27 | INT_MCLK_ON | An internal CGC is located in MCLK domain. Software can enable the internal clock at IDLE time by writing '1' to this bit. If the bit is cleared, then the clock is gated at IDLE time. |
| 26 | SDCC_CLK_EXT_EN | Value 0 (default) - sdcc_clkout is driven via the clock pad and external clock cannot be used for testing the cm_dll_sdc4.<br>Value 1 - External clock can be used as a test clock. |
| 24:23 | SDC4_MCLK_SEL | Selects the sdc4_mclk - input clock of cm_dll_sdc4.<br>Value 1 - feedback clock from CLK pad.<br>Value 2 (default) - free running MCLK (gated between the transactions).<br>Value 3 - free running MCLK divided by 2. |
| 22 | CLK_INV | When set (1), the input clock, which is inserted into the input macros, is inverted. |
| 21 | IO_PAD_PWR_SWITCH | Indication to Pad that power must be switched from 3.3 V to 1.8 V. |
| 20 | CLK_FB_DLY_SEL | Selects the source of feedback clock used by the controller.<br>Value 1 - output of cm_dll_sdc4 is used as feedback clock.<br>Value 0 - feedback clock from CLK pad is used. |
<!-- page 2074 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |

#### 6.5.5.3.4 SDCC_MCI_CMD (Offset: 0xC)

* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State:** 0x00000000

(ARM name: MMCCommand) CPSM: Command Path state machine.

This register must be updated to the MCLK domain so subsequent writes to this register will be ignored until 3 MCLK and 3 HCLK have passed. Software should wait until the `SDCC_MCI_STATUS2[MCLK_REG_WR_ACTIVE]` bit is 0, after writing to `SDCC_MCI_POWER` register and before accessing this register again.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 17 | AUTO_CMD21 | If set (1), CPSM sends CMD21 automatically before sending CMD17 or CMD18. This sequence is needed for CDR autocalibration of cm_dll_sdc4. CMD21 is supported in eMMC4.5 Spec. |
| 16 | AUTO_CMD19 | If set (1), CPSM sends CMD19 automatically before sending CMD17 or CMD18. This sequence is needed for CDR autocalibration of cm_dll_sdc4. CMD19 is supported in SD3.0 Spec. |
| 15 | CCS_DISABLE | If set (1), CPSM sends Command_Completion_Signal (CCS) disable sequence to the external CE-ATA device. |
| 14 | CCS_ENABLE | If set (1), CPSM waits for CCS from external card CE-ATA device. |
| 13 | MCIABORT | Signals the next command will be an abort (stop) command. This bit always read as (0) due to the hardware implementation. See a related note in next field. |
| 12 | DAT_CMD | If set (1) indicates that this is a Command with Data. Note - `SDCC_MCI_CMD[MCIABORT]` and `SDCC_MCI_CMD[DAT_CMD]` bits, bits do not have any effect on the CPSM. They are used to signal the SDIO Interrupt state machine that a Multi-Block (examples: CMD18, CMD25, CMD53, and so on. The rule is that each command with data must set this bit) data transaction is taking place. The DAT_CMD bit signals the start of the data transaction while the MCIABORT bit signals the end. For a pure SD Memory card, these bits are a “don’t care” and should be set to zero by convention. However, some software drivers may chose to manipulate the bits in order to maintain compatibility with Combo cards and/or pure SDIO cards. |
| 11 | PROG_ENA | If set (1), `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[PROG_DONE]` status bit will be asserted when busy is de-asserted. This bit is to be used with a stop or status command after a block write is performed. Does not effect CPSM. |
| 10 | ENABLE | The action of writing to this register (MCI_CMD) with this bit set (1), triggers CPSM to leave the Idle State. |
| 9 | PENDING | If set (1), CPSM waits for 'CmdPend' from the DPSM before it starts sending a command. This bit is designed to be used with SD CMD18 (READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) and SD CMD25 (WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK) which must be terminated with an SD CMD12 (STOP_TRANSMISSION).<br>After CMD18 or CMD25 is sent, the DPSM is enabled to send or receive data of amount `SDCC_MCI_DATA_LENGTH`. After the DPSM finishes the transferring the data, it sends “CmdPend” to the CPSM and goes idle. When the CPSM receives this signal, it sends the currently loaded command which software would normally establish as CMD12. |
<!-- page 2076 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8 | INTERRUPT | If set (1), CPSM disables command timer and waits for interrupt request (Card Response). The START, CMD_INDEX, ARGUMENT, and CRC are a total of 48 bits in length. If the `SDCC_MCI_CMD[INTERRUPT]` bit is zero, the CPSM waits (63-47) 16 MCLK ticks for a response before going back to IDLE. If the `SDCC_MCI_CMD[INTERRUPT]` bit is set, the CPSM waits indefinitely for a card response. |
| 7 | LONGRSP | If set (1), receives a 136-bit long response. |
| 6 | RESPONSE | If set (1), CPSM waits for a response subject to the `SDCC_MCI_CMD[INTERRUPT]` bit above. |
| 5:0 | CMD_INDEX | Command index. |

#### 6.5.5.3.11 SDCC_MCI_STATUS (Offset: 0x34)

* **Type:** R
* **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State:** 0x000C0000

(ARM name: MCIStatus)

This register may need exclusion for QCSR POR Test for bits 25 and 22. Static[30:26], [24:23] and [10:0].

These remain asserted until they are cleared by writing to the appropriate bit in the Clear Register (see `SDCC_MCI_CLEAR` register).

* **XCIS**
  The means used to send the SDIO external-card-interrupt-signal (XCIS) to the SDCC depends on the transfer mode: 1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit. Under 1-bit transfer mode, the XCIS has a dedicated physical connection to the SDCC. Hence once it is asserted, it remains at a high level. Under 4 and 8-bit transfer modes, the XCIS is time multiplexed with physical connection data bit 1. The XCIS is recognized as valid during specific time slots on data bit 1 by the SDCC. How this 'recognition' takes places shows up as different behaviors on `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[SDIO_INTR_OPER]`, `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[SDIO_INTR]` bits, and the actual interrupt sent to the ARM through `SDCC_MCI_INT_MASKn` register.
* **Special[25]**
  The `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[SDIO_INTR_OPER]` indicator reflects the true state of XCIS as it would be observed inside the external SDIO card. As such, there is no bit 25 in `SDCC_MCI_CLEAR` register. The only way to clear `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[SDIO_INTR_OPER]` bit is to clear the appropriate bit in the external card Common Card Control Registers (CCCR). Like 'static' above and 'dynamic' below, bit 25 in `SDCC_MCI_INT_MASKn` register controls actually sending this indicator value to the ARM. This indicator of XCIS is used for normal SDCC operation.
<!-- page 2080 -->

* **Special[22]**
  The `SDCC_MCI_STATUS[SDIO_INTR]` indicator reflects that there has been a low-to-high transition on the connection as explained under XCIS above. This indicator is cleared via bit 22 of `SDCC_MCI_CLEAR` register but any low-to-high transition on the connection sets this indicator again. Further note that this indicator is not routed through the `SDCC_MCI_INT_MASKn` register to the ARM. For bit 22, the raw value of the connection is routed through the `SDCC_MCI_INT_MASKn` register to the ARM. As this raw connection is not aware of specific time slots, the signal sent to the ARM generally toggles in an unpredictable fashion. This is not useful during normal SDCC operation. However, for wake-up with clocks off, the raw connection is desirable.
* **Dynamic[21:11]**
  These change states depending on the state of the underlying logic (for example, FIFO full and empty flags are asserted and de-asserted as data while written to the FIFO).

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | STATUS2_INT | One of the error bits in `SDCC_MCI_STATUS2[4:1]` register is set. |
| 30 | AUTO_CMD19_TIMEOUT | Response or tuning pattern was not received after automatic CMD19's transmission. This status bit should be read only if `SDCC_MCI_CMD[AUTO_CMD19]` bit was set. |
| 29 | BOOT_TIMEOUT | Data was not received within the valid time (according to `SDCC_MCI_CCS_TIMER` register) from the start of boot operation. |
| 28 | BOOT_ACK_ERR | Acknowledge pattern was not received correctly or not within the valid time (according to MCI_ACK_TIME) from the start of boot operation. |
| 27 | BOOT_ACK_REC | Acknowledge pattern was received correctly. |
| 26 | CCS_TIMEOUT | CE-ATA Command Completion Signal timeout. |
| 25 | SDIO_INTR_OPER | SDIO interrupt indicator for normal operation. |
| 24 | ATA_CMD_COMPL | CE-ATA Command Completion Signal has been detected. |
| 23 | PROG_DONE | Programming done. |
| 22 | SDIO_INTR | SDIO interrupt indicator for wake-up. |
| 21 | RXDATA_AVLBL | Data available in receive FIFO. At least 1 word in the Rx FIFO. Software can read 1 word only from the FIFO. |

### 6.5.5.3.14 0x44 SDCC_MCI_FIFO_COUNT

* **Type**: R
* **Clock**: `GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK`, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

The SDCC core operates in two clock domains: `MCLK` and `HCLK`. The CPSM and DPSM operate in `MCLK` domain and `MciFifoDmaCtl` (FIFO/DMA Controller) operates in `HCLK` domain. The `SDCC_MCI_FIFO_COUNT` is a counter of the FIFO Controller that monitors how many words of data must be transferred through the FIFO. At the beginning of a data transaction, the `SDCC_MCI_FIFO_COUNT` counter will be loaded with the `(SDCC_MCI_DATA_LENGTH / 4)` value and then count down during the data transaction until it reaches zero. This register is only useful for debug purposes and should not be used for normal operation since it does not reflect data, which may or may not be in the pipeline.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:0 | DATA_COUNT | Remaining data. |

### 6.5.5.3.17 0x54 SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: `GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK`, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

The register is responsible for handling DCM, which is used in emulation, supports 256 values of shift intervals so 8 bits are required (0:255). Bits [31:30] are used for emulation purposes only.

The procedure for activating the DCM is:
1. Setting `SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE[DCM_RESET]` bit.
2. Clearing `SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE[DCM_RESET]` bit.
3. Waiting until `SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE[DCM_LOCKED]` bit is high.
4. Writing a new phase in `SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE[SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL]` bit field and setting the `SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE[DCM_START]` bit. The clock's placement was executed by the DCM when `SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE[DCM_DONE]` bit is asserted.
<!-- page 2085 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | DCM_DONE | The shift process was finished in DCM and CMD19 can be sent towards the card. This is a read-only bit. |
| 30 | DCM_START | A new value of `SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE[SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL]` bit is ready. Clears the `SDCC_MCI_EMULATION_DLY_LINE[DCM_DONE]` bit. |
| 29 | DCM_LOCKED | Reading the status of the LOCKED DCM's output, which indicates that the output clock is ready for use. |
| 28 | DCM_RESET | Driving reset to DCM. |
| 7:0 | SD_CLK_DLY_CTRL | Input to DCM block in FPGA (8 bits). Controlling the change of the delay interval. The value's range may be 0-255 in DCM block. |

### 6.5.5.3.18 0x58 SDCC_MCI_CCS_TIMER

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: `GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK`, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

This register is used for operation with CE-ATA devices. The CCS timer starts to count at the end of the SD transaction and it advances with every MCLK clock cycle. In boot operation this register is used for storing the number of cycles from initiating the boot operation until the first data is received.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | CCS_TIMER | CE-ATA Command Completion Signal timeout period. |

### 6.5.5.3.19 0x5C SDCC_MCI_RESPONSE_MASK

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: `GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK`, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State**: `0x00000000`

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | RESPONSE_MASK | Mask used to verify the 32-status error bits. Active only when the data pending bit is set in the `SDCC_MCI_DATA_CTL` register. When a bit of this mask is set, the corresponding bit from response [39:8] is checked to be 0 (i.e. shows there is no error). If all bits from mask show no error, the DPSM will be activated without waiting for software write. |

### 6.5.5.3.20 0x60 SDCC_MCI_DLL_CONFIG

* **Type**: RW
* **Clock**: `GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK`, x = 1 or 2
<!-- page 2086 -->

| 16 | BUSY_CHECK_VALID_ALWAYS | In DDR200 mode, the end of busy should be checked after the CRC token was received. There is a counter of 4 cycles for this purpose. If this bit is set, then the end of busy will be checked right after the CRC token. |
| 15 | BAM_ERR_EN | Enabling the assertion of SDCC_MCI_STATUS2[BAM_AXI_MASTER_ERR] field. |

| 13 | FF_CLK_SW_RST_DIS | Disabling the software reset in FF clock domain. |

| 10 | ADMA_INT_DATA | If this bit is set, then the ADMA interrupt is set when the data was already transferred. If this bit is cleared, then the ADMA interrupt is set when the requests related to the descriptors were finished on address channel before the data is processed. |

| 8 | ADMA_HPROT_DIS | If cleared then HPROT is changed in last burst of write transaction if block_count_en is 1, otherwise it is for each end of descriptor. |
| 7 | ADMA_NON_WRD_ALIGN_DIS | If set, the fix for nonword aligned transfers in ADMA is disabled. |
| 6 | DEASSERT_HREADY_DAT_DIS | If set, then hready cannot be deasserted for access to Transfer Mode register in HC address. By default, the hready is de-asserted for enabling the completion of synchronization period to MCLK before the next access. |
| 5 | DEASSERT_HREADY_CMD_DIS | If set, then hready cannot be deasserted for access to Command register in HC address. By default, the hready is de-asserted for enabling the completion of synchronization period to MCLK before the next access. |

| 1 | CYCLES_AFTER_EOB_DIS | Enable bit for the fix that TxFlowControl is not set until end of the block (CRC token reception) in the middle of Tx transaction. The fix is required for releasing each BAM's descriptor separately without waiting to the next descriptor. |

### 6.5.5.3.26 0x80+0x4*n SDCC_MCI_FIFOn, n=[0..15]

- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DATA | FIFO data. This register is aliased to 16 words, 0x080 - 0xBC. In SDCC3, access to the FIFO was executed with 16 words so 16 addresses were defined. However, in SDCC only 8 words are used in each burst so only 8 addresses from the range should be used.<br>When writing to the external SD_Card, writes to the data path FIFO.<br>When reading from the external SD_Card, reads from the data path FIFO. |

### 6.5.5.3.27 0xDC SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_STATUS_REG

- **Type:** R
- **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

HC Spec Defines power and I/O voltage switch bits. A dedicated interrupt sends information to the QCT software driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC. The different tasks are defined in this register.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 3 | IO_HIGH_V | SDCC driver orders that the I/O signaling level is switched to 3.0 V. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 03Eh in HC register (bit 3) or when software reset for all is handled and last supported voltage was 1.8 V. This logic is enabled when SDCC_MCI_GENERICS[SWITCHABLE_SIGNALING_VOLTAGE] = true. |
| 2 | IO_LOW_V | SDCC driver orders that the I/O signaling levels be switched to 1.8 V. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '1' to offset 03Eh in HC register (bit 3). This logic is enabled when SDCC_MCI_GENERICS[SWITCHABLE_SIGNALING_VOLTAGE] = true. |
| 1 | BUS_ON | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power is switched on. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '1' to offset 029h in HC register (bit 0). |
| 0 | BUS_OFF | SDCC driver orders that the SD bus power is switched off. This interrupt is triggered when SDCC driver writes '0' to offset 029h in HC register (bit 0) or when software reset for all is handled. |
<!-- page 2093 -->

### 6.5.5.3.30 0xE8 SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG

- **Type:** RW
- **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
- **Reset State:** 0x00000000

HC Spec Defines power and I/O voltage switch bits. A dedicated interrupt sends information to the QCT software driver for handling the power and voltage tasks with PMIC and then the QCT software driver must report success or fail to this register.
<!-- page 2094 -->

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 9 | HC_CARD_STATE_STABLE | This bit is driving CARD_STATE_STABLE bit in Present State Register. |
| 8 | RST_NOT_WAIT_PWRCTL_REG | RST process does not need to wait for accessing to SDCC_MCI_PWRCTL_CTL_REG register. |
| 7:6 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT_PAD | Value 0 inversion of HC_WRITE_PROTECT is connected to bit 19 in Present State Register.<br>Value 1 input from PAD is used.<br>Value 2 inversion of input from PAD is used. |
| 5 | CARD_DETECT_PIN_LEVEL | This bit reflects the inverse value of the SDCD# pad. Debouncing is not performed on this bit. This bit may be valid when Card State Stable is set to 1, but it is not guaranteed because of propagation delay. Use of this bit is limited to testing since it must be debounced by software.<br>value1: card present.<br>Value 0: no card present. |
| 4 | HC_WRITE_PROTECT | This bit allows to disable the writing. Value 0: write enabled.<br>Value 1: write protected. |
| 3 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate that the signal switch has failed. |
| 2 | IO_SIG_SWITCH_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either I/O Low V interrupt or I/O High V interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate that the signal switch has completed successfully. |
| 1 | BUS_ON_OFF_FAIL | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate that the requested operation has failed. |
| 0 | BUS_ON_OFF_SUCCESS | Host controller clears this bit when it fires either Bus ON interrupt or Bus OFF interrupt. SDCC power control software writes '1' to indicate that the requested operation has completed successfully. |

| Bits | Name | Description |

This register is programmed by multiplying the constant with 1024 and rounding to the nearest integer. For example: if Cchar = 0.67, RO (0.67 * 1024) = 686, hence program TMUX_CHAR = 11'h2AE. |

| 0 | DDR_CAL_EN | The signal is set after the configuration of SDCC_MCI_DDR_CONFIG is finished. When the signal is low, the TCXO domain is being reset. |

### 6.5.5.3.66 SDCC_MCI_DDR_CONFIG
* **Offset:** `0x1B0`
* **Type:** RW
* **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State:** `0x80040853`

Configuration of ddr_config input of DLL

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31 | PRG_DLY_EN | Enables Programmable delay for RCLK_IN. |
| 30 | EXT_PRG_RCLK_DLY_EN | Enables external control of Programmable RCLK delayline. |
| 29:27 | EXT_PRG_RCLK_DLY_CODE | Used only if `SDCC_MCI_DDR_CONFIG[EXT_PRG_RCLK_DLY_EN]` is set. Configuring programmable RCLK delayline process code number. |
| 26:21 | EXT_PRG_RCLK_DLY | Used only if `SDCC_HC_REG_DDR_CONFIG[EXT_PRG_RCLK_DLY_EN]` is set. Programmable RCLK Delay line fine delay control. |
| 20:12 | TCXO_CYCLES_DLY_LINE | Number of TCXO clock cycles between finish of one delay line calibration and beginning of next delay line calibration. |
| 11:9 | TCXO_CYCLES_CNT | Number of TCXO clock cycles for which down counter is enabled for before making each inc/dec decision. |
| 8:0 | PRG_RCLK_DLY | These bits are controlled the programmable delay line. This bus is binary coded. Decimal value = (TCXO period * Decimal value of `SDCC_MCI_DDR_CONFIG[TCXO_CYCLES_CNT]`) / (2*delay needed). For 1.25 ns the formula is (52n*4/2*1.25) = 83 in decimal. |

### 6.5.5.3.67 SDCC_MCI_FIFO_ALTn, n=[0..255]
* **Offset:** `0x400 + 0x4*n`
* **Type:** RW
<!-- page 2113 -->

* **Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2
* **Reset State:** `0x00000000`

Alternative register to `SDCC_MCI_FIFO` (0x80 - 0xBC). The software can use this register range (0x400 - 0x7FC) for accessing all the RAM range (1024 bytes) in FIFO mode. The advantage is that any byte in the RAM can be accessed without repeating the same address.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 31:0 | DATA | WORD is written or received to/from the RAM in FIFO mode. |

| 28 | CK_INTP_SEL | Selects interpolator output |
| 27 | CK_INTP_EN | Enable clock interpolation for finer resolution |
| 26:24 | MCLK_FREQ | Frequency of MCLK <br>Value 000 - 100 - 112 (MHz) <br>Value 001 - 112 - 125 <br>Value 010 - 125 - 137 <br>Value 011 - 137 - 150 <br>Value 100 - 150 - 162 <br>Value 101 - 162 - 175 <br>Value 110 - 175 - 187 <br>Value 111 - 187 - 200 |
<!-- page 2133 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 23:20 | CDR_SELEXT | CDR phase select (gray coded) <br>Value 0000 - phase 0 <br>Value 0001 - phase 1 <br>Value 0011 - phase 2 <br>Value 0010 - phase 3 <br>Value 0110 - phase 4 <br>Value 0111 - phase 5 <br>Value 0101 - phase 6 <br>Value 0100 - phase 7 <br>Value 1100 - phase 8 <br>Value 1101 - phase 9 <br>Value 1111 - phase 10 <br>Value 1110 - phase 11 <br>Value 1010 - phase 12 <br>Value 1011 - phase 13 <br>Value 1001 - phase 14 <br>Value 1000 - phase 15 |
| 19 | CDR_EXT_EN | Enable external control of cdr phase select |
| 18 | CK_OUT_EN | Enable output clock (default value is '1') |
| 17 | CDR_EN | Enable CDR function |
| 16 | DLL_EN | Enable DLL function |
| 15:14 | CDR_UPD_RATE | CDR update rate, low pass filtering window of CDR Max update rate: <br>Value 00 - 0.5 MCLK frequency <br>Value 01 - 0.25 MCLK Frequency (default) <br>Value 10 - 0.125 MCLK frequency <br>Value 11 - 1/16 MCLK Frequency |
| 13:12 | DLL_UPD_RATE | DLL update rate <br>Value 00 - sdc4_mclk/10 <br>Value 01 - sdc4_mclk/20 <br>Value 10 - sdc4_mclk/40 (default) <br>Value 11 - sdc4_mclk/80 |
| 11:10 | DLL_PHASE_DET | DLL phase detector low pass average window <br>Value 00 - 2 cycles <br>Value 01 - 4 cycles (default) <br>Value 10 - 8 cycles <br>Value 11 - 16 cycles |
| 9 | CDR_ALGORITHM_SEL | CDR algorithm select <br>Value 0 - Edge (default) <br>Value 1 - Level |

- **Type**: RW

| Bits | Name | Description |

| 18 | HC_SELECT_IN_EN | Enabling the selection of mode via the vendor-specific register. |

### 6.5.5.3.107 0xA30 SDCC_HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_CSR_CDC_CTLR_CFG0

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_SDCCx_AHB_CLK, x = 1 or 2

The HC_VENDOR_SPECIFIC_CSR_CDC_CTLR_CFG0 register configures the following:

| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 25 | STAGGER_CAL_ENA | 1'b1: Stagger calibration of write and read CDCs once after the other to reduce peak voltage drop.<br>1'b0: Both write and read CDCs calibrated simultaneously.<br>This bit is introduced on the x2 core, so not present on x0 and x1 versions of DIM/PHY. |

| 23:20 | OSC_COUNT_ERR_TOLERANCE | Magnitude of the difference between oscillator count and target count when the algorithm assumes convergence and stops further search. |
| 19 | TRACK_CALIB_MODE | 1'b0: Tracking calibration uses previous Target_count value.<br>1'b1 Accurate mode: Target_count is recomputed at the start of tracking calibration. |
<!-- page 2142 -->
| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 18 | FULL_DELAY | 1'b0: unitstep and subunit caps are from calibration or software settings.<br>1'b1: All unit step and subunit caps are selected for the delay arrays. |
| 17 | HW_AUTOCAL_ENA | 1'b1: Enables periodic auto calibration<br>1'b0: Periodic calibration is disabled |
| 16 | SW_TRIG_FULL_CALIB | A low to high transition on this register bit triggers the CDC calibration state machine to initiate full calibration of the standby delay array. Also resets tracking mode for the delay arrays. |
| 13:12 | OSC_PRE_DIV | The factor by which the raw oscillator frequency is divided before being given to the counting logic.<br>2'b00 Divide by 1<br>2'b01 Divide by 2<br>2'b10 Divide by 4<br>2'b11 Divide by 8 |
| 10:0 | TMUX_CHAR | Cchar is a characterized constant equal to the ratio of output mux offset delay to average unit step delay. This register is programmed by multiplying the constant with 1024 and rounding to the nearest integer. Example: if Cchar = 0.67, RO(0.67 × 1024) = 686, hence program TMUX_CHAR = 11'h2AE. |

## 6.6 Peripheral Web Core (PWC)

This section describes the PWC. Integrated in the device PWC is a general service unit that provides two different services:

* Three output signals with pulse-density-modulation.
* Generates one general-purpose clock (GP_MN).

### 6.6.1 PWC overview

There are three PDM modules integrated within the PWC. Each of the PDM modules has the following specific features:

* PDM0 module uses one CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK0 clock and it has 16-bit resolution
* PDM1 module uses one CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK1 clock and it has 8-bit resolution
* PDM2 module uses one CC_PDM2_CLK clock and it has 16-bit resolution

PWC has integrated one GP_MN clock divider and it provides one general-purpose clock (GP_MN).

Figure 6-84 shows a high-level overview of the PDM instances integrated within the peripheral web core in the SoC.
<!-- page 2159 -->
#### Figure 6-84 PDM overview

*Description:*
The diagram shows the Peripheral Web Core (PWC) and its connections:
*   The PWC contains three PDM modules (**PDM0**, **PDM1**, **PDM2**) and a **GP_MN clock divider**.
*   **PDM0** has two outputs: `GP PDM output 0A` and `GP PDM output 0B`. It also shows a connection to `WEB_TCXO4`.
*   **PDM1** has two outputs: `GP PDM output 1A` and `GP PDM output 1B`.
*   **PDM2** has two outputs: `GP PDM output 2A` and `GP PDM output 2B`.
*   The **GP_MN clock divider** has one output: `GP M_N clock divider output`.
*   **GCC** (Global Clock Controller) provides `Clocks` and `Resets` to the PWC.
*   The PWC interfaces with the `Peripheral and system configuration NoC` via a `PDM_AHB_BRIDGE`.

### 6.6.1.1 PWC acronyms and terms

| Acronym or term | Definition |

| PDM | Pulse Density Modulation |
| TLMM | Top-Level Mode Mux |
<!-- page 2160 -->
### 6.6.1.2 PWC features and key use cases

The peripheral web core operates under a number of specific use cases:

* **PDM use case 1: example 1**: The PDM module used for generating density modulated signals that, after passing through a filter, become analog signals. It can produce fixed densities or alternate between densities to create variations in the analog signal.
* **GP_MN clock divider use case**: The GP_MN clock divider used to produce output clock with frequency and duty-cycle controls through the corresponding control registers.

#### 6.6.1.2.1 PDM use case 1: example 1

PDM generates a fixed density signal, which is a mechanism that will generate a fixed analog value signal after filtering.

#### Figure 6-85: Fixed density signal
*Description:* Representation of a fixed density signal bitstream: `0001000011111111`.

#### 6.6.1.2.2 PDM use case 1: example 2

PDM generates an alternating density signal, which is a mechanism that will result in a change of the analog value after filtering the signal.

#### Figure 6-86: Alternating density signal
*Description:* Representation of alternating density signal bitstreams: `0101000011111111` and `1010000011111111`.

#### 6.6.1.2.3 GP_MN clock divider use case

GP_MN generates an accurate clock based on a native clock (`CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK`). The GP_MN clock divider multiplies the native clock by M, divides it by N, and makes the output duty-cycle equal to D.

#### Figure 6-87: GP_MN clock divider output
*Description:* Diagram showing the parameters for the GP_MN clock divider:
*   Input native clock: `CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK`
*   GP_MN (M value): `1FF`
*   GP_MN (N value): `0FF`
*   GP_MN (D value): `01FF`
*   Output clock: `GP_MN`

### 6.6.4 PWC functional description

The peripheral web core contains two main blocks:
- **WEB_TCXO4** – Contains three PDM submodules, one GP_MN clock divider, and configuration registers for configuring the PDM modules and the GP_MN clock divider.
- **PDM_AHB_BRIDGE** – Bridge between the AHB bus and the configuration registers of the core.

Configuring the submodules is done by accessing the respective configuration registers. The PDM modules and GP_MN clock divider operate based on individual clocks. This is done because the `CC_PDM_AHB_CLK` scales for power reasons while the other submodules need stable clocks for proper operation.

`PDM[0-1]` and the GP_MN clock divider work with the `CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK` clock, which is a relatively slow clock (~5 MHz). But, it does not scale down. For the `PDM2`, a faster clock is required. So, a dedicated `CC_PDM2_CLK` is provided, which runs on ~70 MHz.

#### 6.6.4.1 PWC power and clock management

The peripheral web core has simple power management that is based on scaling down the `CC_PDM_AHB_CLK` clock or turning it off to reduce dynamic power.

In addition to the `CC_PDM_AHB_CLK` scaling, the functional clocks to the peripheral web core submodules can also be gated. When the functional clocks (`CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK[0-1]` and `CC_PDM2_CLK`) are disabled, then the `PDM[0-2]` modules and the GP_MN clock divider stop functioning.

Each of the PDM modules (`PDM[0-2]`) supports internal clock gating that is enabled by default and must be disabled by setting to `0x1` the following bits:
- `PDM0_TOP_CTL[TCXO4_CLK_DISABLE]` – this bit is used to disable `CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK[0]` clock for PDM0 module
- `PDM1_TOP_CTL[TCXO4_CLK_DISABLE1]` – this bit is used to disable `CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK[1]` clock for PDM1 module
- `PDM2_TOP_CTL[PDM2_CLK_DISABLE]` – this bit is used to disable `CC_PDM2_CLK` clock for PDM2 module

#### 6.6.4.2 PWC clocks functional description

The SnapdragonTM 410E device has one general-purpose clock divider output (GP_MN), as well as several general-purpose pulse density modulated (PDM) outputs:
- **GP_PDM** – A configurable pulse-density modulated output (12-bit value configurable through), with the base frequency set at 4.8 MHz.
  - The device supports three different instances of this configurable PDM output (`GP_PDM[0-2]`)
  - Each of the `GP_PDM[0-2]` outputs can be used independently
<!-- page 2165 -->

- **GP_MN** – A general-purpose clock divider output that lets the user configure an intended clock output by first selecting a clock source (always 4.8 MHz) and then programming an intended division ratio (M/N) and a duty cycle value (D).

#### 6.6.4.3 PDM (N-bits)

The operation of the PDM modules is based on the `PDM_VALUE`, which is calculated by setting the following fields:
- `PDM0_CTL[PDM0_DAT]`
- `PDM1_CTL[PDM1_DAT]`
- `PDM2_CTL[PDM2_DAT]`

The `PDM_VALUE` can be calculated using the following formula:
$$PDM\_VALUE = \{ \sim PDM\_DATA[N-1], PDM\_DATA[N-2:0] \}$$
*(Note: Corrected from the raw text formula `PDM_VALUE = {PDM_DATA[N-1], PDM_DATA[N-2]}` to match the examples below)*

Where $N=16$ for PDM0 and PDM2 modules, and $N=8$ for PDM1 module.

For example, if `PDM_DATA` is `0x8000`, the actual `PDM_VALUE` is `0x0`; if `PDM_DATA` is `0x0001`, the actual `PDM_VALUE` is `0x8001`.

The functionality of the PDM module is to ensure that PDM output is 1 or 0, depending on the polarity through bit `PDMn_TOP_CTL[PDMn_POLARITY]` (where $n = 0$ to $2$) and `PDM_VALUE` cycles of PDM clock, each $2^N$ PDM clock cycles.

A feedback register holds the current count of the PDM, and each cycle `PDM_VALUE` is added to the count. When the count overflows, the MSB of the sum is XORed with the `PDMn_POLARITY` value to generate the PDM output.

Once overflowed, the PDM counter MSB is cleared to `0x0`.

Figure 6-90 shows an example of how the `PDM_OUT` is generated.
<!-- page 2166 -->

#### Figure 6-90: PDM counter steps
*Description:* A simplified representation of the PDM accumulation process. It shows `PDM_VALUE` being added repeatedly (+PDM_VALUE). The output (indicated by 1s and 0s) is determined by the MSB of the accumulator. The accumulation happens over a period of $2^N$ cycles.

The PDM output is not cycle accurate, such that it is unknown on a cycle basis when the 1s and 0s occur. Only the total number of 1s and 0s in every $2^N$ clock cycles can be ensured, because the state of the saved feedback data from previous configurations cannot be ensured.

#### 6.6.4.4 GP_MN clock divider

The GP_MN clock divider is configured using the following bit fields:
- `GP_MN_CLK_MDIV[GP_M_VALUE]`
- `GP_MN_CLK_NDIV[GP_N_VALUE]`
- `GP_MN_CLK_DUTY[GP_D_VALUE]`

The GP_MN clock divider receives an input clock (`CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK[2]` clock) with a frequency $f_0$ and produces an output clock with:
$$\text{frequency} = f_0 \times \frac{M}{N}$$
and duty cycle controlled by the value of $D$.

For each $N$ clock cycles, the GP_MN produces $M$ clock cycles.
The value of $D$ indicates the number of native clock cycles in which the GP_MN out is 0 in $2^{13}$ (text says "213") native clock cycles.

Summary of operation and configuration:
- `GP_MN_CLK_MDIV` register holds the $M$ value.
- `GP_MN_CLK_NDIV` register holds the one’s complement of the $N-M$ value.
- `GP_MN_CLK_DUTY` register holds the $D$ value.

The variables $M$, $N$, and $D$ have the following specifications and constraints:
- The maximum value of $M$ is 511.
<!-- page 2167 -->

- The maximum value of $N$ is 8191.
- The value of $M$ cannot exceed the value of $N$ (specifically, $N > 2M$).
- $N$ and $M$ cannot have any common divider other than 1 (they must be coprime).
- $D$ is allowed to be between $M$ and $N-M$ ($M < D < N-M$).

#### 6.6.4.5 PWC reset

The peripheral web core is operating with asynchronous reset logic.

Asserting a reset signal results in setting all outputs to zero.

#### 6.6.4.6 PWC theory of operation
- The functional blocks of the peripheral web core are `PDM[0-2]` and `GP_MN` clock divider.

- **Type:** RW

The `GP_MN_CLK_MDIV` register is the MDIV specification register for the GP_MN clock.


<!-- page 2171 -->

For all GP_MN registers, this clock is generated by dividing the frequency of the CC_PDM_TCXO4_CLK clock by an M/N counter. M, N, and D values have the following specifications and constraints:
* The maximum value of M is 511
* The maximum value of N is 8191
* N > 2M
* The value of M cannot exceed the value of N
* N and M cannot have any common divider else than 1
* D is allowed to be between M and N-M: (M < D < N-M)

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 8:0 | GP_M_VALUE | This register defines the value of M for the M/N counter, which generates the GP_MN clock. |

### 6.6.5.3.8 0x0000 0004 GP_MN_CLK_NDIV

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_PDM_AHB_CLK

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The GP_MN_CLK_NDIV register is the NDIV specification register for the GP_MN clock.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:0 | GP_N_VALUE | This register defines the value (-(N-M)), using 1'Bits complement value of N minus M for the M/N counter, which generates the GP_MN clock. |

### 6.6.5.3.9 0x0000 0008 GP_MN_CLK_DUTY

**Type:** RW

**Clock:** GCC_PDM_AHB_CLK

**Reset State:** 0x00000000

The GP_MN_CLK_DUTY register is the duty cycle specification register for the GP_MN clock.

| Bits | Name | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 12:0 | GP_D_VALUE | This register defines the value of D, which determines the duty cycle of the GP_MN clock. The value of D determines the number of low(0) cycles in an N-cycles interval. The useful value of D must be in the range of M to N minus M (M < D < N-M). |

# 7 Memory Support

## 7.1 External bus interface (EBI)

This section describes the external bus interface (EBI).

### 7.1.1 EBI overview

The EBI comprises Bus Integrated Memory Controller (BIMC), DDR PHYs (DDRPHYs) and AHB2PHY module. The EBI supports the following:
* Single channel 32-bit SDRAM interface
* LPDDR2 and LPDDR3
* Two chip selects
* Up to 2 GB for both chip selects (maximum total density supported is 2 GB)
* Single AHB2PHY interface
* Single CA DDRPHY
* Four DQ DDRPHYs
* Frequencies:
  * 200 MHz – SVS mode
  * 400 MHz – mission mode
  * 533 MHz – turbo mode
<!-- page 2173 -->

Figure 7-1 shows the EBI overview.

#### Figure: EBI overview
*Description:* The block diagram shows the External Bus Interface (EBI) architecture within the Snapdragon 410E SoC, illustrating how internal components interface with external SDRAM. The EBI block contains the Bus Integrated Memory Controller (BIMC), CA DDRPHY, DQ DDRPHYs, and AHB2PHY. The BIMC acts as the central hub, receiving requests from various masters (APSS, GPU, QDSP6, SMMU) and interconnects (SNOC, PCNOC). The APSS has a bidirectional connection and receives interrupts (IRQ) from the EBI. GCC provides clocks and resets to the BIMC, and also distributes clocks to the CA DDRPHY, DQ DDRPHYs, and AHB2PHY. The BIMC communicates with the external SDRAM through the CA DDRPHY (Command/Address physical layer) and DQ DDRPHYs (Data physical layer) which interface through chip pads. The AHB2PHY block interfaces with PCNOC and has bidirectional links with DQ DDRPHYs.
